Importing Benefit Enrollments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Common%20to%20BA_BE/Importing-Benefit-Import-Definition.htm Path: BA/Common to BA_BE/Importing-Benefit-Import-Definition.htm

Importing Benefit Enrollments

Use the Benefit Import process to enroll employees in group benefit plans using the information in an external data file. The process requires you to set up a data file and a benefit import definition. You can set up the data file either before you begin the import or from within the Benefits Import form.

You must set up company benefits and benefit rules before using this process. See “Benefit Groups” and “Benefit Rules” in the Benefits Administration User Guide for more information.

To set up the data file:

  1. Create an Excel spreadsheet that includes at least the following columns of information in the same order as in the template. The data file must be either tab-delimited or comma-delimited.

  • Action Code

  • Company ID

  • Employee ID, Employee SSN, or Employee Clock Number

  • Benefit Plan ID

  • Benefit Plan Type

  • Effective Date

  1. Save the spreadsheet in either CVS or TXT format.

To set up the import definition:

XLS Field Name Field # Type Length Req? Description
A ACTION 1 A 6 R Enter the action code for this import (Add, Change, or Term only).
B COMPANY 2 A 7 R A valid Company ID
C EMPLOYEE_ID 3 A 6 R A valid Employee ID
D OFFER_TYPE 4 A 3 R A valid Offer Type.
E EFFECTIVE_DATE 5 D 10 R MM-DD-YYYY format
F PLAN_ID 6 A 10 R A valid Benefit Plan ID
G PLAN_TYPE 7 A 2 R A valid Plan Type.
H DEDN_START 8 N 10 O Deduction Start Date, MM-DD-YYYY format
I DEDN_ENDS 9 D 10 O Deduction End Date, MM-DD-YYYY format
J SECTION_125 10 D 1 O Indicate Section 125 Y/N?
K NETWORK 11 A 10 R Network ID, if network plans are included
L DOCTOR_ID 12 A 1O O Employee’s Primary Care Physician ID
M DOCTOR_NAME 13 A 20 O Name of employee’s Primary Care Physician
N EE_COVERAGE 14 N 10 O Employee Coverage Amount
O SPS_COVERAGE 15 N 10 O Spouse Coverage Amount
P DPN_COVERAGE 16 N 10 O Dependent Coverage Amount
Q EE_GI_OVER 17 N 10 O Employee’s Guaranty Issue Overlimit Amount
R SP_GI_OVER 18 N 10 O Employee Spouse’s Guaranty Issue Overlimit Amount
S DP_GI_OVER 19 N 10 O Employee Dependent’s Guaranty Issue Overlimit Amount
T PREMIUM 20 N 10 O Benefit Premium Amount
U CONTRIB 21 N 10 O Employee Contribution Amount
V DEPN_ID 22 N 4 R Dependent ID if covered
W DEPN_DOCTOR_ID 23 A 10 O Dependent’s Primary Care Physician ID
X DEPN_DOCTOR_NAME 24 A 20 O Dependent’s Primary Care Physician Name
Y BENEF_ID 25 N 4 O Beneficiary ID
Z BENEF_TYPE 26 A 1 O Beneficiary Type (P/C)
AA BENEF_PCNT 27 N 6 O Percent of Beneficiary Coverage
AB BENEF_PREC 28 N 6 O Beneficiary Precedence
AC WAIVE_REASON 29 A 20 O Reason for waiving coverage
AD ENROLL_STATUS 30 A 2 O Employee Enrollment Status
AE COVRD_DATA 31 A 20 O Employee and Dependent IDs covered

To import benefit enrollments:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).
  2. From Operations|Import Processing, select Benefits Import.
  3. In Import Definition Template, select the name of the benefit import template. The system shows the field number and field label that must be included in the data file in the order shown.
  4. If the data file was not already set up, create it using the instructions at the beginning of this topic.
  5. Click Find File. The Upload a File window opens.
  6. In Pick a file to upload, click Choose File, select the data file, and click submit. When you are notified that the file was uploaded, click Close. You return to the Benefits Import page and the name of the selected data file is shown in Filename.
  7. Click Import. A progress box displays the status.
  8. When the progress box shows that the process is complete, click Close to return to the Benefits Import page or Report to open the Job Control Status Report. See See Viewing the Job Control Status Report

Note: Note: While importing a benefit plan, the Max Days Back Dating value is used to validate a benefit plan that is to be terminated.

Importing Benefit Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Common%20to%20BA_BE/Importing-Benefit-Rules.htm Path: BA/Common to BA_BE/Importing-Benefit-Rules.htm

Importing Benefit Rules

The Benefit Rules Import form can import benefit rules information into the system. You can also view benefit imports in progress and continue working on an import that was paused.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To import benefit rules and access this form:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, under Benefits, click Benefit Imports & Reporting.s

  2. Under Benefit Imports, click Benefit Rules Imports. The Benefit Rules Import form opens.

  3. Click Upload File and then Choose File to select the data file.

  4. You can also click Download Sample Header File hyperlink to download a sample file so that you can view the fields that are required while you upload your own file.

  5. Click Submit. A confirmation message displays.

  6. Click Close.

Next, validate the import:

  1. Click Validate Import File.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close.

  3. Click Import.

  4. When the process is complete, click Close. The data file imported.

  5. Click Print Import Report. The Company Benefit Rules Import Report opens.

  6. Click the XLS link to download the report.

Maintaining Enrollment Details

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Common%20to%20BA_BE/Plan_Enrollment_Details.htm Path: BA/Common to BA_BE/Plan_Enrollment_Details.htm

Maintaining Enrollment Details

To perform the following functions, use the Plan Enrollment Details form.

  • Define gap coverage amounts in gap (GAP) benefit plans.

  • Enable employees to set up beneficiary information in life insurance plans during enrollments.

  • Set up dependencies in accidental death and dismemberment (ADD) or group term life (GTL) insurance plans that require employees to enroll in a basic life (LIF) insurance plan.

  • Establish settings in long term disability (LTD) or short term disability (STD) benefit plans that determine when an employee is required to submit an Evidence of Insurability (EOI) form.

Accessing Plan Enrollment Details

The offer type for a benefit plan determines the options that are available in the Plan Enrollment Details form.

To access the Plan Enrollment Details form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens.

  3. Select a Benefit Plan ID.

  4. Click the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and select Enrollment Details.

The Plan Enrollment Details form opens. You cannot search for this form by normal means.

  1. Here, the Benefit Plan ID is auto-populated based on the benefit plan you select on the Group Benefit Plans form. It is a read-only form.

  2. Make the required updates on the form and click Save.

Defining Gap Coverage in Gap Plans

The options that are available when you select a gap (GAP) benefit plan enable you to define the gap coverage amount for the plan. You can also restrict employees who are enrolled in health savings account (HSA) benefit plans from also enrolling in gap benefit plans.

Before you begin:

  • Set up the gap benefit plan to require a medical dependency at the plan level in the Plan Dependency tab in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

To define gap coverage in gap benefit plans:

  1. Open the Plan Enrollment Details form.

Use this option — To define this

Payment Cycle — The frequency with which the employee’s loan payment is deducted. If the employee does not have a loan, leave the Payment Cycle set to Pay Period.

Effective Date — The effective date for the benefit plan to modify. A benefit plan can have multiple effective dates with different settings that are used for different enrollments. You can click New Effective Date to create a new effective date for the benefit plan.

Gap Coverage Amount — The amount of gap coverage.

HSA Enrollee Not Eligible — Whether to restrict enrollees in HSA plans from also enrolling in the gap benefit plan.

  1. Click Save.

Defining Gap Coverage in Medical Plans

When you select a medical (MED) benefit plan, options are available for you to define the gap coverage maximum.

To define gap coverage maximum:

  1. Open the Plan Enrollment Details form.

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The effective date for the benefit plan to modify. A benefit plan can have multiple effective dates with different settings that are used for different enrollments. You can click New Effective Date to create a new effective date for the benefit plan.

Gap Coverage Maximum — The maximum amount of gap coverage. You cannot set gap coverage maximum amounts on family-rated benefit plans.

  1. Click Save.

Enabling Beneficiary Information

When you select a life insurance plan (LIF, GTL, ADD, LIS, LIC, WLI), the Require beneficiaries section option is available. Select this option if employees can enter beneficiaries during enrollments.

Setting Dependencies in ADD and GTL Plans

When you select an additional life insurance plan (GTL or ADD), options are available for you to set up dependencies in life insurance plans that require employees to enroll in a basic life insurance plan (LIF).

You can also use the Plan Enrollment Details form to set the plan to apply an aggregate spouse maximum. This limits the maximum coverage for the employee’s spouse so that it can never exceed the aggregate coverage amount of an employee’s basic and additional life selections.

To set dependencies in ADD and GTL benefit plans:

  1. Open the Plan Enrollment Details form.

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The effective date for the benefit plan to modify. A benefit plan can have multiple effective dates with different settings that are used for different enrollments. You can click New Effective Date to create a new effective date for the benefit plan.

Require beneficiaries section — Whether to allow employees to enter beneficiaries during enrollments.

Require Basic Life Enrollment — Whether to require enrollment in a basic life insurance plan.

  1. Click Save.

Setting Dependencies in Disability Plans

When you select a long term disability (LTD) or short term disability (STD) benefit plan, options are available for you to define settings that determine when an employee is required to submit an EOI form. Set up an LTD or STD benefit plan to require an EOI form at the plan level in the Documents tab on the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

Enrollments that include disability plans that require an EOI are automatically placed in Pending status and trigger an approval process in the Post Benefit Enrollments form.

To set up dependencies in disability benefit plans:

  1. Open the Plan Enrollment Details form.

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The effective date for the benefit plan to modify. A benefit plan can have multiple effective dates with different settings that are used for different enrollments. You can click New Effective Date to create a new effective date for the benefit plan.

Coverage Minimum — The coverage minimum for the benefit plan.

Coverage Maximum — The coverage maximum for the benefit plan.

Increments — The increments to use for differing coverage levels. For example, if the benefit plan is available in increments of $5,000, enter 5,000.

Guaranteed Issue Amount — The maximum amount that an employee can receive without filing an EOI. The employee is required to submit an EOI to receive further coverage.

Guaranteed Issue Default Percentage — The guaranteed issue default percentage if the benefit plan determines the maximum amount that an employee can receive without filing an EOI. It is based on a percentage of the employee’s salary.

Late Entrant GI Amount — The maximum amount that a late entrant employee can receive without filing an EOI. The employee is required to submit an EOI to receive further coverage.

Late Entrant GI Default Percentage — Whether the benefit plan determines the maximum amount (up to 100%) that a late entrant employee can receive without filing an EOI based on a percentage of the employee’s salary,

  1. Click Save.

Required Documentation Rulesets

The Required Documentation Rulesets panel displays for some offer types. You can use this panel to assign one or more required documentation rulesets to a benefit plan. Employees who fit the conditions of the ruleset during enrollments must download and submit an additional form. For more information on Required Documentation Rulesets, see Assigning Documentation Rulesets.

Setting Up Age Banded Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Age_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm Path: BA/Topics/Age_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm

Setting Up Age Banded Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

This section is a guide to setting up age banded benefit plans for the medical, dental, and vision insurance classes at the system level in PrismHR. It is intended for users who have experience setting up benefit plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Only those settings for age banded benefit plans are covered in this section. Some settings described are used only in Benefits Enrollment, and are labeled accordingly. For more information about using Benefits Enrollment, refer to in-product help or to the Benefits Enrollment User Guide.

Applying the Billing Wash Rule

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Apply-Billing-Wash-Rule.htm Path: BA/Topics/Apply-Billing-Wash-Rule.htm

Applying the Billing Wash Rule

For group benefit plans in PrismHR, the billing wash rule determines whether the system charges plan premiums and deductions for a month. This is determined based on where the coverage start or end date falls in relation to the wash rule date.

The wash rule applies to new hire and terminated employees. The following examples illustrate how the wash rules can affect the benefit deductions of new hire and terminated employees.

New Hire Employees

Scenario 1: No Wash Rule Applied

On the Benefit Plan Setup form:

  • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled

  • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month

On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form:

  • Coverage Starts = 01/08/2021

  • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021

Result: The system performs a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 8) comes before the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system charges the employee their regular scheduled deductions.

Scenario 2: Wash Rule Applied

On the Benefit Plan Setup form:

  • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled

  • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month

On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form:

  • Coverage Starts = 01/29/2021

  • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021

The Deduction Starts field shows Wash Rule applied for 202101.

Result: The system does not perform a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 29) comes after the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system does not charge the employee.

Terminated Employees

The following is an example of a scenario where the system does not apply the wash rule to a group benefit plan for a terminated employee.

Note: Note: If the Coverage Ends On field is set to “End of Month Following Termination Date” and the Wash Rule date is set to “End of Month”, the wash rule is not applied. However, any other Coverage Ends On Option will result in a full month’s charge upon termination.

On the Benefit Plan Setup form:

  • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled

  • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month

On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form:

  • Coverage Starts = 01/22/2021

  • Coverage Ends = 03/05/2021

  • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021

The Deduction Starts field shows Wash Rule applied for 202101.

  • Deduction Ends = 03/05/2021

The Deduction Ends field shows Wash Rule applied for 202103.

Result: The system does not perform a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 22) comes after the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system does not charge the employee. Since the employee was terminated on March 5th (before the 15th day of the month), the system also applies the wash rule to the full month of March.

Building the Benefit Rules XML Download

Benefit Salary Maintenance

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit%20Salary%20Maintenance.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit Salary Maintenance.htm

Benefit Salary Maintenance

Use this form to add an effective date to change employee Benefit Salary and track historical Benefit Salary changes. Thus managing changes to Benefits Salary can be done proactively without real-time changes being necessary for Benefit calculation accuracy.

To access this form to add a new benefit salary and update the effective date:

  1. Click the HRmenu.

  2. From HR|Action, click Benefit Salary Maintenance. The form opens.

  3. Fill in the following fields:

For this option Provide this information
Employee Click this hyperlink to select an employee.
Current Annual Pay Rate The current annual pay rate of the selected employee.
Current Rate Effective Date The date from which the current rate for annual pay applies to the selected employee.
Current Benefit Salary The current Benefit Salary of the selected employee.
New Benefit Salary New Benefit Salary that you want to add for the selected employee.
Benefit Salary Start Date The start date from when you want to apply the updated employee benefit salary.

  1. Click Save to save the new benefit salary for the selected employee. It also updates the current data under the Pay tab on the Employee Details form.

  2. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

Changing the Current and Future Benefit Salary Dates

The Benefit Salary History section streamlines the process of viewing employee’s benefit salary information. You can track historical Benefit Salary changes that you make for the selected employee. Once you make an update to the benefit salary of the selected employee, the history of the dates from which it was made effective is displayed here.

The following column displays:

  • Date Effective - The date from which the updated benefit salary will come into effect.

  • Benefit Salary - The updated benefit salary amount.

The past dates in the Date Effective column are a read-only field. However, the current and future dates under this column are hyperlinks which you can click to edit the effective date.

To edit or add a new effective date:

  1. Under the Benefit Salary History section, in the Date Effective column, select a current or future date. The future dates will be a hyperlink. A dialog box opens.

  2. In the New Effective Date, select an effective date.

  3. Click Save to save the selected benefit salary record with the updated effective date.

  4. Click Cancel to clear the selected New Effective Date.

  5. Click Close to close the modal form and return to the Benefit Salary Maintenance form without making any changes to the selected benefit salary record.

Note: Note: On the Employee Details form, Under the Pay tab, when you delete the current Benefit Salary then the Benefit Salary change is recorded with a null value in the Benefit Salary History section on the Benefit Salary Maintenance form.

To delete a future effective date:

  1. Under the Benefit Salary History section, in the Date Effective column, select the checkbox for a future date.

  2. Click Delete. A confirmation pop-up message stating, <number of selected record(s)> Benefit Salary change will be deleted. Are you sure? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to delete the selected record(s).

  • Click No to return to the form.

Note: Note the following validations for the Date Effective column while using Past/Current/Future effective dates for a Benefit Salary History record.

  • When you enter Past date as the effective date:
  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the date selected for the Benefit Salary Start Date field.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the new history record with the new effective data.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the same effective date with the current data.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  • When you enter Current date as the effective date:

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the date selected for the Benefit Salary Start Date field. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to create the new history record with the new effective data. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the same effective date with the current data. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  • When you enter Future date as the effective date:

If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the current data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the future date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

Note: If there are multiple future dates, the warning message uses the next available pending future date.

  • Click Yes to save the effective date and create the new history with the new effective data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the future date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the future date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the current data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

Benefit Utilities

Use this form to manage Benefit related utilities.

To access this form to add a new benefit salary and update the effective date:

  1. Click the Back Officemenu.

  2. From Operations|Utility Processing, click Benefit Utilities. The form opens.

  3. The form has the following filter:

  • Utility- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • Select - This is the default option.

  • Manage Orphaned Benefit Records - Select this filter to display the Orphaned Record Type filter, which has the following drop-down options:

  • Select - This is the default option.

  • Benefit Plan Setup - The orphaned records due to missing Benefit Plan Setup records.

  • Group Benefit Plan Types - The orphaned records due to missing Plan Type.

  • Plan Types - The orphaned records due to missing Group Benefit Plan Types code.

  • Relationships - The orphaned records due to missing relationship code.

  • SH2 Auto Enroll - Select this filter to identify the existing employees that are eligible for Safe Harbor 2 Match that do not have an active Retirement Plan Enrollment record.

  • Unarchive Enrollments - Select this filter to identify the existing archived employees.

  • Auto Escalation - Select this filter to identify enrollments that are not flagged as Auto Escalation?.

  1. Click Search to get the results based on your filter selection.

  2. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

Using the Manage Orphaned Benefit Records Utility

To use and manage orphaned related benefit records utility:

  1. From the Utility drop-down, select the Manage Orphaned Benefit Records option. The Orphaned Record Type drop-down displays.

  2. Select Benefit Plan Setup, Group Benefit Plan Types, Plan Types, or Relationships from the drop-down list. The Report Filters section displays.

  3. In the Report Filters section, fill in the following fields:

For this option — Provide this information

Client ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

Client Name — This field auto-populates when you select the Client ID.

Benefit Plan ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all the benefit plans. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected benefit plans, enter the Benefit Plan IDs here or click the Benefit Plan ID link and select them from the Select Benefit Plan dialog box. > Note: Note: This field does not display for Relationships Orphaned Record Type.

Plan Description — This field auto-populates when you select the Benefit Plan ID.

  1. Click Search. A job control runs.

  2. The list of orphaned records displays in the Results section.

Note: Note: Based on your selection in the Orphaned Record Type drop-down filter, the results are displayed.

  • If you select Benefit Plan Setup, then in the Results section, the list of orphaned records caused due to deleting Benefit Plan Setup records are displayed.

  • If you select Group Benefit Plan Types, then in the Results section the list of orphaned records due to missing Plan Type are displayed.

  • If you select Plan Types, then in the Results section the list of orphaned records caused by deleting the Group Benefit Plan Type code are displayed.

  • If you select Relationships, then in the Results section the list of orphaned records caused by deleting the Relationship Code are displayed.

This Results section displays the following columns:

For Relationships, the Results section displays the following columns:

  • File Name

  • Employee ID

  • Employment Status Class

  • Client ID

  • Dependent ID

  • Dependent Name

  • Relationship Code

  • Orphaned Reason

Export using the Report button

When you select Utility as Manage Orphaned Benefit Records, then for the options under the Orphaned Record Type drop-down, when you click Search to run the report filters, then under the Results section that is displayed, you can export the report of orphaned records for the selected orphaned record types by clicking the Report button.

In the results section, you can search for an employee or view the results in according to batches as described below:

  • Search Employee Name - This input field allows you to search for a specific employee name. Additionally, when you search for an employee, the results are displayed only within the batch selected.

  • Batch No. - It represents the threshold for the returned records. For example, if the threshold is to display 1000 records in one batch and the total results returned are 2500, then it will be divided into 3 batch, where Batch 1 will have 1000 records, Batch 2 will display the next 1000 records, and Batch 3 will display the remaining 500 records. You can select the batch number from the drop-down list.

Changing an Employee’s Benefit Billing Record

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Adjustments.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Adjustments.htm

Changing an Employee’s Benefit Billing Record

To make changes to an employee’s benefit billing record, use the Benefit Adjustments form.

Note: Note: To quickly access the Benefit Adjustments import template in the Data Import Tool, select Import Benefit Adjustments. You can use the Benefit Adjustments import template to import multiple benefit adjustments for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To access this form and change an employee’s benefit billing record:

  1. Click the HR menu.

  2. From HR|Change, click Benefit Adjustments. The form opens.

  3. Fill in the following fields:

For this option Provide this information
Employee The Employee whose benefit adjustments you want to see. Either enter the employee name or Employee ID to display a list of matching employee records. To search for an employee associated with this client, either click the Employee hyperlink or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the Employee Search Results selector. The system lists any existing adjustments. To sort the records by a column, click the column header to toggle between ascending and descending order.
Next Pay Date: The employee’s next regularly scheduled pay date displays if that payroll is in the Ready state. (This field is for viewing purposes only.)
New Adjustment To add a new benefit adjustment for this employee, click the New Adjustment hyperlink to open the Adjustment Details form.
Filter By Status Use this filter to list all benefit adjustments for the employee by their status. You can choose one of the following dropdown options: - All – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee. - Outstanding – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is less than Cycles. - Complete – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is equal to Cycles.

  • All – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee.

  • Outstanding – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is less than Cycles.

  • Complete – To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is equal to Cycles. | Filter By Plan | Use this filter to list all benefit adjustments for the employee by Benefit Plan. Enter or select the Benefit Plan plan from the Select Benefit Plan selector. | A list appears showing the various benefit adjustments for the selected employee as per selections made above.

  • An option is available to the left of the header named Benefit Plan. Select this option to select, in bulk, all benefit adjustments for the employee which have zero Cycles Billed. Click Delete to delete all such adjustments in bulk.

  • A checkbox is available to the left of each benefit adjustment for the employee which have zero Cycles Billed. Select one or more and click Delete to delete the selected benefit adjustment(s) only.

  • The Delete button will by default remain disabled. It will get enabled only if you try to either delete in bulk or delete selected benefit adjustments for the employee which have zero Cycles Billed. Once you click Delete, you will receive a confirmation stating Adjustments will be deleted. Are you sure?

  • Click Yes to delete the selected adjustments and return to the Benefit Adjustments form with the updated adjustment list.

  • Click No to return to the Benefit Adjustments form without any changes. The selections remain.

New Benefit Adjustment

To enter a new benefit adjustment for a selected employee:

  1. Click the New Adjustment hyperlink on the Benefits Adjustments form. The Adjustment Details form displays.

  2. Complete these fields as required

For this option Provide this information
Benefit Plan ID The Benefit Plan that requires an adjustment. You can enter it here or click the Benefit Plan ID hyperlink and select it from the Select Benefit Plan dialog box. Once you click the Benefit Plan ID hyperlink, the Benefit Plan selector opens which displays the Group Benefit Plans offered by the client. You can use the various filters on the Benefit Plan selector to refine your search for example Plan ID or Name. You also use the following additional filters: - The default High Deductible Plan (HDHP) filter status is All. You can choose any of the following options: - All – The list will include both High Deductible Plans and plans that are not High Deductible Plans. - Yes – The list will include only those benefit plans which are High Deductible Plans. It is indicated with a status Y in the list. - No – The list will include only those benefit plans which are not High Deductible Plans. It is indicated with a status N in the list. - The default Status filter status is Active. You can choose any of the following options: - Active (Default) – The list will display only the active Group Benefit Plans offered by the client. - Terminated – The list will display only the terminated Group Benefit Plans offered by the client - Never Implemented – The list will display only the Group Benefit Plans offered by the client but were never implemented.
- The default High Deductible Plan (HDHP) filter status is All. You can choose any of the following options:
- All – The list will include both High Deductible Plans and plans that are not High Deductible Plans.
- Yes – The list will include only those benefit plans which are High Deductible Plans. It is indicated with a status Y in the list.
- No – The list will include only those benefit plans which are not High Deductible Plans. It is indicated with a status N in the list.
- The default Status filter status is Active. You can choose any of the following options:
- Active (Default) – The list will display only the active Group Benefit Plans offered by the client.
- Terminated – The list will display only the terminated Group Benefit Plans offered by the client
- Never Implemented – The list will display only the Group Benefit Plans offered by the client but were never implemented.
Period (yyymm) The Period for the benefit plan in the format YYYYMM. For example, 201710 for October 2017. If a the pay date for a payroll batch is within this period, the system processes the deduction from the employee’s net earnings, after deducting taxes.
Start Date The start date of the period when this deduction goes into effect.
Bill Amount The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of this adjustment.
Employee Contribution The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount.
Insurance Cost The premium cost associated with this adjustment.
Bill Code Read-only field that displays the related Bill Code for the selected Benefit Plan. > Note: Note: The value in this field is fetched from the corresponding Group Benefit Plan based on the following criteria from the fields on the System Parameters and the Benefit Plan Setup forms: \
System Parameters form (Require Prepay Benefit Account No. field) Benefit Plan Setup form (One Month Prepay field)
No Unchecked
Setup Unchecked
Yes Unchecked
Yes Checked
Deduction Rebate Bill Code Read-only field that displays the related Deduction Rebate Bill Code for the selected Benefit Plan. > Note: Note: The applicable deduction code value in this field is fetched from the Deduction Code in use for the employee enrollment based on the following criteria from the fields on the System Parameters, Benefit Plan Setup, and Employee Benefits Enrollment forms: \
System Parameters form (Require Prepay Benefit Account No. field) Benefit Plan Setup form (One Month Prepay field)
No Unchecked
Setup Unchecked
No Unchecked
Setup Unchecked
Yes Unchecked
Yes Unchecked
Yes Checked
Yes Checked
Net Inv Effect Takes the Bill Code and Deduction Rebate Bill Code values into account and accurately assess and calculates the Net Inv Effect. This will be blank for a new adjustment. The following table illustrates the calculation method based on the values fetched in the Bill Code and the Deduction Rebate Bill Code fields: \
Bill Code found? Deduction Rebate Bill Code found?
Yes N/A
N/A Yes
N/A N/A
Yes Yes
Comment Descriptive comments about this adjustment, typically something that would help someone understand the benefit adjustment. To view comments previously made in a manually created adjustment, either enter an employee in the Employee field or click the field and select one from the list that displays. The previously entered adjustment displays and also displays a comment if one was previously entered.
Adjust Cycles Click this hyperlink to change the number of cycles. > Note: Note: An informative text stating This action will divide the total of the original amounts by the new number of cycles. is displayed on the pop-up displayed. Also, this hyperlink is available only if there are no Cycles Billed for that benefit adjustment record.
Cycles The number of future payroll cycles to apply this adjustment.
Cycles Billed For a new adjustment this value will be zero.
B/R Adjustment The B/R Adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of this adjustment.
Retro Enroll Check this box if the adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Any Employee Contributions for this adjustment will be taken post-tax.
Ref. Number This will be blank for a new adjustment.
  1. Click Save to save this new benefit adjustment.

Edit an Existing Benefit Adjustment

To edit an existing benefit adjustment for a selected employee:

  1. Click the Benefit Plan hyperlink for the benefit adjustment that you want to edit on the Benefits Adjustments form. The Adjustment Details form opens up.

  • When a benefit adjustment is pulled via the payroll process and the Cycles Billed value is updated to the next number in the sequence, the following corresponding information is now listed in the new table on the right of the form:

  • Voucher # – You can click this hyperlink to open the Employee Voucher in a modal. You can navigate to the Benefits tab to view the adjustment details.

  • Pay Date – The Pay Date of the Employee Voucher.

  • Batch # – The Payroll Number of the Employee Voucher.

  • Bill Amount - The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of this adjustment.

  • Employee Contribution – The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount.

  • Net Inv Effect – This will be blank for a new adjustment.

  • Total – The total values for the Bill Amount, Employee Contribution, and Net Inv Effect columns of the vouchers.

  1. Complete these fields as required:

For this option — Provide this information

Benefit Plan ID — This field is pre-populated with the Benefit Plan ID. You cannot change it

Period (yyymm) — The period for the benefit plan in the format YYYYMM. For example, 201710 for October 2017. If a the pay date for a payroll batch is within this period, the system processes the deduction from the employee’s net earnings, after deducting taxes.

Start Date — The start date of the period when this deduction goes into effect.

Bill Amount — The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of this adjustment.

Employee Contribution — The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount.

Insurance Cost — The premium cost associated with this adjustment.

Net Inv Effect — This field will be auto-populated.

Comment — Descriptive comments about this adjustment, typically something that would help someone understand the benefit adjustment. To view comments previously made in a manually created adjustment, either enter an employee in the Employee field or click the field and select one from the list that displays. The previously entered adjustment displays and also displays a comment if one was previously entered.

Adjust Cycles — Click this hyperlink to change the number of cycles.

Cycles — The number of future payroll cycles to apply this adjustment.

Cycles Billed — This field will be auto-populated with the number of cycles billed. When an adjustment record already has cycles billed, the Cycles Billed field for this adjustment will be read only.

B/R Adjustment — The B/R Adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of this adjustment.

Retro Enroll — Check this box if the adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Any Employee Contributions for this adjustment will be taken post-tax.

Ref. Number — This field will be auto-populated.

Note: Note: If the Cycles Billed field value is greater than 0 for a selected benefit adjustment record, then the Period (yyyymm), Bill Amount, Employee Contribution, and Insurance Cost fields become read-only. Also, the Adjust Cycles hyperlink is disabled in this scenario.

  1. Click Save to save changes to this benefit adjustment.

Maintaining Benefit Eligibility Groups

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Groups.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Groups.htm

Maintaining Benefit Eligibility Groups

Use the Benefit Groups form to create benefit groups for each group of employees who have the same benefit eligibility rules for a specified benefit. Each benefit group has the same benefit eligibility requirements and contribution rates. For example, the client may have a “standard” benefit group and an “executive” benefit group.

To create benefit eligibility groups:

  1. From the Onboarding & Benefits work center, select Benefit Plan Maintenance|Group Benefit Plans (Client)|Benefit Groups.

  2. Complete these fields:

Use this option — To define this

Group — The benefit group ID. If you are creating a new group, use something brief but descriptive, for example, STD. After entering a group, you can view the Employees Assigned To form. See Using the Employees Assigned To form. > Note: Note: The system automatically assigns the Primary Benefit Group as “1,” which cannot be changed. (This Benefit Group Name automatically defaults to “PRIMARY,” which can be changed.) If you try to delete the Primary Benefit Group, an error message displays.

Group Name — A descriptive name for the benefit group, for example, Standard.

Retirement Or Benefit Plans Only — Whether the group applies to Retirement plans only, Benefit plans only, or Both.

Stop New Use On — The date after which this benefit group can no longer be added to new benefit rules or new employees.

Stop All Use On — The date after which this benefit group cannot be used.

  1. If a benefit group includes Eligible Benefits for Group Benefit Plans contribution:

Use this option — To define this

Benefit Plan ID — Displays each benefit plan ID for which employees in the benefit group are eligible. Select a plan by clicking Benefit Plan ID.

Plan Description — A description of the Benefit Plan ID.

Import Eligible Benefits — A quick link to import eligible benefit plans. Select this quick link to display the Eligible Benefits import template in the Data Import Tool.

Note: Note the following:

  • The Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans panel enables you to select one or more Benefit Plan IDs only if you have selected Benefit Groups Restrict Eligibility option in the Eligible Benefits Determinant field in the Benefits tab on the Client Details form. If you do not select this option, then you will not be able to select any Benefit Plan IDs. A conditional message, “Access to this section requires the Eligible Benefits Determinant to be set to Benefit Groups Restrict Eligibility on the Client Details form.” also displays in the Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans panel.

  • If the Eligible Benefits panel is disabled and there is any existing data in this panel, then on saving the form, the system displays a message: “Do you wish to clear the existing Benefit Plan IDs in the Eligible Benefits section? Y/N”.

  • Click Yes to clear the existing Benefit Plans data listed in the Eligible Benefits panel and save the rest of the data on the form.

  • Click No to save all the data on the form.

  1. If a benefit group includes a Cafeteria Plancontribution:

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The effective date for the flat company contribution amount.

Contribution Amount — The employer’s flat, monthly contribution amount. The system automatically allocates the employer contributions.

EE First Dollar — If the employee must pay the first dollars, the amount the employee must pay.

EE Premium Only — Whether the cafeteria plan contributes only towards the employee portion of the premium (Yes or No).

  1. Click Save to save changes to the record.

Note:

  • When using the API or an import, the system writes the benefit group to the employee’s record using the current date. A benefit group history record will be created immediately.

  • When using the Bulk Change utility, a benefit group history record will be created immediately.

  • All New Hire processes (manual entry, Onboarding, Import, API) will trigger record creation for a benefit group history record, using the Original Hire Date as the Effective Date assigned to the record.

  • When using the rehire process, the benefit group will be written to the employee record using the current system date as the Effective Date. If the Benefit Group was not changed when using the rehire process, the system still writes the benefit group to the employee’s record using the current date as the Effective Date.

Using the Actions Menu

You can access other benefit group features using the Actions menu:

  • Viewing the Audit Log

  • User fields: Enter values for the company in the User-Defined Fields form. Your organization defines these custom fields.

  • Employee Assigned To: Select this to view a list of employees at the company assigned to the benefit group.

Using the Employees Assigned To form

After entering a benefit group, you can view the Employees Assigned To form under the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

. Use this form to view all employees who are assigned to the selected benefit group for the client.

The form displays two fields:

  • Active: The active employee count displays the number of active employees assigned to the selected benefit group regardless of the filter option selected for the Status.

  • Status: By default, this lists the total number of active employees assigned to the selected benefit group. You can change this to any one of the options from the drop-down.

The grid includes these columns:

Column Name Description
Employee ID When clicked, the Employee Details form opens for the employee.
Employee Name The employee name is listed here.
Employment Status The employment status of the employee will display here.

You can sort this grid by any of these three column headers.

Click Report to run the Employees Assigned To report. After running the report, you can download the data as an XLS file.

Network Zip Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Network_Locations.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Network_Locations.htm

Network Zip Codes

To enter locations by ZIP code for benefit plans that have a network assigned, use the Network Zip Codes form, accessed by selecting Network ZIP Codes in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

from the Group Benefit Plans form. This form only displays in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

when the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected.

Users can also import multiple locations using the Network ZIP Code Import form. For more information, see Importing Network ZIP Codes.

To set up locations for a benefit plan with an assigned network:

  1. The Benefit Plan ID is prepopulated from the Group Benefit Plans form.

  2. Select a Network ID from the drop-down. This is required.

  3. In the ZIP Codes column, enter the five-digit ZIP code where this benefit plan is offered. The City & State will display if the ZIP code exists in the system.

You can enter multiple ZIP Codes as needed: click + to add additional rows.

  1. Click Save.

Setting up Benefit Plan Defaults

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Plan_Defaults.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Plan_Defaults.htm

Setting up Benefit Plan Defaults

Use this form to set up the benefit plan defaults for the selected plan. On the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form, click the Plan Defaults hyperlink for a Benefit Plan ID to open this form for the selected plan. You will not be able to find this form using normal search means.

To set up benefit plan defaults:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
Plan ID This field will be prepopulated.
Plan Description This field will also be prepopulated.
Billing Rate Group Enter a billing rate group for the selected benefit plan or click the Billing Rate Group selector to select it from the Select Rate Group dialog box which will only populate with Billing Rate Groups that are set up for the selected Benefit Plan.
Premium Rate Group Enter a premium rate group for the selected benefit plan or click the Premium Rate Group selector to select it from the Select Rate Group dialog box which will only populate with Premium Rate Groups that are set up for the selected Benefit Plan.
Rule Template ID This field is optional. Rule Template ID is used to calculate eligibility, coverage, and employee contributions in the absence of a client or plan specific rule. Enter a Rule Template ID for the selected benefit plan or click the Rule Template ID selector to select it from the Select Benefit Rule Template dialog box.
One Month Prepay Check this box if one month prepay is required. You cannot enable Prepay when Billing Wash Rule is used.
Add One Month for Prepay Check this box if one month prepay is required. You cannot enable Prepay when Billing Wash Rule is used.
Annual Periods This setting calculates payroll deduction amounts for employee benefit contributions and affects the calculation of weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, or monthly premiums. Select one of the following options: - 48 - 52 48 weeks is generally recommended because the total amount that gets deducted from the client and employee will always equal the same monthly premium (and invoice) from the insurance carrier. However, you can override this setting for any of your individual clients.
  • 48
  • 52 | Use Billing Wash Rule? | Check this box if you want to use Billing Wash Rule. You cannot enable Billing Wash Rule when Prepay is used. | | Cafe Plan Eligible | Check this box if this benefit plan is eligible for Cafe Plan. | | Coverage Ends On | Specify the date when coverage ends by choosing one of the drop-downs. | | Benefit Billing Frequency | Specify how often benefits are billed from the following options: - Pay Period - Monthly - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2 - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3 - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4 |
  • Pay Period
  • Monthly
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4 | Pay Deduction Frequency | Specify how often benefits are deducted from payroll from the following options: - Pay Period - Monthly - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2 - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3 - Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4 |
  • Pay Period
  • Monthly
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3
  • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4

  1. Click Save to save the defaults for the selected benefit plan.

  2. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time and return to the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form.

Note: Once you make any changes to any plan default, this will be the setting applied to all clients processed during the Client Benefit Plan Defaults update.

Setting Up a Benefit Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Plan_Setup.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Plan_Setup.htm

Setting Up a Benefit Plan

To maintain the client’s group benefit, retirement, flexible spending, employer match, and HSA match plans, use the Benefit Plan Setup form.

Note: To quickly access the Client Benefit Plan Import form, select Import Client Benefit Plans. (Set the Plan Class to Group Benefit to view this quick link.) You can use the Client Benefit Plan Import form to import the client benefit plan. After that, you must set up a data file and a benefit import definition.

Benefit plans must first be set up at the system level. When this is done, each plan offered by the client is established in Benefit Plan Setup.

Note: Note: If your organization is using Benefits Enrollment, the forms for flexible spending plans will display in enrollments only if the plans are set up in Benefit Plan Setup and in the Benefits tab in Client Details. see Setting Up Client Benefits for more information.

You can access benefit-related features and settings using the Actions menu:

  • Viewing the Audit Log

  • Using a Default Benefit Plan Template

  • Viewing Employees Assigned to a Benefit Plan

  • Maintaining Benefit Eligibility Groups

  • Setting Up Employee Enrollment Conditions

  • Establishing Eligibility by Benefit Group: Displays only when you select Flexible Spending in the Plan Class drop-down and select the Use Benefit Groups option.

  • Clone Benefits: Creates new benefit plans for this client based on the plans for another client.

Establishing Basic Information

Establish the basic information for the plan in the Benefit Plan Setup panel.

Note: Note: Different panels display on this form depending on the selected Plan Class. Refer to the appropriate panel descriptions for the plan you are editing.

To establish basic information about a plan:

  1. Open the Basic Plan Setup panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Plan Class The plan class (required): this determines the other panels that display on the form.
Plan ID The ID of the benefit plan you want to create or view (required). The system displays the plan information on the rest of the form. > Note: Note: - You cannot delete a benefit plan using the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client as this will orphan the associated benefit rules and can cause payroll errors along with other issues. If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client, you will receive an error stating There are Benefit Rules assigned to this benefit plan. Please remove all rule references. You can only delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are no existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client or after you have removed all the benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client. - You cannot delete a benefit plan using the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA as this will orphan the associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records and can cause payroll errors along with other issues. - If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA, you will receive an error stating This plan cannot be deleted. There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with enrollment history. Example: Employee Enrollment for Employee ID [XXXXX] and Effective Date [XX/XX/XXXX]. - If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Pending, Waived, or Eligible, you will receive a warning stating There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with an enrollment status of pending, waived and/or eligible. Do you wish to continue? - Click Yes to delete the selected Plan ID. - Click No to return to the Benefit Plan Setup form with the selected Plan ID and associated data populated. - You can only delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are no associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA.

Establishing Rate Information

To establish rate information for Group Benefit plans, use the Group Benefits Setup panel.

To establish rate information for group benefit plans:

  1. Open the Group Benefits Setup panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Billing Rate Group The assigned Billing Rate Group for this plan, if it is a billing rate plan. When you click the Billing Rate Group hyperlink, the selector will only display the active billing rate groups assigned to the Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form.
Premium Rate Group The assigned Premium Rate Group for this plan, if it is a premium rate plan. When you click the Premium Rate Group hyperlink, the selector will only display the active premium rate groups assigned to the Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form.
Pending Rate Group The Pending Billing Rate Group for this plan, if appropriate. When you click the Pending Rate Group hyperlink, the selector will only display those billing rate groups assigned to the Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form which have an Effective Date tied to the Billing Rate Group. - When the custom feature code named PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL is NOT assigned to the System Parameters form for a client, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Group Benefits Setup section, the Pending Rate Group field will display as Pending Billing Rate Group.
  • When the custom feature code named PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL is NOT assigned to the System Parameters form for a client, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Group Benefits Setup section, the Pending Rate Group field will display as Pending Billing Rate Group. | Pending Rate Group Effective Date | The date when the pending billing rate group becomes effective. - When the custom feature code named PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL is NOT assigned to the System Parameters form for a client, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Group Benefits Setup section, the Pending Rate Group Effective Date field will now display as Pending Rate Group Effective Date. |
  • When the custom feature code named PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL is NOT assigned to the System Parameters form for a client, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Group Benefits Setup section, the Pending Rate Group Effective Date field will now display as Pending Rate Group Effective Date. | Pend Prem Rate Group | The Pending Premium Rate Group for this plan, if appropriate.
