When you select any option in the Use Billing Wash Rule? field on the Group Benefit Plan form, then that option is displayed with a Default tag in parenthesis in the Use Billing Wash Rule? field on the Benefit Plan Setup form. This setting provides visibility to help you identify the setting that is being used at the global or the system level. For examples on applying the billing wash rule, see Applying the Billing Wash Rule. |
  • Select Yes to enable it, and when enabled, the Wash Rule Date On/Before field displays. You can select for the system to apply the wash rule on or before the 10th Day of the Month through the 20th Day of the Month, or at End of Month.
  • Select No to not apply the wash rule at the global level. | Cafe Plan Eligible | Whether this benefit is eligible for the client’s cafe plan. For example, this option is selected if the client offers $1500 to cover benefit plans and this plan qualifies. | | Benefit Billing Frequency | When plan billing occurs. If you select one of the monthly options, PrismHR bills the client the whole portion at the beginning of the month, and then gives credits for the other pay periods in that month. If you do not make a selection, the system uses the pay period. | | Payroll Deduction Frequency | Whether to override the employee’s normal pay period payroll deduction frequency. The standard is each pay period. | | Payroll Deduction Frequency | If instructed by the PrismHR Customer Support Team, the frequency for calculating premiums. | | Premium Calculation Month/Day | The month and day to use to calculate plan premiums. | | Client Plan Renewal Month/Day | Allow you to provide a plan renewal date for a benefit plan. Select is the default option in both the month and day drop-down lists. A tool-tip is provided with a message stating This field will be used as an override to the date specified on the Group Benefit Plans form. If one exists for the Benefit Plan selected, the Group Benefit Renewal date will be displayed. which explains the functionality of this field. > Note: Note: Please note the following: - This field is used as an override to the date specified on the Group Benefit Plans form (if one exists for the Benefit Plan selected). - On the Group Benefit Plans form, when you assign a value to the Plan Renewal Month field, then that value is displayed as read-only field to the right of the Client Plan Renewal Month/Day field with a label named Group Benefit Renewal on the Benefit Plan Setup form. |
  • This field is used as an override to the date specified on the Group Benefit Plans form (if one exists for the Benefit Plan selected).
  • On the Group Benefit Plans form, when you assign a value to the Plan Renewal Month field, then that value is displayed as read-only field to the right of the Client Plan Renewal Month/Day field with a label named Group Benefit Renewal on the Benefit Plan Setup form. | Network Selection Rule | Network Selection Rule: For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR. | | Carrier Account | A Carrier Account. It does not need to be one of those entered in Group Benefit Plans, but if it is you must enter the same risk factors in the Risk Factor panel. | | Max Days Back Dating | Client-level limit (in days) for back-dating coverage start/end dates. Note: If the Max Days Back Dating field does not have a value defined on the Benefit Plan Setup form, but has a value defined for this field on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the system uses the value defined on the Group Benefit Plans form as default. | | Auto Enrollment | Whether to enable automatic enrollment and set employee waive options for this benefit plan. This option depends upon other settings in the system; see Setting Up Waive Options for more information. - If selected, the employee auto enrolls in the benefit plan and does not have the option to waive coverage. - If not selected, the employee has the option to waive coverage in the benefit plan. Note: Please note the following: - On the Group Benefit Plans form, if you set Auto Enroll field to No, and then if you select the Auto Enrollment checkbox then a warning pop-up stating Benefit Plan <The selectedPlan ID> is flagged as Auto Enroll ‘No’ on the Group Benefit Plans form. This will override the value assigned on the Benefit Plan Setup form. is displayed. A warning message stating This plan is flagged as Auto Enroll ‘No’ on the Group Benefit Plans form. This will override the value assigned on the Benefit Plan Setup form. is also displayed below the selected Plan ID. - On the Group Benefit Plans form, if you set Auto Enroll field to Yes, and then if you select the Auto Enrollment checkbox then a message stating This plan is setup to auto enroll is displayed. |
  • If selected, the employee auto enrolls in the benefit plan and does not have the option to waive coverage.
  • If not selected, the employee has the option to waive coverage in the benefit plan.
  • On the Group Benefit Plans form, if you set Auto Enroll field to No, and then if you select the Auto Enrollment checkbox then a warning pop-up stating Benefit Plan <The selectedPlan ID> is flagged as Auto Enroll ‘No’ on the Group Benefit Plans form. This will override the value assigned on the Benefit Plan Setup form. is displayed. A warning message stating This plan is flagged as Auto Enroll ‘No’ on the Group Benefit Plans form. This will override the value assigned on the Benefit Plan Setup form. is also displayed below the selected Plan ID.
  • On the Group Benefit Plans form, if you set Auto Enroll field to Yes, and then if you select the Auto Enrollment checkbox then a message stating This plan is setup to auto enroll is displayed. | Suppress O/E Auto Term | Whether to prevent the posting procedure from terminating enrollments that are active in that benefit plan. | | Suppress Benefit Adjustment on Employee Termination | Whether the client wants to suppress benefit adjustments that would normally have been created due to payroll timing if an employee is terminated. The Suppress Automatic Benefit Adjustment field in the Benefits tab in the Client Details form overrides this field and must also be selected for this setting to go into effect. | | Default Network ID | The Default Network ID that the system uses as a default for employees who enroll in the plan. | | Rule Date to Use for Take-On | A date that is greater than the PEO start date. This avoids a PEO start date that is less than the benefit rule date (causing employees to not be offered benefits), | | Earliest Premium Rate Date to Use Earliest Billing Rate Date to Use | The available premium and billing rate effective dates set up at the system level for the group benefit plan. If the date you want is not available in the list, set up the effective date and rates at the group benefit plan level. If you have clients with multiple benefit plan billing and premium rates, select these dates to offer those clients interim rates before the next open enrollment date. | ## Setting Up Fringe Benefit Pay Codes

To treat a client-paid portion of this benefit as a fringe benefit, use The Fringe Benefit Pay Codes panel. The system automatically adds the pay code and amount to the Other Earnings section of the calculated regular pay vouchers.

To set up a fringe benefit pay code:

  1. Open the Fringe Benefit Pay Codes panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Fringe Benefit Pay Code Each Fringe Benefit Pay Code to add to the calculated regular pay vouchers.
Add to Retirement Pay Whether to include the pay code in 401(k) wages when calculating retirement benefits.
Only apply to S-Corp Principal Employees Whether only S-Corp Principal employees will have the client benefit portion treated as a fringe benefit. Otherwise, this portion is treated as a normal deduction. > Note: Note the following: - If you enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup only employees who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal employee will have the client-paid portion of the benefit treated as a fringe benefit through the payroll process. (If they are not an S-Corp Principal employee then the employer portion is not treated as a fringe benefit.) - If you do not enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup the system performs as usual and treats the client-paid portion of that benefit as a fringe benefit, assigning it to the defined fringe benefit Pay Code through the payroll process. - The system performs an additional validation during payroll calculation, which checks each employee who is enrolled in the benefit plan to determine if they are an S-Corp Principal. Employees enrolled in the benefit plan who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal must have the client paid portion of that benefit assigned to the defined fringe benefit pay code and listed in Other Payments on their payroll voucher.
  • If you enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup only employees who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal employee will have the client-paid portion of the benefit treated as a fringe benefit through the payroll process. (If they are not an S-Corp Principal employee then the employer portion is not treated as a fringe benefit.)
  • If you do not enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup the system performs as usual and treats the client-paid portion of that benefit as a fringe benefit, assigning it to the defined fringe benefit Pay Code through the payroll process.
  • The system performs an additional validation during payroll calculation, which checks each employee who is enrolled in the benefit plan to determine if they are an S-Corp Principal. Employees enrolled in the benefit plan who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal must have the client paid portion of that benefit assigned to the defined fringe benefit pay code and listed in Other Payments on their payroll voucher. ## Defining Risk Factors

To enter data about risk factors (if necessary), use the Risk Factor panel. The global settings determine whether the risk factor is standard or extended precision, and whether it applies to premiums, billing, or both.

To set up information about risk factors:

  1. Open the Risk Factor panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The date when the premium risk factor goes into effect.

Premium Risk Factor — The Premium Risk Factor to use as a multiplier when calculating the benefit premiums (both cost and billing) for each unique client/benefit plan combination. The Premium Risk Factor amount is applied to the calculated premium for the benefit. If the system uses standard risk factors, the system limits it to two decimal places. (If you enter more, the system rounds it off to two digits.)

Admin Surcharge — Currently this field is suppressed to only allow a blank value. If a user attempts to enter a value in this field, the system displays the following message: The Admin Surcharge feature is not available in this release. This field will be available in a future release.

Applying the Hawaii 1.5% Rule

Note: Note: The Hawaii 1.5% Rule section will only display on the Benefit Plan Setup form for Plan Class selected as Group Benefit. For all other Plan Class, this section will not display on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

To apply Hawaii’s Prepaid Health Care Act 1.5% health insurance premium rate to selected benefit groups, use the Hawaii 1.5% Rule panel.

See Using the Hawaii 1.5% Rule for detailed information on how the system processes this calculation. This calculation is not available in Benefits Enrollment.

You can select the Exclude Plan When Calculating Medical Premium Limit option in the Special Options panel in Group Benefit Plans to exclude benefit plans from the Hawaii medical contribution calculation at the system-level.

To apply Hawaii’s Prepaid Health Care Act 1.5% rate to selected benefit groups:

  1. Open the Hawaii 1.5% Rule panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Benefit Group Each Benefit Group to which the Hawaii 1.5% rule applies. The Group Name displays.
HI 1.5% Rule Applies Whether to apply the Hawaii 1.5% rule to the selected benefit group, otherwise select No.

Defining Participation Requirements at the Client Level

To establish participation requirements ensuring that client and employee enrollments follow carrier guidelines at the client level, use the Participation Requirements panel.

To establish participation requirements criteria:

  1. Select a Participation Requirement Option:

  • No

  • Yes: Enables the Participation Requirement Start Date and Participation Requirement Percentage fields.

  • Use System Default: Uses the values defined at the system level. See Defining Participation Requirements at the System Level.

  1. In the Participation Requirement Start Date field, enter the date clients must meet the participation requirement.

  2. Enter a Participation Requirement Percentage. The value must be a number from 1 to 100.

Establishing Eligibility Criteria

To establish employment type and benefit eligibility requirements for Retirement, Flexible Spending, Employer Match, or HSA Match plans, use the Eligibility Criteria panel.

If you are setting up a flexible spending plan and select the Use Benefit Groups option, this panel does not display. You must set up eligibility criteria in the Eligibility by Benefit Group form, accessible in the Actions menu.

To establish eligibility criteria:

  1. Open the Eligibility Criteria panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Employment Status Class Each employment Status Class that is eligible for this benefit plan. If employees of all status classifications are eligible, you do not need to select any statuses.
Employment Type(s) The employment type or types that are eligible for this plan. If employees of all employment types are eligible, you do not need to select any types.
Minimum Age The minimum age required to be eligible for this plan.
Minimum Days/Months of Service The minimum days/months of service required to be eligible for this plan. Use the drop-down to select Days or Months.
Minimum Annual Hours The minimum annual hours of service required to be eligible for this plan.
Eligibility Days From Whether to count eligibility days from the Hire Date or Status Date for benefit rules calculation of the FSA/HSA Effective Date. - Hire Date: The employee’s original hire date. If the Eligibility Days From option is set to Hire Date, and the life event Source of Effective Date is set to Benefit Rules, the employee eligibility date is based on the original hire date plus any waiting period. - Status Date: The Life Event Date. If the Eligibility Days From option is set to Status Date, and the life event Source of Effective Date is set to Benefit Rules, the employee eligibility date is based on the original Life Event Date plus any waiting period. > Note: Note: If you select a Plan Class of either Retirement or Employer Match, then the Eligibility Days From field will remain disabled.
  • Hire Date: The employee’s original hire date.
  • Status Date: The Life Event Date. | Eligibility Date Used | The Eligibility Date Used determines how the system calculates the date employees meet eligibility requirements for this plan. - Calculated Eligibility Date: The first day of calculated eligibility. - First of Month after Calculated Date: The first of the month after the date of calculated eligibility. - First of Quarter after Calculated Date: The first day of the next quarter after the date of calculated eligibility. - First Semi-Annual after Calculated Date: The first of January or first of July after the date of calculated eligibility. - If Calculated is 1st of month, use that else next 1st of month: If the calculated date is the first of a month, the system uses that. If it is another day in the month, it uses the first of the following month. |
  • Calculated Eligibility Date: The first day of calculated eligibility.
  • First of Month after Calculated Date: The first of the month after the date of calculated eligibility.
  • First of Quarter after Calculated Date: The first day of the next quarter after the date of calculated eligibility.
  • First Semi-Annual after Calculated Date: The first of January or first of July after the date of calculated eligibility.
  • If Calculated is 1st of month, use that else next 1st of month: If the calculated date is the first of a month, the system uses that. If it is another day in the month, it uses the first of the following month. | Auto Enrollment | Whether to override the flag at the plan level. If you select this option, you must enter the Auto Enrollment Percent. This field is disabled if a retirement plan is configured with the Employee Deferral Deduction Code flagged to Prohibit Deductions on the Retirement Plans form. > Note: Note: The Auto Enroll option applies only to Retirement and Employer Match plans. | | Auto Enrollment Percent | If automatic enrollment is enabled, this is the deferral percentage at which employees will be automatically enrolled. If you enter a value which is NOT >=3 and <=10, and the Auto Escalator field below is checked then you will get a warning message stating Auto Enrollment Percent must be between 3%-10% when using Auto Escalator. This field is disabled if a retirement plan is configured with the Employee Deferral Deduction Code flagged to Prohibit Deductions on the Retirement Plans form. However, if there is any existing value for the prohibited retirement plan, then the value is displayed but the field remains disabled. > Note: Note: The Apply Enroll Percent option applies only to Retirement and Employer Match plans. | | Auto Escalator | This field only displays if you enable the Auto Enrollment field for a Retirement Plan. > Note: Note the following: - Unchecked (default): Plans will not automatically escalate contributions annually. - Checked: In addition to auto-enrollment at a default contribution rate, plans will automatically escalate contributions by 1% each year until they reach a predetermined rate by the employer (between 10 and 15%). > Note: Note: When you deselect the Auto Escalator field and save the form, then the system checks for any active retirement plan enrollment records that have the Auto Escalation? field enabled on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. Also, if there are any active retirement plan enrollment records a warning message displays, Auto escalator cannot be unchecked. There are employees using this auto escalator with active enrollments. Example: Employee Enrollment for Employee ID <Employee’s ID> and Effective Date <plan’s effective date>. |
  • Unchecked (default): Plans will not automatically escalate contributions annually.
  • Checked: In addition to auto-enrollment at a default contribution rate, plans will automatically escalate contributions by 1% each year until they reach a predetermined rate by the employer (between 10 and 15%). | Auto Escalator Max Percent | Enter any value between 10-15 (including up to two decimal places), which is the maximum predetermined benefit rate percentage decided by the employer for that client. Note: This field only displays if you enable Auto Enrollment. However, you can only edit the Auto Escalator Max Percent after enabling the Auto Escalator field. > Note: Note the following: - If you enable the Auto Escalator field, this field is mandatory. If you do not enter a value an error message displays, Auto Escalator Max Percent is required when using Auto Escalator. - If you enter a value outside the permitted range a warning message displays, Auto Escalator Max Percent must be between 10%-15% when using Auto Escalator. |
  • If you enable the Auto Escalator field, this field is mandatory. If you do not enter a value an error message displays, Auto Escalator Max Percent is required when using Auto Escalator.
  • If you enter a value outside the permitted range a warning message displays, Auto Escalator Max Percent must be between 10%-15% when using Auto Escalator. | Auto Escalate On | Defines when the auto escalation must occur at the client level. This field only displays if you enable Auto Escalator. This field has the following drop-down options: - –Select–: This option is automatically populated when you do not select any other options.(This option operates the same as Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default) option) - Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default): When this option is selected, then the calculated date for auto escalation should be the next Plan Anniversary Date which is equal to or greater than the Status Date (considered as Plan Anniversary date) assigned to the enrollment record (found on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form) plus 12 months. - Plan Anniversary: This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Retirement Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form. The plan enrollment uses the next Plan Anniversary Date as the calculated date for auto escalation. - Employee Enrollment Anniversary: This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Employee’s retirement enrollment plan. |
  • –Select–: This option is automatically populated when you do not select any other options.(This option operates the same as Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default) option)
  • Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default): When this option is selected, then the calculated date for auto escalation should be the next Plan Anniversary Date which is equal to or greater than the Status Date (considered as Plan Anniversary date) assigned to the enrollment record (found on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form) plus 12 months.
  • Plan Anniversary: This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Retirement Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form. The plan enrollment uses the next Plan Anniversary Date as the calculated date for auto escalation.
  • Employee Enrollment Anniversary: This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Employee’s retirement enrollment plan. ## Specifying Whether to Include Pay Codes

To indicate any pay codes that are a part of retirement earnings, use the Include/Exclude Pay Codes panel.

To indicate pay codes that are part of retirement earnings:

  1. Open the Include/Exclude Pay Codes panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option — To define this

Type — Whether the pay codes are Included or Excluded as part of retirement earnings. You can also leave this field blank (the default setting).

Pay Code — Each Pay Code to include or exclude from the retirement deferral calculations, as determined by the type. The Description displays. The pay code selected applies only if the employee deferral is a percentage.

Defining the HSA Contribution Amount and Frequency

To establish the amount and frequency of the Health Savings Account client contribution, use the Company HSA Contribution panel. This is displayed only after you select Plan Class as HSA Contribution.

To set up the HSA contribution amount and frequency:

  1. Open the Company HSA Contribution panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Contribution Calculation Method The Contribution Calculation Method to use, if any. You can select Standard, Tiered, Scheduled, or Fixed. The default is Standard. If you select Tiered, Scheduled, or Fixed, the appropriate HSA Contribution panel displays. Standard: - The HSA Contribution entered is an annual contribution, applied at the frequency specified in the HSA Contribution Frequency field. - Select the Display Employer Amount in Online Enrollment check box to display the employer contribution amount during benefit enrollments, allowing employees to view the amount their employer contributes to the plan. Tiered: - The Effective Date of the contribution line. - The high-deductible Benefit Plan ID. - The Plan Type (coverage tier). - The Percent of Tier amount to contribute. Scheduled: - The actual Pay Date on which to calculate the scheduled contribution amount. - Either the Lump-Sum Amount to be contributed on the specified pay date, or the Percent of Tier amount to contribute. Fixed: - The Effective Date of the contribution line. - The high-deductible Benefit Plan ID. - The Plan Type (coverage tier). - The Fixed Amount to contribute for the plan ID and plan type. - The amount of the One TimeContribution if appropriate. This option is available only if the Custom Feature Code ONE-TIME-HSA-MATCH is set in System Parameters. - Select the Display Employer Amount in Online Enrollment check box to display the employer contribution amount during benefit enrollments, allowing employees to view the amount their employer contributes to the plan. Dollar Match: - The configuration of HSA contribution calculation that matches one employer dollar for each employee dollar allocated to the HSA plan. - Selecting this option defaults the Contribution Applies To field to a read-only Contributing Employees Only option.
  • The HSA Contribution entered is an annual contribution, applied at the frequency specified in the HSA Contribution Frequency field.
  • Select the Display Employer Amount in Online Enrollment check box to display the employer contribution amount during benefit enrollments, allowing employees to view the amount their employer contributes to the plan.
  • The Effective Date of the contribution line.
  • The high-deductible Benefit Plan ID.
  • The Plan Type (coverage tier).
  • The Percent of Tier amount to contribute.
  • The actual Pay Date on which to calculate the scheduled contribution amount.
  • Either the Lump-Sum Amount to be contributed on the specified pay date, or the Percent of Tier amount to contribute.
  • The Effective Date of the contribution line.
  • The high-deductible Benefit Plan ID.
  • The Plan Type (coverage tier).
  • The Fixed Amount to contribute for the plan ID and plan type.
  • The amount of the One TimeContribution if appropriate. This option is available only if the Custom Feature Code ONE-TIME-HSA-MATCH is set in System Parameters.
  • Select the Display Employer Amount in Online Enrollment check box to display the employer contribution amount during benefit enrollments, allowing employees to view the amount their employer contributes to the plan.
  • The configuration of HSA contribution calculation that matches one employer dollar for each employee dollar allocated to the HSA plan.
  • Selecting this option defaults the Contribution Applies To field to a read-only Contributing Employees Only option. | Contribution Applies To | To which employees the contribution applies to. You can select Contributing Employees Only or All HDHP Employees. The default is Select which means no option is selected. - If you do not select any of the options, then any employee with an HSA account added to their Flex Spending Account setup under Elections for the current Plan Year will receive the employer contribution. - If you select Contributing Employees Only, then any employee with an HSA account added to their Flex Spending Account setup under Elections for the current Plan Year and contributing more than $0.00, will receive the employer contribution. - If you select All HDHP Employees, then the Account Type field is enabled. - Account Type: Select the Employee’s Employee Flexible Spending Account setup configured on the given plan’s FSA types. |
  • If you do not select any of the options, then any employee with an HSA account added to their Flex Spending Account setup under Elections for the current Plan Year will receive the employer contribution.
  • If you select Contributing Employees Only, then any employee with an HSA account added to their Flex Spending Account setup under Elections for the current Plan Year and contributing more than $0.00, will receive the employer contribution.
  • If you select All HDHP Employees, then the Account Type field is enabled.
  • Account Type: Select the Employee’s Employee Flexible Spending Account setup configured on the given plan’s FSA types. | HSA Contribution | The HSA Contribution amount that the client contributes for any employee with a Health Savings Account. (If a different amount is entered on an employee’s account, that value overrides this amount. | | HSA Contribution Frequency | The frequency of the HSA contribution. The system defaults to pay period. | | Maximum Contribution Amount | Here, you can enter the maximum HSA contribution amount in dollar. It is a conditional field and is displayed only when you select Contribution Calculation Method to Dollar Match. |

  1. Click Save to save the selected Plan ID record.

  2. Click Delete to delete the selected Plan ID.

  • You cannot delete a benefit plan using the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client as this will orphan the associated benefit rules and can cause payroll errors along with other issues. If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client, you will receive an error stating There are Benefit Rules assigned to this benefit plan. Please remove all rule references. You can only delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are no existing benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client or after you have removed all the benefit rules for that Plan ID for the client.

  • You cannot delete a benefit plan using the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA as this will orphan the associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records and can cause payroll errors along with other issues.

  • If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA, you will receive an error stating This plan cannot be deleted. There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with enrollment history. Example: Employee Enrollment for Employee ID [XXXXX] and Effective Date [XX/XX/XXXX].

  • If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Pending, Waived, or Eligible, you will receive a warning stating There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with an enrollment status of pending, waived and/or eligible. Do you wish to continue?

  • Click Yes to delete the selected Plan ID.

  • Click No to return to the Benefit Plan Setup form with the selected Plan ID and associated data populated.

  • You can only delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are no associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA.

  1. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time. All unsaved changes will be lost.

lrImporting Benefit Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Rates_Import.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Rates_Import.htm

lrImporting Benefit Rates

Use this Benefit Rates Import form to initiate a new import or complete an existing import in progress of benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You can also view completed benefit rates imports on this form. This benefit rates import process cannot be used to change or overwrite existing benefit rates.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, on the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits, click Benefit Imports & Reporting. Under Benefit Imports, click Benefit Rates Import.

[Image: screenshot]

You can also search for this form on the search box in the main navigation search bar.

[Image: screenshot]

This form has the following two sections:

  • Imports in Progress

  • Past Imports

Imports in Progress

When you access this form for the first time, all the tables will be blank and you should select the New Import button to proceed to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import screen to define and begin a new benefit rate import.

[Image: screenshot]

User – This field is a dropdown. By default, the user id of the user who has logged in will display here. You can also select a different user from the drop-down.

This section displays all benefit rate imports that are not completed successfully for the selected user. This section will display the last 7 imports in progress at a glance on-screen for the selected user. In case there are more than 7 imports in progress for the selected user, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the imports in progress for the selected user. The information is displayed in a table that has the following columns:

  1. Name – This is the import name that was provided for that benefit rate import. If you click one of the names, it will take you to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import screen for further action to complete the import.

  2. Type – This is the benefit rate type that you are importing for the import. This will be:

a. Premium Rates OR
b. Billing Rates
— —

  1. Plan Used for Template – This is the Benefit Plan ID used for the import template.

  2. Last Modified Date – This shows when this import was last worked upon.

  3. Last Modified User – This shows the user id of the user who worked on the import last.

  4. Status – This shows the status of the import in progress and can be any one of the following:

a. Template Defined – When an import has been defined but no import file is uploaded.
b. Ready for Import – When an import has been defined AND an import file is uploaded.
— —
  1. — Import Errors – When an import attempt has failed. This will produce a Benefit Rate Import Error Report
  1. Error Report – When the Status above is either Template Defined or Ready for Import, this column will display a ‘-’ [dash]. When the Status above is Import Errors, then this column will display a link to open and view the error report for the corresponding import that was not successful. It provides a list of all the errors that this import encountered. You can correct these errors and try again to complete the import. Following is a sample Benefit Rate Import Error Report.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Actions – If you want to delete an existing import in progress, you can click the recycle bin icon. Click yes to confirm deletion.

New Import – If you want to initiate a new Benefit Rates Import using a predefined benefit rates import template, click this button which will take you to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import screen. All the fields will be blank on that screen. You will need to fill in the necessary fields to set up and complete the import.

Past Imports

This section lists all the benefit rate imports completed successfully for the selected date range. By default, the date range is a calendar month ending on the current date. You can manually change the date range. This section will display the last 7 completed imports at a glance on-screen for the selected date range. In case there are more than 7 completed imports for the selected date range, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the completed imports for the selected date range.

Past Imports that are older than one year (since completion date) are automatically deleted and no longer display in the table.

The completed imports are sorted first by Date Completed and then by Name. The latest imports are listed at the top.

[Image: screenshot]

The information is displayed in a table that has the following columns:

  1. Name – This is the import name that you had provided for that benefit rate import.

  2. Type – This is the benefit rate type that you imported. This will be:

a. Premium Rates OR
b. Billing Rates
— —

  1. Plan Used for Template – This is the Benefit Plan ID used for the import template.

  2. Date Completed – This is the date when the benefit rate was imported into PrismHR.

  3. Processed by User – This is the user ID of the user who completed the benefit rate import.

  4. Import File – This is the benefit rates import file that was used for the import. Following is a sample import file used for Billing Rates plan type:

[Image: screenshot]

Billing Rates Age Banded

The following table provides at a glance the rate template for Age Banded Billing Rates.

Premium Rates Composite Rates
Group Benefit Plan Setup Rate Template (header) file & Import Fields
A benefit plan setup as follows: Insurance Class = Medical, Dental or Vision Family Rated Premiums = No Termination Date = [blank] OR Date > current date Rate Group for Premium Rates = No Tobacco Banded Rates = No Gender Banded Rates = No Spouse Gender Banded = No Wellness Banded Rates = No Age Banded Medical Rates = Yes Billing Rates Vary By Network = No 1. Benefit Plan ID 2. Rate Group 3. Plan Type 4. Effective Date 5. From Age 6. To Age 7. Total Bill Amount 8. Employee Bill Amount 9. Dependents Bill Amount
  1. Benefit Plan ID
  2. Rate Group
  3. Plan Type
  4. Effective Date
  5. From Age
  6. To Age
  7. Total Bill Amount
  8. Employee Bill Amount
  9. Dependents Bill Amount > Note: Note: You must have access to premium rates form to perform this action.

Please make a note of the following errors to avoid while preparing your import file using this template:

  1. For Plan ID

  1. — You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import.

  2. — If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import.

  3. — Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  4. — Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plans form are excluded.

  1. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Premium, Employee Premium]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.

  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file

  1. — does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.

  2. — is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.

  3. — is NOT in the list of benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.

  1. Multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:

  1. — If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.

  2. — Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0-19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.

  3. — The From Age and To Age fields in the import file must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.

  4. — The initial From Age in the import file must be 0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.

  1. If the Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .

  2. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.

  3. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.

  4. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file

  1. — has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
b. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  1. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount. If Employee Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:

  1. — Plan Type Coverage Class can be found in Group Benefit Plan Types in the Coverage Class field.

  2. — Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount.

  1. If Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .

  2. Dependent Bill Amount is a calculated amount based on Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount.

  1. — If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount.

  2. — If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

  3. — Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  1. The following are required values on the import. [Benefit Plan ID, Rate Group, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Bill Amount and Employee Bill Amount]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.

  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file:

  1. — does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.

  2. — is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.

a. Only one line of rates is allowed.

  1. — If import file is set up with more than one line for an effective date combo then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).

  2. — If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.

  3. — If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.

  1. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.

  2. If the rate on the import file has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.

  3. If the rate is negative on the import file, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.

  4. For Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, if Employee Premium is on the import file, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Else, you will receive an error message stating Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Refer to the Coverage Class field selection on the Group Benefit Plan Types form for details.

  5. If your import file has Dependent Premium > 0 for a Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, you will receive an error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .

  6. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Premium. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.

  7. If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type with coverage class is not selected as Single (employee) coverage, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, you will receive an error stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount.

Note: If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then the Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

  2. — If the Family Rate Premium field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premium. Not supported for Import.

  3. — Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  4. — Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premium Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plan form are excluded.

  1. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Rate Group (if applicable), Network ID (if applicable based on plan setup), Plan Type, Employee Gender (if applicable), Spouse Gender (if applicable), Effective Date, Non-Tobacco Premium, Tobacco Premium, Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) (if applicable), Dependents (Spouse Tobacco) (if applicable)]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.

  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file:

  1. — does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.

  2. — is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.

  3. — is NOT in the list of Benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.

  1. Age Banded Medical Rates
a. If Age Banded Medical Rates = No, then only one line of rate is allowed.

  1. — If the import file has more than one rate for the same Effective Date then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).

  2. — If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.

  3. — If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.

  1. — If Age Banded Medical Rates = Yes, then multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:

  2. — If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.

  1. — Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0-19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.

  2. — The From Age and To Age fields must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.

  3. — Initial From Age must be 0, otherwise the import will fail with an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.

  1. If the Plan Type on the import file

  1. — does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .

  2. — has a Coverage Class of Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefits Plan Types form, you will receive an error stating Spouse coverage is not allowed for Plan Type .

  1. The Rate Group on the import file:

  1. — must be an existing Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group does not exist.

  2. — must be an active Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form i.e. the field Inactive must be unchecked. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group is inactive.

  1. Network ID on the import must exist under the section Plan Networks on the Group Benefit Plan form. If not import line fails with error message stating Network ID does not exist on Plan ID .

  2. If the Employee Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Employee Gender is not found.

  3. If the Spouse Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Spouse Gender is not found.

  4. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.

  5. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Network ID (if applicable based on plan setup), Rate Group (if applicable), Plan Type, Employee Gender (if applicable), Spouse Gender (if applicable) and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.

  6. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file:

  1. — has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
b. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.

Tobacco rates have no calculations. Rates entered are what is used.

  1. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount. If Employee Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:

  2. — Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount.

  1. If Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .

  2. Dependent Bill Amount is a calculated amount based on Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount.

  1. — If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount.

  2. — If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

  1. — has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
b. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  1. Total Premium must equal Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium. If Employee Premium is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:

  1. — Plan Type Coverage Class can be found in Group Benefit Plan Types in the Coverage Class field.

  2. — Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium.

  1. If Dependent Premium > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .

  2. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.

  1. — If Dependent Premium is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Premium PLUS the Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.

  2. — If Dependent Premium is blank on the import file, then Dependent Premium will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Premium minus Employee Premium)

Please make a note of the following errors to avoid while preparing your import file using this template:

  1. For Plan ID

  1. — You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import.

  2. — If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import.

  3. — Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  4. — Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plan form are excluded.

  1. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Premium, Employee Premium]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.

  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file;

  1. — does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.

  2. — is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.

  3. — is NOT in the list of Benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.

  1. If the Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .

  2. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.

  3. Only one line of rates per Effective Date is allowed.

  1. — If import file is set up with more than one line of rates for an Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).

  2. — If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.

  3. — If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.

  1. If a rate on the import file;

  1. — has more than 2 decimals, you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.

  2. — is a negative value, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.

  1. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.

  2. If Employee Premium is on the import file, and the Plan Type has Single (employee) coverage selected in the Coverage Class field on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Else, you will receive an error message stating Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Refer to the Coverage Class field selection on the Group Benefit Plan Types form for details.

  3. If your import file has Dependent Premium > 0 for a Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, you will receive an error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .

  • Total Premium must equal Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.

  • If Dependent Premium is on the import file and Plan Type with coverage class is not selected as Single (employee) coverage, the Employee Premium PLUS the Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium. Otherwise, you will receive an error stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.

  • If Dependent Premium is blank on the import file, then the Dependent Premium will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Premium minus Employee Premium)

Please make a note of the following errors to avoid while preparing your import file using this template:

  1. For Plan ID

  1. — You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import.

  2. — If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import.

  3. — Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  4. — Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plans form are excluded.

  1. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Network ID (if applicable based on plan setup), Rate Group (if applicable), Plan Type, Employee Gender (if applicable), Spouse Gender (if applicable), Effective Date, Non-Tobacco Premium, Tobacco Premium, Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) (if applicable), Dependents (Spouse Tobacco) (if applicable)]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.

  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file

  1. — does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.

  2. — is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.

  3. — is NOT in the list of Benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.

  1. Age Banded Medical Rates
a. If Age Banded Medical Rates = No, then only one line of rate is allowed.

  1. — If the import file has more than one rate for the same Effective Date then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).

  2. — If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.

  3. — If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.

  1. — If Age Banded Medical Rates = Yes, then multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:

  2. — If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.

  1. — Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0-19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.

  2. — The From Age and To Age fields must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.

  3. — Initial From Age must be 0, otherwise the import will fail with an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.

  1. If the Network ID on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Networks on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error message stating Network ID does not exist on Plan ID .

  2. The Rate Group for this import must be:

  1. — an existing Rate Group on the Billing Rate Groups form. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group does not exist.

  2. — on the Billing Rate Groups form with the field Premium Rate Group checked, otherwise you will get an error message stating Rate Group is not a Premium Rate Group.

  3. — an active Rate Group on the Billing Rate Groups form i.e. the field Inactive must be unchecked. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group is inactive.

  1. If the Plan Type on the import file

  1. — does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .

  2. — has a Coverage Class of Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefits Plan Types form and the import file also has Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) OR Dependents (Spouse Tobacco), you will receive an error stating Dependent Premium is not allowed for an Employee Only Plan Type..

  1. If the Employee Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Employee Gender is not found.

  2. If the Spouse Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Spouse Gender is not found. Spouse gender is not applicable if the Plan Type being used is set up with a Coverage Class of Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefits Plan Types form. If spouse is included on import file for such a plan type, you will receive an error message stating Spouse Gender is not required for Plan Type .

  3. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.

  4. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Network ID (if applicable based on plan setup), Rate Group (if applicable), Plan Type, Employee Gender (if applicable), Spouse Gender (if applicable) and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.

  5. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file:

  1. — has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
b. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.

Tobacco rates have no calculations. Rates entered are what is used.

Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.

Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Rates_Import_Setup_and_File_Import.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Rates_Import_Setup_and_File_Import.htm

Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import

Use this Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import form to set up and import new benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You also need to use this form to complete existing Imports in Progress.

Note:

  • You can only access this form from the lrImporting Benefit Rates form. From the Benefit Rates Import form:

  • You can click the New Import button to come to this form, OR,

  • You can click the Name link of an existing Import in Progress to come to this form.

Using the New Import button

When you click the New Import button on the lrImporting Benefit Rates form, you come to this form. All fields on this form will be blank.

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Description
Import Name Give the import a unique name that does not already exist in PrismHR to identify it. - The name can have alpha-numeric characters but cannot contain special characters. - The import name cannot contain spaces. - Import names must contain at least 3 characters.

  • The name can have alpha-numeric characters but cannot contain special characters.

  • The import name cannot contain spaces.

  • Import names must contain at least 3 characters. | Which Rate are you Importing? | Select one of the following benefit rate types from the following: - Premium Rates OR - Billing Rates |

  • Premium Rates OR

  • Billing Rates | Plan ID | This link only becomes active after you select a benefit rate type above. This defines the import template for the rest of the procedure. You can enter the Plan ID manually or click the Plan ID link and select a plan as your template builder based on pre-defined defaults and selectable filters. > Note: Note: You cannot manually enter a Plan ID if the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage Entered Manually in the Group Benefit Plans form for that plan. Since these plans do not have rate tables, there are no rates that can be imported in Group Benefit Plans, and they cannot be supported in the Benefit Rate Import. These plans will not show up when you are using the Select Benefit Plan selector. | Please note that:

  • If you manually enter a Plan ID and try to save the form without entering a benefit rate type, an error message displays.

  • You can only select an active plan for the import.

  • If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is enabled, then you must exclude family rates plans from the import.

  • Only Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported.

  • Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plan form are excluded.

  • For Premium Rates import, the following is a sample selector which you can customize according to your needs:

[Image: screenshot]

  • For Billing Rates import, the following is a sample selector which you can customize according to your needs:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save to save your import template once you have provided a valid input for all the three required fields noted above. A line item is listed in the Imports in Progress section on the lrImporting Benefit Rates form. Upon save, the Import Name field and the rate type become read only. However, you can still edit the Plan ID field. A warning displays when you try to edit this field.

Please note that:

  • Import Names must contain at least 3 characters.

  • Rate type selection is required.

  • The Plan ID field cannot be blank.

What is the import template builder?

Based on the benefit plan that you enter in the Plan ID field, you can import numerous benefit plans that have the same setup.

Example: If the Plan ID has Age Banded Medical Rates and Rate Groups for Premium Rates, then a plan with only Age Banded Medical Rates WOULD NOT be included in a Premium Rate Table but WOULD be included in a Billing Rate Table, since Rate Groups for Premium Rates is not used for Billing Rates. If BOTH plans do not have any values checked, then these are considered to match.

If you enter an age banded medical plan, any medical, dental and vision plan that is age banded can be imported together. Please note that the benefit plans need to be an exact match. Using the prior example, it cannot be age banded and tobacco banded.

Once you save your import template, the following section displays a list of all plans that match the setup as the selected Plan ID. This table is a reference for all the different possible setups. In the example above, we have selected a medical plan that is age banded, so that column is populated below.

Note: Note: If you try to change the Plan ID at this point, the system displays a warning that this action may affect the plans that can be included in this import. If an import file has been uploaded, it will be removed. If you select Yes, then the Plan ID changes and the table of available plans that can be imported based on the plan selection also changes. This would affect what can be included in the import file.

  • The updated Plan ID is saved to the import definition template.

  • The table of available plans is updated based on the newly selected Plan ID.

  • The Premium and Billing Rate Template available via the links in the Import Template Builder is updated based on the new Plan ID.

  • If there is an import file already uploaded, the file is removed from the import.

  • Since this is a change to the import, the Imports in Progress table on the Benefit Rate Import form is updated with Last Modified User and Last Modified Date.

Obtaining, Editing, and Uploading the Billing Rates Template

In the example above, we are importing billing rates. In this case we would see a Billing Rates Template button.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click the Billing Rates Template button to get the template.

  • This is a .csv file that will be downloaded on your system.

  • The template containers headers depending upon the benefit rate type selected for import.

  • Headers are required for each field.

Prepare your import file by adding your import data to this template. For example, this template comes from our example for age banded medical plan:

[Image: screenshot]

These are all the fields required for this import. These headers will be unique to a particular type of import.

Note: If you are importing Premium Rates, then a Premium Rates Template button displays. The headers in the premium rates template are different from the billing rates template.

[Image: screenshot]

Once you click the Premium Rates Template button the .csv template file will be downloaded on your system. Following is a sample premium rates composite rates template:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Select File in the Upload Billing Rates section once you have created your import file.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Add Files in the Select files dialog box to select the relevant benefit rates import file for the import from your system.

[Image: screenshot]

PrismHR provides the following import templates based on the selected Benefit Plan ID. For each type of template the validations will vary and so will the error messages. Click on the template downloaded to see the validations required to create your import file.

  • Premium Rates Composite Rates

  • Billing Rates Composite Rates

  • Premium Rates Age Banded

  • Billing Rates Age Banded

  • Premium Rates Vary by Network

  • Billing Rates Vary by Network

  • Premium Rates Gender Banded

  • Billing Rates Gender Banded

  • Premium Rates Gender/Spouse Banded

  • Billing Rates Gender/Spouse Banded

  • Premium Rates Rate Groups

  • Premium Rates Tobacco Rates- Billing Rates Tobacco Rates

  • Premium Rates Wellness Rates

  • Billing Rates Wellness Rates

  • Billing Rates Vary By Network BOTH

  1. Click Start Upload once you have added your benefit rates import file for the import to upload it. Once the upload is complete click Close to close the dialog box.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. The file name displays in the Upload Billing Rates section.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: If you want to upload a different import file, click the recycle bin icon to delete the uploaded file.

  1. Click Import Rates to import the benefit rates into PrismHR. This button is not visible until the import file is uploaded. A job progress window displays the processing steps.
  1. — If the processing completes without errors, click Close to close the job progress window. When the import is successful, you return to the Benefit Rates Import form and receive a confirmation message. The import displays under the Past Imports section on the form.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. — If the processing completes with errors, click Close to close the job progress window. The Benefit Rate Import Error Report displays for the import, showing all the errors preventing a successful import. You can correct all the listed errors in your import file, delete the existing import file on the system, upload the corrected import file and continue.

Note: Note: Click Close to close this form at any time. If you close this form before successfully completing an import, then the import will be listed under the Imports in Progress section on the Benefit Rates Import form with the appropriate Status. You can click that import anytime to resume your import from where you left off.

Using the Name link under Imports in Progress

If the Status of the Import is:

  • Template Defined – Continue from Step 1 in the procedure above.

  • Ready for Import – Continue from Step 5 in the procedure above.

  • Import Errors – Make necessary corrections to your import file and continue from Step 1 in the procedure above.

To validate what was imported, go to the Group Benefit Plans form. Enter the Benefit Plan ID for which you had imported the rates. Select Actions and then select Premium Rates or Billing Rates whichever is applicable. Then complete the information on the form that matches what you imported.

Benefit Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Rules.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Rules.htm

Setting Up Employee Enrollment Conditions

Use the Benefit Rules form to establish the conditions that employees of a client must satisfy to enroll in a benefit plan.

Note: To quickly access the Benefit Rules Import form, select Import Benefit Rules. You can use procedures to create the benefit rules import file and to import benefit rules information into PrismHR from a tab-delimited text file.

You can also access benefit-related features and settings using the Actions menu:

  • Audit

  • Clone Another Rule: Creates Company Benefit Rules records with any benefits found on the company you select- Copy Rule to other Benefit Groups: Copies a benefit rule to another benefit group

Creating Benefit Rules

You can define the benefit plan using the Benefit Rules form.

To create the benefit plan rules:

  1. On the Work Centers menu, select Benefit Plan Maintenance, then Benefit Rules.

Calculating Life Insurance Coverage for Commissioned Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefit_Rules_Coverage_Commission.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefit_Rules_Coverage_Commission.htm

Calculating Life Insurance Coverage for Commissioned Employees

PrismHR has a process for automatically calculating life insurance coverage for employees who are paid on a commission basis or who have a zero pay rate. If the employee Pay Method is set to Commission or their Pay Rate is set to zero on the Pay tab of Employee Details, the system automatically calculates the life insurance coverage amount by extrapolating the year-to-date amounts paid in either the previous or current year. Otherwise, the calculation is based on the employee’s Annual Pay.

If the employee was paid during the previous year, the system uses the amount paid during that year to extrapolate the employee’s annual pay:

  • If the employee was employed during the entire previous year, the system uses the amount that was paid in that year for the annual pay amount and the life insurance coverage calculation is based on that amount.

  • If the employee was paid during only part of the year, the system uses that amount to extrapolate the amount that would have been paid over the course of the whole year, and then the system uses that amount for the annual pay. For example, if the employee was paid $25,000 during the last six months of the previous year, the calculated annual pay amount would be $50,000.

If the employee was not paid during the previous year, the amount paid year-to-date in the current year is used to calculate the annual pay. If the employee was paid $25,000 for the first six months of the year and that is the year-to-date amount, then the calculated annual pay amount is $50,000.

If the employee was not paid in the current or previous year, the calculated annual pay is zero.
