Storing an Employee’s Benefits Per Hour

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Benefits_Per_Hour.htm Path: BA/Topics/Benefits_Per_Hour.htm

Storing an Employee’s Benefits Per Hour

Use the Benefits Per Hour form to store the employee’s benefits per hour record using the memo class of pay codes.

Note: Note: The benefits per hour record created here has no impact on payroll, which continues to use the benefit per hour rate stored in the Employee Details form.

Note: Note: If you enter a Pay Code that is not a memo pay code the following warning displays: Pay code must have a pay class of memo.

To access this form and store an employee’s benefits per hour:

  1. Access the Employee Details form in the HR|Change menu.

  2. Enter or select an employee.

  3. Open the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and select Benefits Per Hour. The Benefits Per Hour form displays the selected employee’s ID in the Employee field.

  4. Enter or select the Pay Code. The Description displays.

  5. Set the Status as Active or Inactive.

  6. Enter the benefits per hour Amount.

  7. Click Save.

Setting Bond/EPLI Insurance Billing Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Billing_Rates_Bond_EPLI.htm Path: BA/Topics/Billing_Rates_Bond_EPLI.htm

Setting Bond/EPLI Insurance Billing Rates

To set the billing rates for a bond insurance or EPLI (employment practices liability insurance) group benefit plan, use the Billing Rates form.

To set billing rates for a bond insurance or EPLI group benefit plan:

  1. Start on the Group Benefit Plans form.

  2. Enter the ID of the plan you want to edit.

  3. In the Actions menu, click Billing Rates.

  4. Set the following parameters.

Use this option — To define this

Copy from Premium Rates — Age-range information from the Premium Rates record is copied for the benefit plan. An error displays if there is no corresponding premium rates record. The Effective Date must be entered in the Billing Rates form for the Copy from Premium Rates option to display.

Benefit Plan ID — A value that is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Rate Group — An option that displays when you select No or Both in the Billing Rates Vary By Network list in the Other Processing Parameters panel. The rates you enter apply only to this rate group. Your organization might charge different clients at different rates for the same benefit plan. PrismHR allows you to define these different rates using rate groups. You can use as many rate groups as needed; see Rate Groups.

Effective Date — The date when the rate goes into effect. Saving rates according to the effective date enables you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date. Saving rates according to the effective date allows you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates billing using the rates with the most recent effective date. For short- or long-term disability benefit plans, the effective dates indicate whether the rate is set to standard or extended precision. If you selected the LTD/STD Use Extended Precision Rates option in the main form, you can only choose an effective date with extended precision, otherwise you can only select a date with standard precision.

Rate/Hundred — The billing rate for bond insurance expressed as an amount per hundred dollars of employee earnings. The rate relates to the Cost Basis field in the Group Benefit Plan form. For example, if the cost basis is Monthly, the rate represents monthly billing rates.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Use this option — To define this

Copy from Premium Rates — Age-range information from the Premium Rates record is copied for the benefit plan. An error displays if there is no corresponding premium rates record. The Effective Date must be entered in the Billing Rates form for the Copy from Premium Rates option to display.

Benefit Plan ID — A value that is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Network ID — The Network field displays when Yes or Both is selected in the Billing Rates Vary By Network list in the Other Processing Parameters panel. > Note: Note: When a benefit plan is set up to use networks (for billing, premium or both) and a network is marked as Inactive, the inactive network now displays in the Network ID dropdown with ‘(Inactive)’ next to it. All inactive networks filter to the bottom of the list in the order that they appear on the networks grid. You cannot modify or add new rates for Inactive networks. However, you can view existing rates for Inactive networks. When an inactive network is selected, the table is disabled. The Save and Delete buttons are also disabled. A warning message displays stating The selected network is inactive. No modifications can be made. Click the OK button to acknowledge the message.

Plan Type — The list contains only the plan types defined for the group benefit plan.

Employee Gender: — The list displays only when Gender Banded Rates is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

Spouse Gender: — The gender of the employee’s spouse’s. The list displays only when Spouse Gender Banded Rates is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

Effective Date — The date when the rate goes into effect. Saving rates according to the effective date enables you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date.

Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) — Enter the cost associated with covering an employee’s non-tobacco using spouse for this plan type and age group.

  1. If the benefit plan is not set up as tobacco banded:

Use this option — To define this

Total Bill Amount — The total amount to bill to the client for the cost of this plan. The Total Bill Amount is the sum of the Employee Bill Amount and Dependents Bill Amount. When you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Bill Amount of 500 and an Employee Bill Amount of 300, the system populates Dependents Bill Amount with 200.

Employee Bill Amount — The amount to bill the employee for this plan.

Dependents Bill Amount — The amount to bill the depending for this plan.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter billing rates for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Use the Billing Rates form to enter the billing rates for a medical, dental, or vision group benefit plan that charges different rates by both rate group and network.

Different fields display in the form depending on whether the benefit plan is set up as tobacco banded by selecting Tobacco Banded Rates in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

To set health plan billing rates by rate group and network:

  1. Start on the Group Benefit Plans form.

  2. Enter the ID of the plan you want to edit.

  3. On the Actions menu, click Billing Rates.

  4. Set the following parameters.

Use this option — To define this

Copy from Premium Rates — Age-range information from the Premium Rates record is copied for the benefit plan. An error displays if there is no corresponding premium rates record. The Effective Date must be entered in the Billing Rates form for the Copy from Premium Rates option to display.

Benefit Plan ID — A value that is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Network ID — The Network option displays when Both is selected in the Billing Rates Vary By Network list in the Other Processing Parameters panel.

Rate Group — The Rate Group option displays when Both is selected in the Billing Rates Vary By Network list in the Other Processing Parameters panel.

Employee Gender — Displays only when Gender Banded Rates is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

Spouse Gender — The gender of the employee’s spouse. The list displays only when Spouse Gender Banded Rates is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

Effective Date — The date when the rate goes into effect. Saving rates according to the effective date enables you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date.

  1. Define each year of age. If you need to create an additional age row, click + or press Tab.

Use this option — To define this

From Age To Age — The starting age for each line and the upper age limit. Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields. For example, 0-99.

  1. If the benefit plan is set up as tobacco banded:

Use this option — To define this

Non-Tobacco Premium — The amount billed to the client for the plan type and age group for non-tobacco using employees.

Tobacco Premium — The amount billed to the client for the plan type and age group for tobacco using employees.

Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) — Enter the cost associated with covering an employee’s non-tobacco using spouse for this plan type and age group.

Dependents (Spouse Tobacco) — If covered, enter the cost associated with covering an employee’s tobacco using spouse for this plan type and age group.

  1. If the benefit plan is not set up as tobacco banded:

Use this option — To define this

Total Bill Amount — The total amount to bill to the client for the cost of this plan. The Total Bill Amount is the sum of the Employee Bill Amount and Dependents Bill Amount. When you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Bill Amount of 500 and an Employee Bill Amount of 300, the system populates Dependents Bill Amount with 200.

Employee Bill Amount — The amount to bill the employee for this plan.

Dependents Bill Amount — The amount to bill the depending for this plan.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter billing rates for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Setting Coverage Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/BR_Coverage_Rules.htm Path: BA/Topics/BR_Coverage_Rules.htm

Setting Coverage Rules

If the same insurance coverage amount or calculation method applies to each employee regardless of benefit groups or rules, you can define it in Group Benefit Plans. Otherwise, use the Coverage Rules panel in Benefit Rules to define the rules for life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability plans.

Define Life Insurance Coverage Rules

If you offer life insurance coverage for commission employees, see Calculating Life Insurance Coverage for Commissioned Employees.

To define life insurance coverage rules:

  1. On the Benefit Rules form, locate the Coverage Rules panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Multiplier Pay Basis The Multiplier Pay Basis to use when calculating insurance coverage. If you do not make a selection, the system defaults to annualized pay.
Pay Multiplier If the amount of insurance coverage is equal to an amount multiplied by the employee’s annual base pay, annual Pay Multiplier. Enter 0 if a flat amount applies. If the amount of insurance coverage increases depending upon the employee’s years of service, Pay Multipliers can be entered based on Years of Service.
Rounding Method The Rounding Method to use to round calculated numbers to a whole number. Leave this field blank if you do not want to round off the calculated value.
Round Before/After When to determine life insurance coverage: - Before: The system rounds up before multiplying. - After: The system rounds up after multiplying.
  • Before: The system rounds up before multiplying.
  • After: The system rounds up after multiplying. | Coverage Maximum | The Coverage Maximum allowed under this plan. | | Coverage Minimum | The Coverage Minimum allowed under this plan. | | Coverage Amount | The flat Coverage Amount. | | Add to Calculated Coverage | The flat amount to Add to Calculated Coverage. | | Years of Service | Years of Service as a full year value (for example, 1 for one year, 5 for five years). You cannot enter a fraction (for example 5.5 for five and a half years). If the amount of insurance coverage increases depending upon the employee’s years of service, Pay Multiplier can be based on Years of Service. |
  1. Click Save.

Defining Disability Coverage Rules

To establish the coverage rules for age-banded disability insurance plans, Use the Disability Coverage Rules panel (or the Disability Salary Band Rules panel for salary-banded disability insurance plans.

To define disability coverage rules:

  1. Locate the Disability Coverage Rules or Disability Salary Band Rules panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Percent of Base The Percent of Base pay that is insured. If the benefit is not based on a percentage of the base, the value is 0.
Rounding Method The method used to round calculated numbers to a whole number. If you do not want to round off the calculated value, select nothing.
Benefit Amount The Benefit Amount if the coverage is not calculated as a percentage of the base pay. If the coverage is calculated as a percentage of the base pay, the maximum coverage allowed.
Alternate Base Calculation The Alternate Base Calculation to use: - Average Last Calendar Year’s Earnings - Average Last Two Years’ Earnings - Average Prior Year Earnings
  • Average Last Calendar Year’s Earnings
  • Average Last Two Years’ Earnings
  • Average Prior Year Earnings | Maximum Coverage | The maximum insurance coverage amount or an amount based on Years of Service. | | From Annual Salary To Annual Salary | The salary range covered by the rule. | | Coverage | The Coverage amount for the rule. |
  1. Click Save.

Establishing Eligibility Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/BR_Eligibility_Rules.htm Path: BA/Topics/BR_Eligibility_Rules.htm

Establishing Eligibility Rules

To establish employee eligibility rules for this benefit, use the Eligibility Rules panel in Benefit Rules.

To establish employee eligibility rules:

  1. On the Benefit Rules form, locate the Eligibility Rules panel.

  2. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Employment Status Class Each Employment Status Class that is eligible for this benefit. The Description displays. If employees of all status classifications are eligible, you do not need to enter any statuses.
Minimum Age The Minimum Age required to be eligible for this benefit.
Maximum Age This field allows to set the Maximum Age value for eligibility in a given plan.
Minimum Days or Months Of Service Whether employees must meet Minimum Days or Months Of Service to be eligible for this benefit, and the number of days or months. For example: - An employee hired on 3/2/2026 whose eligibility date is set as the first of the month on or following sixty days is eligible for this benefit on 5/1/2026 because the sixty days requirement passes on 4/30/2026. - An employee hired on 3/2/2026 whose eligibility date is set as the first of the month on or following two months is eligible for this benefit on 6/1/2026 because the two months requirement passes on 5/2/2026.
  • An employee hired on 3/2/2026 whose eligibility date is set as the first of the month on or following sixty days is eligible for this benefit on 5/1/2026 because the sixty days requirement passes on 4/30/2026.
  • An employee hired on 3/2/2026 whose eligibility date is set as the first of the month on or following two months is eligible for this benefit on 6/1/2026 because the two months requirement passes on 5/2/2026. | Eligibility Days From | The day to use for calculating eligibility based on days of service: Hire Date or Status Date. - Hire Date - Eligibility is based on the employee’s latest hire date, regardless of the employee type at that time. - Status Date - Eligibility is based on the earliest date when the employee’s status was active, considering the employee type (for example, when the employee was also full- time). |
  • Hire Date - Eligibility is based on the employee’s latest hire date, regardless of the employee type at that time.
  • Status Date - Eligibility is based on the earliest date when the employee’s status was active, considering the employee type (for example, when the employee was also full- time). | Eligibility Date Used | The date used to determine how to calculate the date when employees meet eligibility requirements for this plan: - 1st of the Month After Calculated Date – An employee hired on 9/1/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 12/1/2026, the first of the month following two months. - If calculated date is the 1st of the month, use that, else next 1st of the month – An employee hired on 9/1/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 11/1/2026, the first of the month coinciding with or following two months. - Calculated Eligibility Date – An employee hired on 9/3/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 11/3/2026, following two months. |
  • 1st of the Month After Calculated Date – An employee hired on 9/1/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 12/1/2026, the first of the month following two months.
  • If calculated date is the 1st of the month, use that, else next 1st of the month – An employee hired on 9/1/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 11/1/2026, the first of the month coinciding with or following two months.
  • Calculated Eligibility Date – An employee hired on 9/3/2026 with a two-month waiting period is eligible for this benefit on 11/3/2026, following two months. | Employment Type | Each Employment Type that is eligible for this benefit. The Description displays. If employees of all employment types are eligible, you do not need to enter any types. | | Exempt/Non-Exempt | The employee FLSA status required to be eligible for this benefit, or nothing if employees of all statuses are eligible. | | Network Availability Stop Date | An expiration date for the network attached to the benefit. |
  1. Click Save.

Changing Benefit Plans for Multiple Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Benefit-Plan.htm Path: BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Benefit-Plan.htm

Changing Benefit Plans for Multiple Employees

To migrate or terminate benefit plans for multiple employees at one time, use the Bulk Change Benefit Plan form.

To change benefit plans for multiple employees:

  1. On the Client menu, select Client|Action > Bulk Change Benefit Plan. The Bulk Change Benefit Plan form displays.

  2. To improve the response time for loading results, you can filter the results with the following criteria:

  • Control Group

  • Clients

  • Benefit Plans

Click Continue. To load all results without filtering, do not select any criteria and click Continue. The load time is longer than normal.

Column — Description

Ctrl Group — A unique code describing the client control group. This value is defined on the Client Details form on the Benefits tab.

Client ID — The unique identifier for the client.

Client Name — The name of the client.

Employee ID — The unique identifier for the employee.

Employee Name — The name of the employee.

Benefit Group — The benefit group the employee is assigned.

Benefit Plan ID — A unique identifier for the benefit plan.

Benefit Plan Description — A brief description of the benefit plan.

Coverage Type — A unique code describing the benefit plan type. For example, FAM for family. This value is defined on the Group Benefit Plan Types form.

Enrollment Status — A unique code describing the enrollment status. For example, A for active. This value is defined on the Employee Statuses form.

  1. Using the checkmarks, hold the CTRL key and select multiple employees from the list. The employees must have the same coverage type.

  2. Complete the following:

Use this option… — To do this…

Migrate Benefit Plan — To migrate employee enrollments to another benefit plan. 1. Click Migrate Benefit Plan. The Migrate Benefit Plan dialog box displays. 2. In Benefit plan to migrate to, select the benefit plan to migrate the selected employees. 3. In Effective Date, select the date for the change to take effect. 4. Click Continue. To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Terminate Benefit Plan — To terminate employee enrollments from benefit plans. 1. Click Terminate Benefit Plan. The Terminate Benefit Plan dialog box displays. 2. In Termination Date, select the date for the employee enrollment to terminate. 3. (Optional) To increase performance of the process, select Suppress the normal calculation of benefits adjustments. to prevent the process from creating any benefit adjustments. 4. Click Continue. To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Performing Bulk Changes to Retirement Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Retirement-Plan.htm Path: BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Retirement-Plan.htm

Performing Bulk Changes to Retirement Plans

Use the Bulk Change Retirement Plan form to perform a bulk change to retirement plan enrollment records from one plan to another. This operation updates the Plan ID on each employee’s plan enrollment record. Associated retirement plan loan records and standard deduction records are also updated with the new plan ID and deduction codes. You can run this process for all companies or for a single company.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To perform a bulk retirement plan change for a group of employees:

  1. On the Back Office menu, select Operations|Action > Bulk Change Retirement Plan.
  2. Click From Retirement Plan to select the plan ID you want to change.
  3. Click To Retirement Plan to select the plan ID you want to switch to.
  4. Select a client (optional).
  5. Click Update.
  6. The system displays a pop-up window with a preview of the changes that is to be made by the program, including From code tp To Code for each deduction type, counts of clients, employees, and deduction records impacted, and errors expected from running the process.
  7. Click Yes to complete the update to all indicated records.
  8. Clicking No if you do not want to make update. You will be returned to the original screen without any changes.

Changing the Wellness Status for Multiple Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Wellness-Status.htm Path: BA/Topics/Bulk-Change-Wellness-Status.htm

Changing the Wellness Status for Multiple Employees

To manage the wellness status for multiple employees, use the Bulk Change Wellness Status form.

To open the Bulk Change Wellness Status form:

  1. In the Back Office menu, select Operations|Action > Bulk Change Wellness Status. The Bulk Change Wellness Status form displays.

  2. To improve the response time for loading results, you can filter the results with the following criteria:

  • Control Group

  • Clients

  • Plans

  • Qualify

Click Continue. To load all results without filtering, do not select any criteria and click Continue. The load time is longer than normal.

Column Description
Ctrl Group A unique code describing the client control group. This value is defined on the Client Details form on the Benefits tab.
Client ID The unique identifier for the client.
Client Name The name of the client.
EE ID The unique identifier for the employee.
EE Name The name of the employee.
Plan ID A unique identifier for the benefit plan.
Description A brief description of the benefit plan.
Hire Date The date the employee was hired. You can filter by date.
Enroll Status A unique code describing the enrollment status. For example, A for active. This value is defined on the Employee Statuses form.
Qualify The employee’s qualification status: - No Value - Qualifies - Does Not Qualify
  • No Value
  • Qualifies
  • Does Not Qualify ## Approving Assessments

On the Employee Details form Personal tab, approving assessments:

  • Changes the employee qualification status to Qualifies

  • Updates the completion date

  • Sets the effective date of the change

To approve employee assessments:

  1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list.

  2. Click Approve Assessments. The Approve Assessments dialog box displays.

  3. In Assessment Completion Date, select a date to mark the employee assessment complete.

  4. In Effective Date for Status Change, select a date for the employees’ enrollment in the wellness benefits plan to take effect. The effective date affects employee rates.

  5. Click Continue.

To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Declining Assessments

On the Employee Details form Personal tab, declining assessments:

  • Changes the employee qualification status to Does Not Qualify- Updates the completion date

  • Sets the effective date of the change

To decline employee assessments:

  1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list.

  2. Click Decline Assessments. The Decline Assessments dialog box displays.

  3. In Assessment Completion Date, select a date to mark the employee assessment complete.

  4. In Effective Date for Status Change, select a date for the employees’ enrollment in the wellness benefits plan to take effect. The effective date affects employee rates.

  5. Click Continue.

To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Resetting Assessments

In preparation for open enrollment, you must reset employee assessments every year. On the Employee Details form Personal tab, resetting assessments:

  • Resets the assessment completion date to blank

  • Updates the assessment due date based on the open enrollment date

To reset employee assessments:

  1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list.

  2. Click Reset Assessments. The Reset Assessments dialog box displays.

  3. In Enter the correlating OE effective date, select the open enrollment effective date.

  4. Click Continue.

To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Defining Cafeteria Plan Contributions

A cafeteria plan is an employee benefit plan that enables employees to choose from a variety of pretax benefits. A cafeteria plan can also be referred to as a flexible benefit plan or Section 125 plan.

To establish the contribution to an employee cafeteria plan, use the Cafeteria Plan Contribution form.

To establish the contribution to an employee cafeteria plan:

  1. In the Cafeteria Plan Contribution form, provide the following information:

Use this option — To define this

Effective Date — The date when the contribution amount goes into effect.

Contribution Amount — The flat Contribution Amount for this cafeteria benefit plan. The system allocates the company’s contribution automatically.

Benefit Group Cafeteria Plan Contributions — It is a read-only section that displays the Cafeteria Plan Contributions set on the Benefit Groups form.

Benefit Group — This link allows you to select available Benefit Groups. The Benefit Group displayed is default to the employee’s assigned Benefit Group as of today’s date.

  1. Click Save.

[Image: screenshot]

, then the system displays an error message.

Setting Up Client Benefits

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Client_Benefits.htm Path: BA/Topics/Client_Benefits.htm

Setting Up Client Benefits

Set up group benefits, workers’ compensation, and retirement plan information for clients with the Benefits tab in Client Details.

To access this form:

  1. Select Client.
  2. From Client|Change, select Client Details.
  3. Click the Benefits tab.

Establishing Employer Group Benefit Parameters

Set employer group benefit plan parameters with the Group Benefits panel.

Note: Note: If your organization uses Benefits Enrollment, the forms for flexible spending plans display in enrollments only if the plans are set up in Benefit Plan Setup and in the Benefits tab in Client Details.

  1. Complete these fields as required.
Use this option To define this
Section 125 Plan Select an existing 125 plan or type in a plan name.
HSA Plan Select an existing HSA plan or type in a plan name.
Maintains Own HDHP Select if the client maintains a high deductible health plan. This suppresses the system’s validation when setting up an employee HSA..
Eligible Benefits Determinant Select to make benefits available to an employee if the client makes different sets of benefits available to their employees based on department, division, location, or benefit group. The system checks what benefits employees are eligible for based on the determinant. The Eligible Benefits Determinant field should be set to appropriate restrict eligibility to access the Eligible Benefits sections on the corresponding forms.
Suppress Automatic Benefit Adjustment Select if the client does not want to automatically calculate benefit adjustments.
Control Group Client Acts as a master company for the control group, if any. Use control groups to aggregate data when there are multiple clients that are treated as related entities for Affordable Care Act (ACA) or retirement plan reporting purposes. As an example, if an employee works 20 hours at company A and 20 hours at company B, the system treats that employee as having worked 40 hours, for the purposes of the ACA, and reports that for both companies A and B.
Auto Create Open Enrollments Select to create employee web enrollment forms automatically.
Auto Post Open Enrollments Select to post employee web enrollment forms automatically.
Include Employer Cost in Employee Self-Service Select to Include Employer Cost in Employee Self-Service. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)
Employee Calculation Based On The calculation method (Per Period, Per Month, or System Default) to use for calculating employee costs during enrollments. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)
Disable Accelerated Catchup? Select one of the following options: - Unchecked - (Default) Catchup 60-63 option is available at the client level - Checked - Catchup 60-63 option is disabled at the client level - When disabled, the 60-63 Catch Up does not apply and functionality works as it did before. - When Catch Up Limit is applied at the system level on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form only, Vertex limits the sheltered amount based on IRS limits. - When Catch Up Limit is applied to the Retirement Plans form, under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section, the regular contribution overrides Vertex but not for Catch Up (can contribute higher for catchup but sheltered limited at 7500) - When limits are applied to the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, then the regular and catch up overrides the Vertex limits and use the employee enrollment limits for deferral and taxation.
  • Unchecked - (Default) Catchup 60-63 option is available at the client level
  • Checked - Catchup 60-63 option is disabled at the client level
  • When disabled, the 60-63 Catch Up does not apply and functionality works as it did before.
  • When Catch Up Limit is applied at the system level on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form only, Vertex limits the sheltered amount based on IRS limits.
  • When Catch Up Limit is applied to the Retirement Plans form, under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section, the regular contribution overrides Vertex but not for Catch Up (can contribute higher for catchup but sheltered limited at 7500)
  • When limits are applied to the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, then the regular and catch up overrides the Vertex limits and use the employee enrollment limits for deferral and taxation. | Benefit Rules Good Through Date | An expiration date for the benefit rules set up for the client. This setting is used in the New Hire Suspension Process; see Suspending Benefit Enrollments for more information on related settings. | | Allow Auto Enroll Suspension? | Select to suspend auto-enrollments when an employee is hired. | | Cobra Plan Client Sponsored | For compliance with the American Rescue Plan Act. Select if the COBRA benefit plan is sponsored by the client instead of the employer. | | Allow Edit Dependents in Enrollment Workflow? | Allows employees to make changes to their dependents during the Onboarding process and enrollment workflow. |
  1. Click Save.

Selecting a Retirement Plan

To specify a retirement plan for the client:

  1. Select one or more retirement plans that the client participates in from the Retirement Plans panel.

  2. (Optional) Enter the TPA Plan ID for each plan if retirement plan information is reported to a third-party administrator.

Note: Note: Start and end dates are displayed for a plan if these dates are configured in Benefit Plan Setup.

Setting Up ACA Reporting

Indicate whether a client is considered a large employer under Affordable Care Act (ACA) guidelines for each year with The ACA Reporting table. You can also set it so employees can access information in Employee Portal (EP).

To set up ACA reporting for each year:

  1. Locate the ACA Reporting grid, which contains rows for each ACA year.
  2. Create a new row for the current year, as needed.
  3. Complete these fields as required. | Use this option | To define this | | | — | — | — | | ACA Large Employer | Select if the client meets the IRS definition of a large employer for that year. (The system defaults to No if nothing is selected.) | | | Show in ESS | Select if employees are allowed to view their 1095-C information in Employee Portal (EP). (The system defaults to No if nothing is selected.) Note: You should do this for a reporting year when you have built the registers and confirmed that the information is complete. | | | 1095 Employer | Select the information to use in the Applicable Large Employer Member fields on Form 1095-C: - 1094c: Employer name and address from Form 1094‑C settings. - Employer Master: Employer name and address from Employer Details. | | | | • | 1094c: Employer name and address from Form 1094‑C settings. | | | • | Employer Master: Employer name and address from Employer Details. |
  4. Click Save.

Setting Up Workers’ Compensation Insurance

Set workers’ compensation insurance parameters with the Workers’ Compensation Insurance panel.

  1. Complete these fields as required.
Use this option To define this
Policy Select an existing policy or type in a workers’ compensation policy that covers the employees for a client.
Policy Effective Date Set a date for a client’s coverage.
Use Rate Templates Select to use table-based rate templates instead of the traditional method when calculating workers’ compensation.
1099 Contractors Covered Select if 1099 contractors are covered by the policy. Workers’ compensation calculates for 1099 employees as well as other employees.
Calculation Options Use this option to calculate workers’ compensation accruals from the following options: - Time Sheet Location Based - Resident State Based - When you select this option AND the “Remote Location” is checked in the Worksite Locations form, the employee is treated for WC purposes as the state of their resident geocode and not the WC state assigned to the worksite location. The employee override is not required if the worksite option is selected. > Note: Note: Use these options only if you understand how they impact calculations. For example, the Resident State Based option works only for employees who also have the Tax Geocode Override Option option set to Override Work Geocode with Resident Geocode on the Employee Details > Other tab. (See Tracking Other Employee Information) .
  • Time Sheet Location Based
  • Resident State Based - When you select this option AND the “Remote Location” is checked in the Worksite Locations form, the employee is treated for WC purposes as the state of their resident geocode and not the WC state assigned to the worksite location. The employee override is not required if the worksite option is selected. | Use Company/Mod Discount | Select to use W/C accrual modifiers when calculating workers’ compensation liability for the policy. This overrides the global values set for the policy. This only affects the modifier or discount used for the accrual (cost) calculation, not the client’s workers’ compensation billing modifier/discount if this is a PEO client company. | | Policy Sub ID | Use this option if the policy has a sub-ID or sub-policy identifier. This displays on the Client Details form and certain Benefits Enrollment functionality. No pricing or processing variations are allowed based on the sub-ID; it is merely a memo. |
  1. Click Save.

Maintaining Enrollment Eligibility Criteria

Filter employees who are not eligible for benefits enrollment from receiving enrollment notifications and access to online enrollments with the Benefits Enrollment Eligibility Criteria panel. Filters can also exclude ineligible employees from being included in the Client Enrollment Summary Report.

If fields are left blank, the system uses client benefit rules to create an enrollment. If fields are completed, the selected parameters override the system default settings.

Note: Note: If you override the system default settings, it is recommended to complete all fields in the panel. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Use this option — To define this

Elig Status Code — The employee status codes that are eligible for enrollment, such as A (Active), L (Leave of Absence), and so on. Required.

Elig Type Code — The employee type codes that are eligible for enrollment, such as FT (Full-Time), PT (Part‑Time), and so on. Required.

Minimum Age — The minimum age you want to apply to benefits enrollment eligibility.

Minimum Length of Service (Days) — The minimum number of days you want to apply to benefits enrollment eligibility. The value entered must in days (for example, “30” for thirty days).

  1. Click Save.

Establishing Client Ownership

Set up information about the client owners with the Client Ownership panel.

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Use this option — To define this

Contact ID — Select a Contact ID or type in an ID for each person associated with ownership of the client.

Owner Name — Enter the name of the owner

Owner — Select whether the contact is an owner (Yes or No).

Percent — Set the percentage of ownership that a contact has in a client.

Owner Group — (Optional): Select the group a contact belongs to. Use this only when more than one owner exists. For example, if two families own the company, enter “1” or “2” to indicate the family to which the contact belongs.

Owner Relation — Set this in conjunction with Owner Group to indicate the contact person’s relationship to the owner. For example, Child of Owner.

  1. Click Save.

Displaying the Client Benefits Overview

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Client_Benefits_Overview.htm Path: BA/Topics/Client_Benefits_Overview.htm

Displaying the Client Benefits Overview

To display the benefit plans that the client offers to its employees, use the Client Benefits Overview form.

  • Click the Plan ID to view the Benefit Plan Setup.

  • Click the Group/Rules date to view the Benefit Rules.

  • Enable the View rules that are not found to display the Group/Rules for which rules have not been set.

  • Enable the Include retirement only benefit groups field to filter Benefit Groups data that are flagged as Retirement only.

  • Enable the View benefit groups past stop all use on date field to filter and view the data of Benefit Groups past the Stop All Use On date.

  • Click Reload to refresh and pull the latest data.

  • Click Report to run a report on this form and export the data.

This form has the following columns:

  • Plan ID
  • Plan Description
  • HDHP Plan
  • Rate Group
  • Group/Rules
  • Template
  • Start Date
  • End Date
  • Section 125 Eligible
  • Deduction Code - If Section 125 Eligible column is flagged with Y value, then the Deduction Code for that record will be displayed as 125 Deduction Code. However, if Section 125 Eligible column is flagged with N value, then the normal Deduction Code for that record will be displayed.
  • Rebate Bill Code - The value displayed in the Rebate Bill Code column is based on the value displayed for 125 Deduction Code or Deduction Code. If Rebate Bill Code is not assigned for a record, then the system displays N/A.
  • Bill Code

Note: The form displays all the Primary Plan IDs in Bold format. Additionally, the form displays the Secondary Plan IDs in normal text format along with all the data for that Plan ID even when you click on a header to sort the data. The form displays the same format of Primary Plans in Bold and the Secondary Plans in normal text after you select the View plans past end date and the View rules that are not found checkboxes.

Note: The header toggle icon allows you to customize the on-form report by showing or hiding specific columns. Additionally, the Enable All button is available in the column selector. This option appears when one or more columns are deselected, allowing you to quickly restore the full view.

Viewing the Benefit Plan Setup

To view or edit the benefit setup plan:

  1. In the Benefit Plan Setup form, review the plan information and make changes if needed. See “Benefit Plan Setup” for details.

  2. Click Save.

Viewing Benefit Rules

To view or edit the benefit rules:

  1. In the Benefit Rules form, review the benefit rules and make changes if needed. See “Benefit Rules” for details.

  2. Click Save to save any changes.

Viewing Clients Assigned to a Benefit Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Clients%20Assigned%20To.htm Path: BA/Topics/Clients Assigned To.htm

Viewing Clients Assigned to a Benefit Plan

Use the Client Assigned To form to view the clients assigned to a benefit plan selected on the Group Benefit Plans form.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, first select a Benefit Plan ID on the Group Benefit Plans form. Then, on the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

, click Clients Assigned To.

[Image: screenshot]

This form displays the count of clients who have the selected benefit plan assigned to them in active status.

The Status drop-down has the following options:

  • Active – This is the default option. This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned and is active.

  • Terminated – This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned but is terminated.

  • Never Implemented – This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned but was never implemented.

  • All – This option shows a list of all clients having the selected plan assigned to them in any of the above three statuses.

The table includes the following columns. Click on a column header to sort the data accordingly. For example, if you click on Start Date, the data will be sorted based on the start date.

Column — Description

Client ID — The ID of the client assigned the selected plan. If you click Client ID, the Benefit Plan Setup form displays in a modal with the Benefit Plan ID pre-populated along with all corresponding setup information for that Plan and client.

Client Name — The name of the client is assigned the selected plan.

Start Date — The start date of the selected plan for the client.

Stop Date — The stop date of the selected plan for the client.

Status — The status of the selected plan for the client. A=Active; T=Terminated; N=Never Implemented.

Active Enrollments — The number of active enrollments for the selected plan for the client.

Click Report to run a report to view the exported data of the clients assigned to the relevant benefit plan ID. You can download this report into a XLS file on your system.

COBRA Participant Record

Field Name Description
Participant ID Click the Participant ID link and select the code or identifier from the Select Enrollee selector. The Select Enrollee selector contains the enrollee IDs for any participant who has an existing COBRA enrollee record. This section is read only and displays any billing transactions for the participant. This section shows the following fields in a table:

Field Name Description
Date The date the transaction occurred.
Type The type of recorded transaction (Adjustment, Payment, Fee).
Amount The amount of the transaction.
Subsidy Given to Enrollee Any subsidy credit the employee received for this transaction.
Subsidy Credited Back to Employer Any subsidy credit the employer received for this transaction.
Date Credit Taken The date the subsidy credit was taken.
Check Number The check number if it was entered during transaction posting.

It also shows the following amounts as applicable:

Field Name — Description

Balance Due — A calculated running total of all transactions that reflects any balance due from the participant.

Total Subsidized to Enroll — A calculated total of all subsidies the participant received.

Total Subsidies Credited Back to the Employer — A calculated total of all subsidies the employer received.

Partial Payments Pending Credit to Employer — Any partial payments pending credit to the employer.

COBRA Dates

Field Name Description
Date of Qualifying Event Enter the date of the event which qualified this person for COBRA benefit eligibility.
Administrator Notified Date This field is optional. This applies to ASO clients only. Enter the date the client notified the COBRA administrator of the qualifying event.
Benefits Expiration Date Enter the date this person’s benefits will expire if not continued under COBRA.
COBRA Coverage Period Starts This is the date when the COBRA continuation coverage period begins. The continuation coverage expiration date is calculated from this date.
COBRA Coverage Period Ends Enter the date that the COBRA coverage period will end. This is dependent on the number of months of coverage, based on the qualifying event.
Election Notice Due Date Enter the date the initial notification letter is due to be sent.
Election Notice Sent Date This field is optional. Enter the date the Election Notice for COBRA continuation coverage was sent to this enrollee.
Eligibility Cutoff Date This field is optional. Enter the date by which a decision to enroll must be made. After this date, COBRA benefit eligibility will no longer be active.
ARPA Notice This field is optional. This field applies to ARPA notices that were required in 2021. If checked, ARPA-style election notices will generate for individuals whose COBRA coverage start date falls within the assigned start and stop date. If unchecked, the qualifying event date will be used.
ARPA Election Notice Sent This field is optional. Enter the date when ARPA election notice was sent.
ARPA Extension Notice Sent This field is optional. Enter the date when ARPA extension notice was sent.
Continuation Coverage Accepted This field is optional, if the COBRA status is inactive. However, if the COBRA status is active, then this field is required. Enter the date that the participant elected to continue coverage under COBRA.
First Premium Due Date This field is optional. Enter the date the first premium is due from this beneficiary. This is normally forty-five days from the date the person elects COBRA continuation coverage.
First Premium Receipt Date This field is optional. Enter the date the first premium payment was received from the participant.
Termination Notice Printed This field is optional. Applies to terminated enrollees.
Certified Letter Reference Number This field is optional. Enter the reference number for the certified or registered initial notification letter sent to this person.
Certified Letter Status This field is optional. Select the status of the certified letter sent to this person from the following: - Signed - Returned

Enter the date the second notice was sent. | | Third Notification Due Date | This field is optional. Enter the date by which the third notification should be sent to the COBRA Beneficiary. | | Third Notification Sent Date | This field is optional. COBRA Processing Parameters

Use this form to set up all necessary information for COBRA processing. The information entered on this screen is used in a variety of COBRA processes including but not limited to:

  • Calculating dates on the participant record

  • Calculating invoice dates

  • Calculating COBRA notice dates

  • Calculating COBRA fees on the COBRA Benefit Enrollment record

  • Calculating COBRA costs

  • Printing capabilities

  • COBRA prompts in Prism when an employee is terminated

  • Qualifying events that are available in PrismHR

  • COBRA termination reasons

  • COBRA notice addresses

  • Subsidy amounts and dates

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Setup click COBRA Processing Parameters.

To set up the COBRA Processing Parameters:

  1. Complete the following COBRA Processing Parameters section:
Field Name Description
COBRA Election Eligibility Expiry days Enter the number of days from the later of the benefits expiration date / election notice date that COBRA benefits must be elected before COBRA Election eligibility expires. By default this displays 60.
Initial Premium Due days Enter the number of days from the COBRA enrollment date that first COBRA premium is due from the COBRA beneficiary. By default this displays 45.
COBRA Election Notice due days Enter the number of days from the COBRA qualifying event date that the Election Notice Form should be sent to the COBRA beneficiary. By default this displays 14.
COBRA Coverage Period Starts On Select one from the following drop-down: - Qualifying Event - Select this option to start the COBRA coverage period from the date of the COBRA qualifying event. - Loss of Group Benefit Coverage - This is the default option. Select this option to start the COBRA coverage period from the date when normal coverage is lost.
  • Qualifying Event - Select this option to start the COBRA coverage period from the date of the COBRA qualifying event.
  • Loss of Group Benefit Coverage - This is the default option. Select this option to start the COBRA coverage period from the date when normal coverage is lost. | Custom Notices: Notice 2 Process Name Notice 3 Process Name Notice 2 is due Notice 3 is due | If you provide custom notices, fill up the following, or else leave it blank: Enter the name of the process that creates notification number two. Enter the number of days from the (Select one from the following drop-down:) that the second notice should be sent to the COBRA beneficiary. - Qualifying Event Date - This is the default option - Benefits Expiration Date - Enrollment Date Enter the number of days from the (Select one from the following drop-down:) that the third notice should be sent to the COBRA beneficiary. - Qualifying Event Date - This is the default option. - Benefits Expiration Date - Enrollment Date |

  1. Complete the following COBRA Subsidy Set-up section: This section is optional. Use this section when you want to subsidize part of the COBRA continuation premiums paid by terminated employees.
Field Name Description
Start Date Enter the start date of the date range here. The subsidy will be applied to enrollees who had their COBRA qualifying event on or after this date. The default is the first date of the current year.
Stop Date If you enter a stop date, then enrollees created on or after that date will not be subsidized. Enrollees created before that date continue to be subsidized. The default is the last date of the current month.

Number of Subsidized Billing Cycles If you want to subsidize COBRA premiums for all enrollees for a fixed number of billing cycles, enter it here. The default value is 6.
Use Coverage Start For ARPA Election Notice End Date? This field is optional. By default this field is unchecked. This field applies to ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) election notices that were required in 2021. - If unchecked, the COBRA qualifying event date will be used. - If checked, ARPA election notices will generate for individuals whose COBRA coverage start date falls within the assigned start and stop date.
  • If unchecked, the COBRA qualifying event date will be used.

Uncheck the box if you want to set up this COBRA processing parameter otherwise. |

COBRA Dependent Participant Questions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/COBRA_Dependent_Participant_Questions.htm Path: BA/Topics/COBRA_Dependent_Participant_Questions.htm

COBRA Dependent Participant Questions

The COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form is used to gather the information needed to add or update a COBRA Participant record for one or more terminated dependents. The system determines the Qualifying Event Date and Coverage End Date shown on the form depending on for you depending on how the dependent is being terminated.

For example, if the terminated dependent was already covered under an existing Coverage Detail record and you are terminating dependent coverage by adding a new Coverage Detail record with a new Coverage Effective Date, the Qualifying Event Date is the same as the Coverage Effective Date and the Coverage End Date is set as the day before the Coverage Effective Date.

To complete the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form:

  1. Select the Qualifying Event. > Note: Note: If your access privileges allow, you can also edit the Social Security No. field. Updating the Social Security No. field on the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form also updates the Social Security Number field on the Employee Dependents form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Dependents).
  2. Click Save on the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form. A final confirmation message displays listing all dependents whose COBRA Participant records have been added or updated: [Image: COBRA Participant Record Update Confirmation Message]
  3. Click OK on the confirmation message. The Employee Benefits Enrollment record is saved and the COBRA Participant record is updated or added as applicable.

Setting Up Composite Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Comp_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm Path: BA/Topics/Comp_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm

Setting Up Composite Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

This section explains how to set up composite benefit plans for the medical, dental, and vision insurance classes at the system level in PrismHR. It is intended for users who have experience setting up benefit plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Only those settings for composite benefit plans are covered in this section. Some settings are used only in Benefits Enrollment, and are labeled accordingly. For more information about using Benefits Enrollment, refer to in-product help or to the Benefits Enrollment User Guide.

Copying a Rule to Another Benefit Group

Copying a Rule to Another Benefit Group

Use this option To define this

Copying Rates from Another Plan Type

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Copying_Rates_from_Other_Plan.htm Path: BA/Topics/Copying_Rates_from_Other_Plan.htm

Copying Rates from Another Plan Type

When premium rates are defined for a plan, you can copy those rates to another plan in the same year using the Premium Rates form. For example, you can copy the rates for the employee and spouse plan to the family plan.

To copy plan rates from another plan type:

  1. In the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] , click Audit and provide the following information:

  2. Select a Plan Type.

  3. Enter a new Effective Date. The Copy from another plan type link displays.

  4. Click Copy from another plan type. A pop-up window opens.

  5. Select the plan from which to copy the premium rates.

  6. Click Copy. The rates populate the table.

  7. Click OK to close the success message.

  8. Make any necessary edits.

  9. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  10. Enter the rates for another plan, either manually or by copying.

  11. Click Close when you are finished.

Creating Benefit Rule Templates

Use this form to create a benefit rule template that can then be assigned via Benefit Plan Setup. Use this template to calculate eligibility, coverage and employee contributions if there is no client or plan specific rule.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form:

  1. Click the Work Centers menu.

  2. Under Onboarding & Benefits, select Benefit Plan Maintenance.

  3. Under Group Benefit Plans (Global), select Benefit Rule Templates.

To create benefit rule templates:

  1. In Template ID, select one of the following options:

  • To create a new template, enter a name.

  • To edit an existing template, click the link and select a template code from the Select Benefit Rules Template list.

  1. In Eligibility Rules, specify the following information:
In this field Enter this
Employment Status Class Select the employee statuses associated with this benefit rules template: - Active - On leave - Terminated
  • Active
  • On leave
  • Terminated | Employment Type | Select the types of employment associated with this benefit rules template. | | Minimum Days of Service | The minimum days of service required to be eligible for this benefit. | | Minimum Age | The minimum age required to be eligible for this benefit. |
  1. In Contribution Rules, specify the following information:
In this field Enter this
Contribution rules amount made by Select Employee or Company.
Contribution Method The calculation method for contribution amounts: - Percentage – The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage. - Fixed – The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount. - Fixed EE, Percent DEP – The employee’s contribution towards the premium is a fixed amount, and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage. - Percent EE, Fixed DEP – The employee’s contribution towards the premium is calculated by percentage and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount.
  • Percentage – The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage.
  • Fixed – The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount.
  • Fixed EE, Percent DEP – The employee’s contribution towards the premium is a fixed amount, and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage.
  • Percent EE, Fixed DEP – The employee’s contribution towards the premium is calculated by percentage and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount. | Employee Contribution Amount | Using the Contribution Method, the total employee contribution per pay period. | | Dependent Contribution Amount | The amount of the dependent contribution. | | Exempt take on employees from minimum days of service requirement | If selected, exempts imported employees from the minimum service requirement. |
  1. In Group Life/Disability Insurance, specify the following information:

Life Insurance - In this field — Enter this

Pay Multiplier — If the amount of insurance coverage is equal to an amount multiplied by the employee’s annual base pay, annual pay multiplier. Enter 0 if a flat amount applies. If the amount of insurance coverage increases depending upon the employee’s years of service, Pay Multipliers can be entered based on Years of Service.

Coverage Maximum — The coverage maximum allowed under this plan.

Coverage Amount — The flat coverage amount.

Rounding Method — The rounding method to use to round calculated numbers to a whole number. Leave this field blank if you do not want to round off the calculated value.

Disability Insurance - In this field — Enter this

Percent of Base — The percent of base pay that is insured. If the benefit is not based on a percentage of the base, the value is 0.

Benefit Amount — The benefit amount if the coverage is not calculated as a percentage of the base pay. If the coverage is calculated as a percentage of the base pay, the maximum coverage allowed.

Rounding Method — The method used to round calculated numbers to a whole number. Leave this field blank if you do not want to round off the calculated value.

  1. Click Save.

  2. Click Yes to confirm.

Using a Default Benefit Plan Template

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Default_Benefit.htm Path: BA/Topics/Default_Benefit.htm

Using a Default Benefit Plan Template

To have PrismHR automatically generate the Benefit Plan Setup based on the Company Benefit Defaults templates, use the Default Benefit form. The default templates are maintained in the backend system.

  1. In the Benefit Plan Setup form, open the Actions menu and select Default Benefit. The system prompts you with a confirmation message.

  2. Click Yes to continue. PrismHR creates benefit plans for the client based on the appropriate template. It checks the Cost Center in Client Details.

  • If there is a cost center set for the client, the system uses the Company Benefit Defaults template for that cost center.

  • If there is no cost center, it uses the ALL template.

Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Eligible_ZIP_codes.htm Path: BA/Topics/Eligible_ZIP_codes.htm

Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes

To enter eligible locations by ZIP code, use the Eligible ZIP Codes form. Use this form only for benefit plans that are not set up to collect network information.

Note: Note: To access the Eligible ZIP Codes form, select Eligible Zip Codes on the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

in the Group Benefit Plans form.

Only employee home locations that match the ZIP codes entered on the plan are eligible for enrollment. If no ZIP codes are entered for the benefit plan, employees can enroll regardless of home location.

If the benefit plan is set up for networks (the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected) you must set up network ZIP codes in the Benefit Network Locations form; see Setting Benefit Network Locations.

Note: Note: To quickly access the Eligible ZIP Codes import template, select Import Eligible ZIP Codes. You can use the Eligible ZIP Codes import template to import eligible ZIP codes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To enter eligible locations by ZIP code:

  1. Open the Eligible ZIP Codes form.

  2. Enter the ZIP Codes to attach to the benefit plan. The City and State displays. You can also click Zip Code and select the ZIP Codes from the Select ZIP Codes selector that displays. On this selector, you can filter the ZIP Codes according to State by using the State drop-down filter.

  3. Click Save.

Updating ZIP Codes

To attach ZIP codes to a benefit plan, you must first enter them at the system level.

If you enter a ZIP code that is not in the system, an error message displays. You can correct this by entering the ZIP code in the Zip Codes form. When the ZIP code record is in the system, you can then attach it to the benefit plan; see Setting Up Zip Codes for more information.

Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Benefit_Overview.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Benefit_Overview.htm

Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans

Use the Employee Benefit Overview form to display a benefit summary for an employee.

To access this form and display an employee’s benefit overview:

  1. Click the HR menu.

  2. From HR|View, click Employee Benefit Overview. The form opens.

  3. Enter an Employee ID or click the link and select an ID from the modal. General information such as the pay period and employee type displays, along with an overview table that provides plan details. The details that display are:

Field — Description

Age — Displays the employee’s current age.

Hire Date — Records the date the employee joined the organization.

Status — Identifies the employee’s current employment status.

Employee Type — Specifies the employee’s work classification.

Benefit Group — Displays the employee assigned to a benefits eligibility group.

Pay Period — Displays how often the organization pays the employee.

FLSA Exempt — Indicates whether the employee qualifies for exemption from overtime requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA). Note: The FLSA Exempt field does not display any value if you do not select an Employee ID or click the Cancel button.

Marital Status — Records the employee’s marital status.

Dependents — Displays the number of dependents associated with the employee.

  1. Review the plan information in the Employee Benefit Overview table:

Field — Description

Plan ID — The plan ID in which the employee is enrolled. Click a Plan ID to open the Employee Benefit Details form, which summarizes benefit plan details such as plan type code, lists employee dependents, and displays the coverage and billing history.

Plan Name — Name of the benefit plan, such as 120 Medical.

Status — Status for an employee with respect to the plan. Options are Eligible, Terminated, and Waived.

Pre Tax — When checked, this indicates that deductions are taken out pre-tax for this employee.

HDHP Plan — Indicates whether or not a plan is an HDHP plan.

Coverage Level — Indicates who the plan covers, such as Employee or Family. An amount of coverage can also be listed, which is the cap on coverage for this employee. It displays the Type Code for any benefit plan that uses the group benefit plan types. It displays the Benefit Plan Type when you hover on the text. For example, if there is a benefit plan using the Group Benefit Plan Types, then the hover text displays the Type Code and Type Description (FAM - FAMILY). Similarly, for other benefit plans, the hover text displays the Coverage Amount (25,000.00).

Coverage Start — Date that benefit coverage starts.

Deduction Start — Date that benefit deductions start.

Coverage End — Date that benefit coverage ends.

Deduction End — Date that benefit deductions stop.

Pending Ben Adj — Displays the pending benefit adjustments count. Note: If the column has a value greater than 0, then a hyperlink is available. Click the count hyperlink to open the Benefit Adjustments modal form with the selected Benefit Plan prepopulated in the Filter By Plan field.

Employee Contribution — Dollar amount that an employee contributes for benefits.

Employer Contribution — Dollar amount that an employer contributes for benefits.

Note: The header toggle icon allows you to customize the on-form report by showing or hiding specific columns. Additionally, the Enable All button is available in the column selector. This option appears when one or more columns are deselected, allowing you to quickly restore the full view.

  1. Review the plan’s scheduled deductions, arrears, and outstanding benefit adjustments for an employee’s benefits by expanding the Outstanding Billing section:
  • Recurring Deduction: This grid displays the same information available on the Recurring Deductions form. Click this link to open the Recurring Deductions modal form. On the modal form that displays, the Employee ID and the Cancel button is disabled.

Please note the following:

  • If no data is available for the employee, then the Recurring Deductions grid displays a message stating: There are no existing Recurring Deduction records.

  • Clicking Save on the modal form saves the data.

  • Click Close to return to the main form.

  • Benefits Adjustments: This grid displays the list of outstanding benefit adjustments available on the Benefit Adjustments form. Click this link to open the Benefits Adjustments modal form.

Please note the following:

  • If no data is available for the employee, then the Benefit Adjustments grid displays a message stating, There are no existing billing adjustment records.

  • Unlike on the main Benefit Adjustments form, the Employee Benefit Overview option available under the Actions menu is not displayed on the Benefit Adjustments modal form.

  • The Employee ID and the Cancel button are disabled on the modal form.

  • You can add and save new adjustment from the modal form.

  • Click Close to return to the main form.

  • Deduction Arrears: It is a hyperlink. This grid displays the same information available on the Employee Deduction Arrears form. Click this link to open the Employee Deduction Arrears modal form.

Please note the following:

  • If no data is available for the employee, then the Deduction Arrears grid displays a message stating, There are no existing arrears records.

  • The Employee ID and the Cancel button is disabled on the modal form.

  • Clicking Save on the modal form saves the data after you confirm.

  • Click Close to return to the main form.

  1. View the billing history for a specific employee/plan along with the ability to select custom date range to review billing history by expanding the Billing History section:

  • Under the Selection Parameters section, the Defined Ranges drop-down field is available for you to select from a list of pre-defined date ranges or enter your own date range to review billing history.

  • The Defined Ranges drop-down contains the following options:

  • Current Month (default) – The date range is displayed as the first day of current month and the last day of current month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 6/1/2024-6/30/2024.

  • Prior Month – The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous month and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 5/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 2 Months – The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 3 Months – The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous three months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 3/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Custom Date Range – You can choose dates in the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before fields.

Note: This Pay Date range for this drop-down option is limited to 6 months. If the date range entered is longer than 6 months, then a warning message displays.

  • Select Batch ID – You can select the Payroll Number.

Note: When you select Select Batch ID option from the drop-down, then a Payroll Voucher field, which is a hyperlink appears where you can select a payroll number from the Select Payroll Number selector that displays. You can also type in the payroll number in the Payroll Number field. If you enter a payroll number that does not match with the data set available on the Select Payroll Number selector, then an error is displayed stating, is not a valid payroll number for this action.

  • Click the Benefit Plan ID link if you want to select specific benefit plans for inclusion in the displayed data.

  • Click Download Report button to open the report results window for the Benefit Billing Detail Report with existing parameters from the Billing History fields. The report displays the Offer Type indicator to the right of the Plan ID.

Note: The Download Report button is disabled when there are no results for a defined date range.

The following graphic illustrates the employee contributions chart. The legend displays an alphabetical list of plan names. Click the up and down arrows to view different pages in the legend.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Benefits_Enrollment.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Benefits_Enrollment.htm

Manually Enrolling an Employee in a Benefit Plan

To manually enroll an employee in a benefit plan, use the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

Note: Note: If the employee qualifies for COBRA benefits, the system prompts you to specify whether you want to maintain the COBRA benefits. Click No if you want to edit non-COBRA benefits. Click Yes to edit the COBRA benefit information. The form is very similar to this one; see Enrolling a COBRA Participant to learn about COBRA enrollees.

You can access detailed information about the employee’s benefits using the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

:

  • Benefit Detail Audit: See Viewing the Audit Log

  • Benefit Overview: See Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans

  • Benefits Adjustment: See Changing an Employee’s Benefit Billing Record.

  • CAFE Contribution: See Defining Cafeteria Plan Contributions.

  • Dependents: See Maintaining Employee Dependents- Employee Details: See Maintaining Employee Details

  • Employee Flexible Spending Accounts: See Enrolling Employees in Flexible Spending Accounts.

  • Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry: See Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry.

  • Enrollment Audit: See Displaying Enrollment History.

  • History: See Displaying Employee Benefit History

  • Retirement Plan Enrollment: See Retirement Plan Enrollment.

  • Rule Override: See Overriding a Client’s Eligibility Rules

  • User Fields: See Entering Information for Custom Fields.

Maintaining Basic Enrollment Information

To maintain the basic information for the employee and the plan, use the Benefits Enrollment panel.

Note: Note: Click Switch to COBRA Mode to view the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) version of this form.

To maintain the basic information:

  1. Open the Benefits Enrollment panel.

Additionally, when a rule for Maximum Age is defined on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form for a given Employee ID and Plan ID, the override rule takes precedence over any existing client rule for the field.

Establishing Coverage Details

To establish the amount of coverage, premium rates, and other information, use the Coverage Detail panel.

To establish coverage details:

  1. Open the Coverage Detail panel.
