Please note the following:

  • Other panels can display, based on the Benefit Plan. Refer to the relevant panel descriptions.

  • While creating an Employee Benefits Enrollment Detail record for an employee configured with Life Insurance plan for Spouse Age Reduction set as Use Employee Schedule, the system considers the following:

  • The system displays both the Spouse Coverage Basis and the reduced Spouse Coverage Amount in the Coverage Details section of the Employee Benefit Enrollment form.

  • If spouse coverage amount is entered then the Spouse Coverage Basis must be set equal to Spouse Coverage Amount.

  • If the spouse does not meet an age threshold for the reduction schedule and a Spousal Coverage Amount is entered, the Spouse Coverage Amount is stored as the initial coverage amount.

  • If the spouse meets age threshold for the reduction schedule and a Spousal Coverage Amount is entered, then:

  • the Spouse Coverage Basis is calculated to reflect the age reduction for the spouse’s age. For example, if spouse is 65 years and reduction to 80% is applied at 65, then for an election of $100,000, the calculated Coverage Basis is $125,000.

  • if an amount is entered that results in the coverage basis exceeding the Spouse Life Coverage End Amount then an error message is displayed.

  • While using the Benefits Import tool to import new Benefit Detail Record for Voluntary Life elections, if the Spouse Coverage Amount is imported and the spouse is at or above the first reduction age, then the Coverage Basis is calculated to reflect the appropriate reduction as defined on the plan setup.

  • If a plan is configured with Employee DOB for Spouse Life field enabled on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the above scenarios should use employee age instead of the Spouse age.

  • Similarly, the system considers the above scenarios while creating an Employee Benefits Enrollment Detail record for an employee configured with Life Insurance plan for Spouse Age Reduction set as Separate Spouse Schedule.

When a spouse covered under an employee life plan crosses a configured Dependent Spouse Age Reduction threshold, then during the payroll process, the system automatically creates a new Life Insurance benefit detail record with the correct Effective Date and reduced coverage amount, using the existing employee age-reduction logic.

Please note the following:

  • The above logic applies when spouse age is calculated from spouse Date of Birth (DOB) or, when configured, from the employee DOB, and continues to respect plans where Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is set to No under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the Group Benefit Plans form.
  • The Voluntary Life premium calculations now follows the logic that when a plan is configured to ReduceCoverage and Premium and Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is enabled with either Use Employee Schedule or Separate Spouse Schedule under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the spouse premiums are reduced in line with the spouse coverage reduction for manual enrollments.
  • Similarly, the Voluntary Life premium calculations include that when a plan is configured with ReduceCoverage and Premium and Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is enabled with either Use Employee Schedule or Separate Spouse Schedule under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the spouse premiums are reduced in line with the spouse coverage amount. Please note that when ReduceCoverage and Premium is not selected, then the spouse premiums remain unreduced even when a spouse age reduction schedule is configured.

Establishing Billing History

To establish and view the billing history for a specific employee/plan along with the ability to select custom date range to review billing history, expand the Billing History section.

  1. Expand the Billing History section. Under this section you can perform the following actions:

Under the Selection Parameters section, the Defined Ranges drop-down field is available for you to select from a list of pre-defined date ranges or enter your own date range to review billing history.

The Defined Ranges drop-down contains the following options:

  • Current Month (default)- The date range is displayed as the first day of current month and the last day of current month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 6/1/2024-6/30/2024.

  • Year-to-date- The date range is displayed as the first day of the current year till the current system date. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition displayed on this selection will be 1/1/2024-6/15/2024.

  • Prior Month- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous month and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 5/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 2 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 3 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous three months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 3/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior Year- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous year and the last day of the previous year. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 1/1/2023-12/31/2023.

  • Custom Date Range- You can choose dates in the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before fields.

  • When you select Custom Date Range option from the drop-down, two fields, Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before appears where you can specify a date range other than the one listed above and successfully generate accurate report results.

Note: This Pay Date range for this drop-down option is limited to 6 months. If the date range entered is longer than 6 months, then a warning message stating, Pay Date range is limited to 6 months. Please select a Pay Date which is greater than or equal to . is displayed.

  • Select Batch ID- You can select the Payroll Number.

Note: When you select Select Batch ID option from the drop-down, then a Payroll Voucher field, which is a hyperlink appears where you can select a payroll number from the Select Payroll Number selector that displays. You can also type in the payroll number in the Payroll Number field. If you enter a payroll number that does not match with the data set available on the Select Payroll Number selector, then an error is displayed stating, is not a valid payroll number for this action.

  1. Click Download Report button to open the report results window for the Benefit Billing Detail Report with existing parameters from the Billing History fields. The report displays the Offer Type indicator to the right of the Plan ID.

Note: The Download Report button is disabled when there are no results for a defined date range.

Specifying Whether a Rate Guaranty Applies

For life insurance plans, the system displays the rate guaranty for specific date ranges, if it applies to the plan.

  • The Rate Guaranty Start Date is the start of the guaranty period, and is the date used for Age and Rate. If the plan is an ongoing 5-year guaranty plan, ensure the list includes as many 5-year periods that can possibly apply. Once the employee is out of guaranty periods, the system resumes using the current date for all transactions.

  • After the final Rate Guaranty End Date passes, the system uses the current Age and Rate for any future calculations.

Displaying Group-Term-Life Taxable Earnings

For life insurance plans, the system displays the group-term taxable earnings for the employee, if applicable.

  • The Benefit Start Date for YTD GTL Taxable is the start date for the employee’s group-term life taxable earnings.

  • The Tax Year displays the year in which taxable benefits accrued against this plan.

  • The Taxable Benefit Accrued displays the amount of taxable benefits that accrued against this plan.

Enrolling a COBRA Participant

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Cobra_Benefits_Enrollment.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Cobra_Benefits_Enrollment.htm

Enrolling a COBRA Participant

To enroll a Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) participant in a benefit plan, use the Employee Benefits Enrollment (COBRA) form. Access this form by clicking Switch to Cobra Mode at the top of the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. With the exception of a few field labels, this is the same as the usual benefit enrollment form. see Manually Enrolling an Employee in a Benefit Plan for panel and field descriptions.

COBRA enrollees are:

  • A terminated employee

  • An employee who no longer has benefits through the company (for example, they dropped from full-time to part-time)

  • A dependent of an employee

Note: Note: Click Switch to Employee Mode to view the non-COBRA version of this form.

To establish the amount of coverage, premium rates, and other information, use the Coverage Detail panel.

Defining Coverage Details

To define the coverage details:

  1. On the Employee Benefits Enrollment (COBRA) form, go to Coverage Detail panel.

Use this option — To define this

Existing Effective Date — The date on which the selected plan becomes effective. If this is a new enrollment record, enter the same date as the Coverage Starts date.

Plan Type — The benefit plan type.

Updated Carrier — Whether the insurance carrier has been notified of any coverage changes.

  1. Click Save.

Maintaining COBRA Participant Enrollment

This section covers COBRA Participant Enrollment maintenance and includes steps for performing actions such as terminating dependent coverage.

Terminating COBRA Dependent Coverage

There are multiple methods for terminating COBRA dependent coverage depending on your practices AND depending on the circumstances under which dependent coverage is terminated. Some of the methods include:

  • Entering a Coverage End Date on the associated Coverage Detail record.
  • Adding a new Coverage Detail record for an existing COBRA participant with the same Coverage Effective Date/ Qualifying Event Date.
  • Adding a new Coverage Detail record for an existing COBRA participant with a new Coverage Effective Date/Qualifying Event Date.
  • Adding a new Coverage Detail record for a new COBRA participant (where the dependent was previously covered under an employer plan but NOT as a COBRA participant.)

The method you choose can determine the way important dates (such as Qualifying Event Date, Coverage Effective Date, and Coverage End Date) are recorded in the system. For more details on how dates are derived and recorded based on the termination method used, see the “How Dates Are Determined When Terminating Dependent Coverage” section of this topic.

To terminate COBRA dependent coverage:

  1. On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form in the Coverage Detail panel, add a new Coverage Detail record (recommended) or update the Coverage End Date of an existing Coverage Detail record and then click Save on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. > Note: Note: You do not need to switch to COBRA view to perform these steps. In our example, we are adding a new Coverage Detail record where the dependent already has an existing COBRA participant record. We have clicked Enter New Date to add a different Coverage Effective Date, and we have changed the Plan type from EMPLOYEE + CHILD to EMPLOYEE as we are terminating dependent coverage for the child: [Image: Terminating a COBRA Dependent By Adding a New Coverage Detail Record] Then, in the “Covered Dependents” section, we removed the child dependent and clicked Save. [Image: Remove Dependent and Click Save] The following message displays: [Image: Terminate COBRA Dependent Message - Existing COBRA Participant Record on File] > Note: Note: The message verbiage varies slightly depending on whether the terminated dependent has an existing COBRA Participant record. As previously mentioned, message dates may also vary depending on the termination method used. Here is an example of the message you receive when the dependent is not an existing COBRA Participant. [Image: Terminate COBRA Dependent Message - No Existing COBRA Participant Record] Additionally, if you are terminating multiple dependents, the message repeats for each dependent which allows you to specify for each dependent whether to simply terminate their coverage by selecting No or whether to terminate the existing coverage but then also promote new or updated coverage details to a new or updated COBRA Participant record by selecting Yes.
  2. What do you want to do?
  • Select Yes if you want to add the new coverage details to a COBRA Participant record. This is the option you select when you are terminating dependent coverage in order to establish new or update coverage details.
  • Select No if you do not want to include the plan under new effective dates. This is the option you select when you want to terminate coverage completely without promoting any new or updated coverage details to a new or updated COBRA Participant record. The existing COBRA Participant record is updated to reflect the Coverage End Date only.
  1. If you select Yes:
  • The COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form displays as shown in the image below: [Image: COBRA Dependent Participant Question] The system determines the Qualifying Event Date and Coverage End Date for you depending on the scenario. In our example, the terminated dependent was already covered under an existing Coverage Detail record. A new Coverage detail record with a new Coverage Effective Date was added. Therefore, in our example above, the Qualifying Event Date is the same as the Coverage Effective Date we entered, and the Coverage End Date is set as the day before the Coverage Effective Date.
  • Select the Qualifying Event. > Note: Note: If your access privileges allow, you can also edit the Social Security No. field. Updating the Social Security No. field on the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form also updates the Social Security Number field on the Employee Dependents form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Dependents).
  • Click Save on the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form. A final confirmation message displays listing all dependents whose COBRA Participant records have been added or updated: [Image: COBRA Participant Record Update Confirmation Message]
  • Click OK on the confirmation message.
  • The Employee Benefits Enrollment record is saved and the COBRA Participant record is updated or added with the Coverage Effective Date, Qualifying Event, Qualifying Event Date and Coverage End Date. > Note: Note: In our example scenario, a new COBRA Participant Record is added because the new Coverage Detail record Effective Date/ Qualifying Event Date is different on the previous Coverage Detail record. If we had added new Coverage Details using the same Coverage Effective Date/Qualifying Event Date, the existing COBRA Participant record associated with these coverage details would have been updated. If you select No: The Employee Benefits Enrollment record is saved. The process of terminating the dependent is complete with no further action required. The prior Coverage Detail record that included the terminated dependent(s) is updated with the Coverage End Date. The Coverage End Date is the day before the new Coverage Detail record effective date and is displayed in the Coverage End Date column of the “Covered Dependents” section on the Employee Benefits Enrollment record.

How Dates Are Determined When Terminating Dependent Coverage

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Entering an End Date on an Existing Coverage Detail Record:

  • Coverage End Date in the “Dependent [dependent’s full name] was covered before but will not be as of…” message that displays when you enter the End Date on the existing Coverage Detail record and click Save = Coverage End Date you entered on the Coverage Detail record + one day.
  • Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The Coverage End Date you entered on the existing Coverage Detail record.
  • New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) = Coverage End Date you entered on the existing Coverage Detail record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for an Existing COBRA Participant with the Same Qualifying Event Date

  • Coverage End Date in the “Dependent [dependent’s full name] was covered before but will not be as of…” message that displays when you add the new Coverage Detail record and click Save = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.
  • Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective Date.
  • New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for an Existing COBRA Participant with a Different Qualifying Event Date

  • Coverage End Date = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.
  • Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective Date.
  • New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record. > Note: Note: There is no difference between the way the dates are determined when an existing COBRA dependent is terminated by adding a new coverage detail record with the same OR different qualifying event dates. The system uses this distinction to determine whether to create a new COBRA Participant record or update the existing COBRA Participant record (if you selected the option to add the new coverage details to a COBRA Participant record.) New Qualifying Event Date = New COBRA Participant record. Same Qualifying Event Date = Updated COBRA Participant record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage by Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for a New COBRA Participant

  • Coverage End Date = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.
  • Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective Date.
  • New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date (if applicable) = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.

Enrolling Employees in Flexible Spending Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Flex_Spending_Accounts.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Flex_Spending_Accounts.htm

Enrolling Employees in Flexible Spending Accounts

To enroll employees in Flexible Spending Account (FSA) plans, use the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form.

At the onset of participation in the plan, the employee must choose and commit to a total contribution amount. This amount funds either medical or dependent care expenses incurred by the employee within the plan year.

When the employee is enrolled in a Flexible Spending Account plan, PrismHR automatically adds the deduction to the employee’s deduction form. The system calculates the deduction each payroll period. The system uses a calculation that ensures the employee’s deduction amount is always up-to-date, even if the employee switches payroll groups, misses a paycheck, and so on.

To set up basic FSA plan parameters for an employee:

  1. Complete the following information as required in the Flexible Spending Accounts panel.
Use this option To define this
Employee The employee for whom basic information is being set up. Either type the name or ID to display list of matching employee records, or click Employee to open the search window. The system lists any existing adjustments.
Plan Year The FSA Plan Year for which the accounts and elections apply. The system tracks every plan year and their associated accounts, elections, and other information. If the employee continues participation in the plan from one year to the next, you must use this form to establish a new account with a new committed total contribution amount for the next year. HSA plan years must have the format HSXX, where XX is the year. Click Plan Year to display the available plan years in the Existing Plan Years section. The system displays the starting date and ending date for each plan. Click the name of a plan year from the list of plans to display the details for that plan for the indicated employee.
Override Deduction Start Date The date when FSA plan deductions begin. The deduction applies to any payrolls with a pay date on or after this date
Override Deduction Stop Date The date when FSA plan deductions cease. The system stops calculating the deduction in any payrolls processed with a pay date after this date.
Next Pay Date A read-only field to view the employee’s next scheduled pay date on the form. > Note: Note: Please note the following: - When you do not select any employee, then the value in this field is blank. - For the Next Pay Date field to be displayed, the payroll process must be in timesheet entry state and the payroll must not be calculated. If a payroll has been calculated and finalized then the Next Pay Date field will display as expected.
  • When you do not select any employee, then the value in this field is blank.
  • For the Next Pay Date field to be displayed, the payroll process must be in timesheet entry state and the payroll must not be calculated. If a payroll has been calculated and finalized then the Next Pay Date field will display as expected.
  1. Click Save.

The following example illustrates the Flexible Spending Accounts panel.

[Image: screenshot]

Entering Employee Elections

To enter an employee’s elections for a plan, use the Elections panel.

To enter the employee’s elections:

  1. Complete the following information as required in the Elections panel.
Use this option To define this
Account Code Each Flexible Spending Account Code for this FSA plan. The account description displays.
Plan Year Election The amount the employee has committed to funding the flexible spending account.
Plan Year to Date - Deductions Deductions that were taken from the employee’s pay check.
Plan Year to Date - Reimbursements Reimbursements that have been paid.
Override Start Date The date on which to begin payroll deductions for this FSA plan.
Override Stop Date The date on which to end payroll deductions for this FSA plan.
  1. Click Save.

Note: Note: When you enter an employee’s elections in the Elections panel, the Carryover Deduction column is blank. After completing the payroll process, the system will update the carryover column with the calculated carryover amount for an employee with a mid-year plan.

The following example illustrates the Elections panel for an employee with a mid-year plan.

[Image: screenshot]

Setting Up Override Calculations

To set up override calculations for a flexible spending account, use the Override Calculations panel.

To set up override calculations:

  1. Complete the following information as required in the Override Calculations panel.

Use this option — To define this

Account — Each account selected in the Elections panel.

Deduction Override — The non-standard deduction override to deduct each pay period, if the employee changed pay cycles, or was not enrolled for the entire year.

Match Override — The non-standard match override contributed by the company each pay period.

Periods — The alternate deduction period schedule when the deduction and match override amounts apply, instead of applying them to all deduction periods.

Over Date — The pay date on which this override applies. If left blank, the system applies the override amount for all pay dates. Override amounts will be used for all pay dates if the Over Date field is left blank.

HDHP Not Required — Whether the employee has a Health Savings Account (HSA) but is not enrolled in a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP). Usually, HDHP enrollment is a requirement

Suppress Contribution Limits — Whether to ignore the HSA Maximum Annual Contributions when calculating deductions for this employee.

HSA PEO Match Override — Enter an amount if you want to override the match set at the system level in the back end.

  1. Click Save.

Defining Whether Account Balances Carry Forward

To determine whether a flexible spending account allows the employee to carry a positive balance forward at the end of a calendar year into the next year, use the Account Balances panel.

The Account Balances panel lists each Account selected in the Elections panel. It also displays the Funded Balance and the Elected Balance.

To define whether account balances carry forward to the next year:

  1. Complete the information as required in the Account Balances panel.

  2. For each account, indicate whether the FSA account balance will Carry Forward into the next calendar year.

  3. Click Save.

Viewing FSA Activity

To list the vouchers that include deductions and reimbursements, use the Flexible Spending Account Activity panel.

Note: Note: This information is for reference only.

To list deductions and reimbursements:

  1. Review the information that displays in the Flexible Spending Account Activity panel.
Column Description
Voucher No. The pay voucher where the transaction occurred.
Pay Date The date on the pay voucher.
Account Type The type of FSA account.
Account Description The description of the FSA account.
Deduction The deduction amount.
Reimbursement Amt. The reimbursement amount.
Reference No. The FSA Reference number for the reimbursed entry.
  1. When finished, close the panel.

Defining the Company Match

To define the company’s annual match and view the match year-to-date amounts for the flexible spending account, use the Company Match panel. The Matched YTD is the amount paid by the company so far this year.

To define the company match:

  1. Complete the following information as required in the Company Match panel.

  2. For each account, enter the company’s Annual Match commitment to the employee.

  3. Click Save.

Maintaining Employee Retirement Loans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Retirement_Loans.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Retirement_Loans.htm

Maintaining Employee Retirement Loans

To set up or modify loans that employees can take against their retirement plans, use the Employee Retirement Loans form. The IRS governs the available loan amount, the term of the loan, and the repayment schedule for principal and interest. Under certain conditions, the employee can access the loaned fund without incurring tax liability.

To create a new loan:

  1. Open the Employee Retirement Loans form.

  2. Click Set Up New Loan. The system generates a loan number and displays it in Loan Number.

Use this option — To define this

Employee — The Employee for whom the loan is being created. Either type the name or ID to display a list of matching employee records, or click Employee to open the search window. The system lists any existing adjustments. The employee must have a retirement plan defined in PrismHR.

  1. Click Save.

To edit an existing loan:

  1. Open the Employee Retirement Loans form.

  2. Click Loan Number and select the Loan ID. The form populates with the current information.

  3. Make the changes.

  4. Click Save.

To maintain the details of the loan:

  1. On the Retirement Loans Details panel:
Use this option To define this
Retirement Plan The retirement plan on which to base the loan.
Loan Amount The total loan amount granted to the employee.
Loan Date The date of the loan. This is for reference only; the deduction begins in the next payroll period, regardless of the date entered in this field.
Reason for Loan The reason the company allowed the loan. For example, you might want to make a note of the reasons or circumstances for the loan, or other pertinent information.
Payment Amount The payment amount per pay period as detailed in the plan administrator’s schedule. The plan administrator should provide you a loan amortization schedule that details the amount of the loan payment and the total pay back amount. The frequency of the loan payment depends on the retirement plan’s Loan Payment Cycle; see Retirement Plan Enrollment.
Pay Back Amount The total amount the employee must pay back on this loan. The value might not match the Loan Amount because it can include principal and interest.
TPA Loan Identifier The TPA loan identifier. This information may be required for TPA reporting.
Deduction Start Date The pay date when payroll deductions begin. If you leave this field blank, deductions commence immediately. The system calculates and displays the other values: - Paid Back to Date: Amount received against the loan. - Balance Due: Current balance due on the loan.
  • Paid Back to Date: Amount received against the loan.
  • Balance Due: Current balance due on the loan.
  1. Click Save.

To set up loan override payment information:

  1. On the Override Payment panel:
Use this option To define this
Override Payment Amount The override payment amount.
Override From Pay Date The date the override begins.
Override To Pay Date The date the override ends.
  1. Click Save.

To view and enter paid back adjustments on the loan:

  1. On the Adjustments panel:

Use this option — To define this

Paid Back Adjustment — The amount to apply to the current balance. The information in the table updates automatically.

New Balance Equals — The new balance amount. The system updates this balance automatically based on the Paid Back Adjustment.

  1. Click Save. The table is updated with the following values:

  • Adjusted By: User ID of the person who entered the adjustment.

  • On Date: Date on which user saved the adjustment.

  • At Time: Time at which the user saved the adjustment.

  • Amount: Amount of the adjustment.

Displaying Employee Retirement Plan Totals

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employee_Retirement_Plan_Register.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employee_Retirement_Plan_Register.htm

Displaying Employee Retirement Plan Totals

To display employee retirement plan totals for the specified plan year and plan year period, use the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

To display employee retirement plan totals:

  1. Open the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

Use this option — To define this

Employee ID — The Employee for the retirement plan. Either type the name or ID to display list of matching employee records. Click Employee to open the search window.

Plan ID — Enter or select the Retirement Plan plan from the Select Plan selector.

Plan Year — The retirement plan year.

Plan Year Period — The plan year period. The employee’s current retirement plan information displays.

Qualified Retirement Earnings — The amount of qualified retirement earnings to update.

Elective Contributions (Pre-Tax) — The pre-tax elective contribution amount of the employee.

Catch-Up Contributions (Pre-Tax) — The pre-tax catch-up contribution amount of the employee.

Roth Contributions (Post-Tax) — The post-tax Roth contribution amount of the employee.

Roth Catch-Up Contributions (Post-Tax) — The post-tax Roth catch-up contribution amount of the employee.

Employee Contributions (Post Tax) — The post-tax elective contribution amount of the employee.

Employer Contribution — The contribution amount made by the employer.

Employer Non-Elective Contributions — The non-elective contribution amount made by the employer.

Employer Safe Harbor Type 1 Contribution — Employer’s Safe Harbor Type 1 contribution amount.

Employer Safe Harbor Type 2 Contribution — Employer’s Safe Harbor Type 2 contribution amount.

Successor Retirement Deferral — The amount of successor retirement deferral (pre-tax contributions) made by the employee with a previous employer. The system takes this amount into consideration when calculating a deferral limit, but it is not reported to the third-party administrator of the current plan.

Successor Catch-up Deferral — The deferral amount (pre-tax catch-up contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.

Successor ROTH Deferral — The Roth deferral amount (post-tax contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.

Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral — The Roth catch-up contribution amount (post-tax catch-up contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.

PEO Contribution — The contribution made by the PEO.

Employee Retirement Loan Payments — The retirement loan payments made by the employee.

  1. Click Cancel when you finish reviewing the information.

The form also displays an interactive bar charts to visualize employee earnings, contributions, and employer contributions against applicable IRS limits. Once you select an Employee ID, Plan ID, and Plan Year, then the new bar charts displays Year-to-Date totals up to four charts:

  • 401K Earnings vs. Annual Compensation
  • Employee Contributions
  • HPE Employee Contributions - It is displayed only for HPE employees only
  • Total EE & ER Contributions

Each chart displays actual values alongside the applicable limit. You can hover over a section to view the detailed breakdown of all contribution types and totals. Selecting any bar opens a detail view with an itemized chart and access to the underlying voucher list.

Viewing Employees Assigned to a Benefit Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Employees%20Assigned%20To.htm Path: BA/Topics/Employees Assigned To.htm

Viewing Employees Assigned to a Benefit Plan

Use the Employees Assigned To form to view the employees that are enrolled in the selected Benefit Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

To access this form, after you have selected a Plan Class on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Actions menu, click Employees Assigned To. You cannot find this form using normal search means. This form need to be added to your User Role to access this form.

Note: Note: The Employee Assigned To option under the Actions menu is available only if the Plan Class field is set to Group Benefit on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

  • The Active employee count displays the number of active employees based on the active Enrollment Status count.

  • The Enrollment Status filter displays total number of Active employees assigned to the selected Benefit Plan by default. You can change this to any one of the options from the drop-down.

  • The grid contains the following columns:

  • Employee ID: If you click on this hyperlink the Employee Benefits Enrollment modal form is displayed. The Employee and the Benefit Plan fields on the modal form is pre-populated and is in a read-only format. The Employee ID hyperlink is accessible only if you have Full or Inquiry access to that employee in the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

  • Employee Name: The employee name is listed here.

  • Employment Status: The employment status of the employee will display here.

  • Enrollment Status: The enrollments status of the employee will display here.

  • Coverage Level: The insurance coverage level of the employee will display here.

  • You can sort this grid by any of the five headers noted above.

  • You can scroll to see all employees on a page. There are 11 employees listed per page. If there are more than 11 employees listed, then you can scroll to subsequent pages.

  • Click Close to close this form and return to the Benefit Plan Setup form.

  • Click Report to run a report for the Employees Assigned To. Once the report is run, you can export the data of the employees assigned to the relevant benefit plan. You can download this report into a XLS file on your system.

Establishing Election Details

To establish retirement plan election information, use the Election Details panel in the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

The percent and amount settings in this panel are mutually exclusive. Define either a percentage or a flat amount, not both. You can set a maximum percent only for the Elective Amount field.

To set up general retirement plan information for an employee:

  1. Open the Election Details panel.
Use this option… To define this…
Effective Date Whether to edit an existing effective date or establish a new effective date.
New Effective Date A new effective date. The new record populates with the information entered in the Election Details panel on the previous record.
Delete Effective Date icon Click this hyperlink to delete the enrollment details effective as of the Effective Date for the employee.
Elective Percent / Elective Amount The elective percentage or amount in dollar that the employee elects to defer on a pre-tax basis. They can select to choose the amount between dollar or percent from the drop-down.
Auto Escalation? This field will display only if the Auto Escalator field is checked for this retirement plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form. - Unchecked – Auto Escalation does not apply. - Checked – Auto Escalation applies to an Elective Percent. You can select this checkbox only when: - Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 and Percent is selected. - Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 with Percent selected and additional values exist in the Employee Contributions table. > Note: Note: Additionally, when an employee is auto enrolled in a retirement plan, the Auto Escalation? field is automatically checked. - When you flag the Auto Escalation? field then, the Payroll Calculation process triggers a retirement auto enrollment record to be created for eligible employees using the calculated date with the defined auto enrollment percent (between 3% - 10%) up to the maximum defined amount which is set on the Benefit Plan Setup form. - Also, when an existing retirement plan enrollment has the Auto Escalation? field flagged and has a Next Auto Escalation Date which is less than or equal to the calculated payroll, then a new Election Detail is automatically created with an Effective Date equal to the defined Next Auto Escalation Date. The value in the Amount column for Elective Percent field reflects the prior election amount in addition to the auto escalation percent. Please note the following validations on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form: - For an existing Retirement Plan Enrollment record, when the Auto Escalation? field is checked and if you change value in any field which affects employee election amounts for contributions, then while saving the form a warning message displays. - You cannot select the Auto Escalation? checkbox if you are using Dollar as the value for Elective contribution method. If you use the Dollar as the value and select the Auto Escalation? checkbox, then a warning message displays.
  • Unchecked – Auto Escalation does not apply.
  • Checked – Auto Escalation applies to an Elective Percent.
  • Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 and Percent is selected.
  • Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 with Percent selected and additional values exist in the Employee Contributions table.
  • When you flag the Auto Escalation? field then, the Payroll Calculation process triggers a retirement auto enrollment record to be created for eligible employees using the calculated date with the defined auto enrollment percent (between 3% - 10%) up to the maximum defined amount which is set on the Benefit Plan Setup form.
  • Also, when an existing retirement plan enrollment has the Auto Escalation? field flagged and has a Next Auto Escalation Date which is less than or equal to the calculated payroll, then a new Election Detail is automatically created with an Effective Date equal to the defined Next Auto Escalation Date. The value in the Amount column for Elective Percent field reflects the prior election amount in addition to the auto escalation percent.
  • For an existing Retirement Plan Enrollment record, when the Auto Escalation? field is checked and if you change value in any field which affects employee election amounts for contributions, then while saving the form a warning message displays.
  • You cannot select the Auto Escalation? checkbox if you are using Dollar as the value for Elective contribution method. If you use the Dollar as the value and select the Auto Escalation? checkbox, then a warning message displays. | Next Auto Escalation Date | It is a read-only field which displays the next escalation date. This field is displayed only if you have checked the Auto Escalation? field. | | Not to exceed this percent of retirement pay | If you have entered an elective amount, and you do not want that amount to exceed a certain percentage of retirement pay, enter it here. | | Catch-Up Percent Catch-Up Amount | The employee’s elective contribution for catch-up contributions.: - The Catch-Up Percent that the employee elects to defer on a pre-tax basis. - The Catch-Up Amount that the employee elects to contribute on a pre-tax basis. |
  • The Catch-Up Percent that the employee elects to defer on a pre-tax basis.
  • The Catch-Up Amount that the employee elects to contribute on a pre-tax basis. | Roth Percent Roth Amount | Either of the following values: - The Roth Percent the employee elects to contribute. - The Roth Amount the employee elects to contribute. |
  • The Roth Percent the employee elects to contribute.
  • The Roth Amount the employee elects to contribute. | Roth Catch-Up Percent Roth Catch-Up Amount | The employee’s elective contribution for Roth contributions. Either of the following values - The Roth Catch-Up Percent the employee elects to contribute. - The Roth Catch-Up Amount the employee elects to contribute. |
  • The Roth Catch-Up Percent the employee elects to contribute.
  • The Roth Catch-Up Amount the employee elects to contribute. | Post-Tax Percent Post-Tax Amount | The post-tax contribution value. Either of the following values: - The Post-Tax Percent the employee elects to defer on a post-tax basis. - The Post-Tax Amount the employee elects for post-tax contributions. |
  • The Post-Tax Percent the employee elects to defer on a post-tax basis.
  • The Post-Tax Amount the employee elects for post-tax contributions. | Key Employee | Whether the employee is a key employee for the purpose of 401(k) plan discrimination testing and reporting. | | Highly Compensated | Whether the employee is highly compensated for the purpose of 401(k) plan discrimination testing and reporting. | | Ownership Percent | The Ownership Percent. | | Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant | For a Highly Paid Employee (HPE), this read-only Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant panel tracks if the employee met or exceeded the HPE threshold in the prior tax year. For example, for tax year 2024, if the employee met this threshold, then the Retirement Year record would be entered as 2025 with the HPE Prior Year option selected as Yes. The table is displayed only when you select a plan and provide an effective date and the data is fetched from the Other tab on the Employee Details form. |
  1. Click Save.

Field Name Description

Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

When you set up benefit plans, you create sets of benefits for groups or categories of employees. In general, a group benefit plan contains:

  • States that offer the plan

  • Covered plan types (also called tiers)

  • Premium rates

  • Billing rates

Before you define the benefit plans, you must define the group benefit plan types. You set up group benefit plans at the system level, but you can also administer them at the client level.

HSA, FSA, and Section 125 Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Front-Matter/BA_UG_Chapter_HSAPlans.htm Path: BA/Topics/Front-Matter/BA_UG_Chapter_HSAPlans.htm

HSA, FSA, and Section 125 Benefit Plans

A health savings account (HSA) is a tax-exempt savings account that, when paired with a qualified high-deductible health plan (QHDHP), can be used to pay for certain medical expenses. Funds deposited are not taxed, nor are withdrawals for qualified expenses.

A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) lets employees take home a larger paycheck by reducing their taxable income. Employees enrolled contribute tax-free dollars into an account that can be used throughout the year on qualified medical, dental and vision or qualified dependent care expenses — reducing out-of-pocket costs

Section 125 plans enable participating employees to direct a portion of their pre-tax salary to be used to pay for approved premiums, health, dental, and vision care expenses and dependent care expenses.

While you can establish FSA and HSA plans under Section 125 settings, PrismHR allows you to maintain your FSA and HSA benefit plans separately. The HSA Plans form is typically used when your FSA and HSA plan years differ.

Setting Up FSA Account Types and Year Limits

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/FSA_Accounts.htm Path: BA/Topics/FSA_Accounts.htm

Setting Up FSA Account Types and Year Limits

To maintain flexible spending account (FSA) types, use the Flex Spend Account Types form. FSA plan types are also used in setting up health savings account (HSA) plans.

Setting Account Types

To maintain flexible spending account (FSA) types:

  1. Open the Flexible Spending Account Types form.
Use this option To define this
Account Code An alphanumeric Account Code for the FSA plan. If you are defining a plan type for a health savings account (HSA) plan, the Account Code must begin with the letters HSA, for example: “HSADEP.”
Account Description A brief account description of the FSA plan.
Account Description (Spanish) A brief account description of the FSA plan in Spanish.
Plan Year Limit The maximum annual amount an employee can contribute to this FSA plan. If a maximum amount does not apply, enter 0. The Plan Year Limit is the default amount for all plan years. If nothing listed in the Plan Year Limit panel, the system will use this.
Reimburse in Arrears Whether the employee can be reimbursed more than was contributed to this FSA plan.
Reimbursement Detail Required Whether detailed expense information is required for a reimbursement request.
Classify As Dependent Care Whether this FSA plan type is for dependent care. Dependent Care FSA taxes vary for each state.
Classify As Health Care Whether this FSA plan type is for health care. There is an annual maximum amount that can be sheltered from taxes.
Maximum Carry-forward Amount Whether amounts can carry over from one year to the next.
Plan Year Election is a Monthly Amount Whether to calculate the election as a monthly amount. This requires additional processing; select this option only when necessary.
Third Party Assigned Code Whether the third-party company uses a different account code for this FSA account type.
Deduction Taken Post-tax Whether to take the plan deductions after calculating taxes. Typically, FSA deductions are made pre-tax.
Offer Type Whether to include the benefit plan in benefits and open enrollments in Benefits Enrollment. Offer types classify the benefit plan and assure that the plan displays correctly in enrollment workflows. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) For an HSA plan, select HSA - Health Savings Account.
Stamp Date Used as Override Stop Date When EE is Terminated This field has the following drop-downs: - Select – This is the default setting. Select this option if you want FSA/HSA enrollments for this Account Type to remain active when the employee is terminated. Any Account Type that earlier had the Stamp Term Date as Override Stop Date At EE Term? field unchecked will be set to this option. - Employee’s Date of Termination – Select this option if you want to apply the employee termination date as an override stop date on Section 125 benefit plans. So the employee termination date will populate on the Override Stop Date field on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form. Any Account Type that earlier had the Stamp Term Date as Override Stop Date At EE Term? field checked will be set to this option. - End of Month following Termination Date – Select this option if you want to apply the last date of the month during which the employee was terminated as an override stop date. So the last date of the month during which the employee was terminated will populate on the Override Stop Date field on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form.
  • Select – This is the default setting. Select this option if you want FSA/HSA enrollments for this Account Type to remain active when the employee is terminated. Any Account Type that earlier had the Stamp Term Date as Override Stop Date At EE Term? field unchecked will be set to this option.
  • Employee’s Date of Termination – Select this option if you want to apply the employee termination date as an override stop date on Section 125 benefit plans. So the employee termination date will populate on the Override Stop Date field on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form. Any Account Type that earlier had the Stamp Term Date as Override Stop Date At EE Term? field checked will be set to this option.
  • End of Month following Termination Date – Select this option if you want to apply the last date of the month during which the employee was terminated as an override stop date. So the last date of the month during which the employee was terminated will populate on the Override Stop Date field on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form.
  1. Click Save.

Setting the Plan Year Limit

To maintain annual overrides of the amount an employee can contribute to a plan for each year that had an override amount, use the Plan Year Limit panel. This information is required in Benefits Enrollment.

To maintain annual overrides of the amount an employee can contribute to a plan:

  1. Open the Plan Year Limit panel.

Use this option — To define this

Plan Year — The benefit Plan Year.

Plan Year Limit — The maximum annual amount an employee can contribute to the benefit plan.

Minimum Amount — The minimum annual amount an employee must contribute to the benefit plan (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Max Individual Amount — The maximum annual amount an employee can contribute as an individual to the benefit plan (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Max Household Amount — The maximum annual amount an employee can contribute as a Household to the benefit plan field (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Catch-Up Limit (>55) — The catch‑up amount an employee who is age fifty-five or over can contribute as a Household to the benefit plan in the Catch-Up Limit (>55) field. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) > Note: Note: This amount applies to employees age 54 if they turn 55 during the plan year. For example, an HSA plan year starts 01/01/2020 and ends 12/31/2020. In that year, an employee turns 55. The system lets the employee elect the additional Catch-Up Limit amount when they are 54.

  1. Click Save.

Configuring Age Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/GBP_Age_Parameters.htm Path: BA/Topics/GBP_Age_Parameters.htm

Configuring Age Parameters

To establish the age parameters in which a group benefit plan is offered, use the Age Parameters panel on the Group Benefit Plans form.

Note: Note: The Age Parameters panel only displays when you select an existing Benefit Plan ID which has an Insurance Class set up as Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, or Life Insurance.

To configure the age parameters in which a plan is offered:

  1. Open the Age Parameters panel.
Use this option To define this
Age Calculation (Month/Day) - The Age Calculation Month method used to calculate employees’ age for insurance premium calculations. - The Age Calculation Day on which employees’ insurance premium ages are based. The drop-down field only displays when you select a valid month (January-December).
  • The Age Calculation Month method used to calculate employees’ age for insurance premium calculations.
  • The Age Calculation Day on which employees’ insurance premium ages are based. The drop-down field only displays when you select a valid month (January-December). | Dependent’s Age Limit | The age at which the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. If the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The selected value determines when the dependent age limit becomes effective: - On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. - End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. Therefore, the dependent is longer eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified. - End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective. For example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017 and the plan effective date is April 25, 2017, the dependent is still considered eligible for coverage and is able to enroll even if the dependent’s actual age has reached the age limit specified. |
  • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.
  • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.
  • End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. | Disabled Dependent Eligible | Whether disabled dependents who are above the age specified in the Disabled Alt Age Limit (who would otherwise be ineligible for coverage) are eligible for benefits. This field is displayed only if the Dependent’s Age Limit field has a value. | | Disabled Alt Age Limit | If the dependent is disabled, specify the age limit. This field is visible only if the Disabled Dependent Eligible field is checked. | | Override Dependent Age Limits By State | Configure state level override(s) for Dependent Age Limits to easily manage differences in plans at the state level. - Unchecked – (Default) The Dependent Age Limit State Overrides table remains hidden. - Checked – The Dependent Age Limit Override table is displayed with the following column headers: - States – Enter the state code or select from the Select States selector. - Dep Age Limit – Provide the dependent age limit. - Dep Age Calculation Method – Select how you want to calculate the dependent’s age from the drop-down options. The available options are: - On date of birth (DOB) - End of DOB year - End of DOB month - Disabled Dep? – Specify if the dependent is disabled. - Disabled Alt Age Limit – If the dependent is disabled, specify the age limit. This field is enabled only if you select Yes for the Disabled Dep? field. Please note the following: - If there are no states listed in this table, then upon saving the form an error message displays: No state listed in the dependent age limit override table. - If you do not input any value in any of the rows in the table, then an error message displays upon saving: The [field name] for the state of [State value] is missing from the dependent age limit override table. - The system uses the State’s Dependent Age limit and its related Calculation Method and Disabled Eligibility Limit as an override for determining when the Dependent Age Limit becomes effective. If there is no override configured for a given state in the Dependent Age Limit Override table, then the system uses the existing Dependent Age Limit (and related fields’) values as default. |
  • Unchecked – (Default) The Dependent Age Limit State Overrides table remains hidden.
  • Checked – The Dependent Age Limit Override table is displayed with the following column headers:
  • States – Enter the state code or select from the Select States selector.
  • Dep Age Limit – Provide the dependent age limit.
  • Dep Age Calculation Method – Select how you want to calculate the dependent’s age from the drop-down options. The available options are:
  • On date of birth (DOB)
  • End of DOB year
  • End of DOB month
  • Disabled Dep? – Specify if the dependent is disabled.
  • Disabled Alt Age Limit – If the dependent is disabled, specify the age limit. This field is enabled only if you select Yes for the Disabled Dep? field.
  • If there are no states listed in this table, then upon saving the form an error message displays: No state listed in the dependent age limit override table.
  • If you do not input any value in any of the rows in the table, then an error message displays upon saving: The [field name] for the state of [State value] is missing from the dependent age limit override table.
  • The system uses the State’s Dependent Age limit and its related Calculation Method and Disabled Eligibility Limit as an override for determining when the Dependent Age Limit becomes effective. If there is no override configured for a given state in the Dependent Age Limit Override table, then the system uses the existing Dependent Age Limit (and related fields’) values as default. | Use Spouse DOB for Dependent Age | Whether to use the spouse date of birth for medical, dental, and vision calculations. | | Use Current Year for Age Calculation | Whether to use the current year for employee age calculations. | | Base Age Calculation on Coverage Start Date | Whether to use the employee’s age at the time of the coverage start date if it is greater than the age calculated by the plan based on the plan settings. | | Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty | Whether the age and rate dates are fixed by guaranty. When you select this field, if there are any Employee Benefit Enrollments records tied to the Benefit Plan that have a status of Active, then a message displays: There are active employees in this benefit plan. The Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty will not apply to employees enrolled prior to this flag being checked. The current coverage detail record for each employee will need to be saved or a new coverage detail record created in order to apply the Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty. | | Number of Years Guaranty | The number of years guaranty for a medical, dental, or vision plan that requires age-banded billing. |
  1. Click Save.

Copying a Benefit Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/GBP_Copy_Benefit_Plan.htm Path: BA/Topics/GBP_Copy_Benefit_Plan.htm

Copying a Benefit Plan

To copy an existing group benefit plan to a new benefit plan ID, use the Copy Benefit Plan form, accessed in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

on the Group Benefit Plans form.

To copy a benefit plan:

  1. In the Group Benefit Plans form, open the benefit plan you want to copy.

  2. In the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] , click Copy Benefit Plan.

Use this option To define this
Benefit Plan ID to Copy to A new plan ID for the copy of the benefit plan.

  1. Click Accept.

  2. Click OK to continue. The system displays the Confirmation dialog. Click Yes to confirm and overwrite the existing benefit plan, or No to close without making changes. The system copies the record and displays the processing status.

  3. Click Close.

Note: Note: Validation to the Copy Benefit Plan feature is now in place to prevent copying a plan to itself. This prevents billing rates from being inadvertently deleted when the source and destination IDs are identical.

Maintaining Coverage Amounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/GBP_Coverage_Amounts.htm Path: BA/Topics/GBP_Coverage_Amounts.htm

Maintaining Coverage Amounts

To maintain coverage amounts for a life insurance plan that covers employees, spouses, and dependents, use the Coverage Amounts panel and the Age Reduction Schedule panel on the Group Benefit Plans form.

To maintain coverage amounts for a life insurance plan that covers employees:

  1. Open the Coverage Amounts panel:

Use this option — To define this

Employee Life Coverage Start Amount — The start amount for the plan coverage. This field is required.

Employee Life Coverage End Amount or Employee Salary Multiplier — The Employee Life Coverage End Amount or Employee Salary Multiplier. This field is required and cannot be less than the Employee Life Coverage Start Amount. > Note: Note: The default rounding method, when set to select, rounds based on the Coverage increment. For example, a 1,000 increment will round to the nearest thousand, and a 10,000 increment rounds to the nearest ten thousand.

Employee Life Coverage Increment amount — The increment amount. This field is required.

  1. Click Save.

To maintain coverage amounts for a life insurance plan that covers spouses:

  1. Open the Coverage Amounts panel.

Use this option — To define this

Spouse Life Coverage Start Amount — The start amount for the plan coverage. This field is required.

Spouse Life Coverage End Amount — The end amount for the plan coverage. This field is required and cannot be less than the Spouse Life Coverage Start Amount.

Spouse Life Coverage Increment amount — The increment amount. This field is required.

Percent for Spouse — This option must be selected for spouse-only life insurance plans that have the offer type set to Life Insurance - Basic - Spouse Only (LIS).

For Spouse — Whether eligibility is independent of the employee.

  1. Click Save.

To maintain coverage amounts for a life insurance plan that covers dependents:

  1. Open the Coverage Amounts panel.

Use this option — To define this

Depens Life Coverage Start Amount — The start amount for the plan coverage. This field is required.

Depens Life Coverage End Amount — The end amount for the plan coverage. This field is required and cannot be less than the Spouse Life Coverage Start Amount.

Depens Life Coverage Increment — The increment amount. This field is required.

Percent for Dependents — This option must be selected for dependent-only life insurance plans that have the offer type set to Life Insurance - Basic - Child Only (CIS).

For Dependents — Whether eligibility is independent of the employee.

  1. Click Save.

Specifying the Age Reduction Schedule

If the amount of coverage varies by age, specify the percent of full coverage by age in the Age Reduction Schedule table.

To specify the age reduction schedule:

  1. Open the Age Reduction Schedule panel.

Use this option — To define this

Age — Provide the age that you want it to vary for amount of coverage.

Percent of Full Coverage — The percent of full coverage if the amount of coverage varies by age. The premium cost remains the same, but the coverage cost varies depending on the age specified.

Minimum Reduced Coverage — The minimum amount of coverage that may be offered for the age specified. If the result of a coverage reduction calculation causes the coverage amount to fall below the Minimum Reduced Coverage amount specified for the age bracket, the Minimum Reduced Coverage amount is applied by the system as the new coverage amount for the employee.

Reduce coverage and premium — Whether both the coverage and premium amounts are reduced.

Reduce — Whether both the coverage and premium amounts are reduced. From the drop-down options, you can either select Coverage Only or Coverage and Premium.

Dependent Spouse Age Reduction — Allows you to include spouse age reduction behavior and schedule. This field has the following drop-down option: - No - Use Employee Schedule - Separate Spouse Schedule When you select the Separate Spouse Schedule option, then the system displays a conditional dependent age reduction multi-value grid where you can add Age and Percentage of Full Coverage for spouse.

Dependent Reduction Provision — Content that you enter here will be displayed to the employees in online Benefits Enrollment when dependents are selected to be covered.

Dependent Reduction Provision (Spanish) — Enter the Dependent Reduction Provision content in Spanish.

  1. Click Save.

Defining Guaranteed Issue Limits

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/GBP_Guaranteed_Issue_Limits.htm Path: BA/Topics/GBP_Guaranteed_Issue_Limits.htm

Defining Guaranteed Issue Limits

Use the Guaranteed Issue Limits panel to set limits for an employee, spouse, and dependents if a life insurance plan is guaranteed to be issued.

To define guaranteed issue limits for a life insurance plan:

  1. Open the Guaranteed Issue Limits panel:

Use this option — To define this

Initial Eligibility Days — The number of days required to determine a late entrant enrollee. The initial period is the later of this number of days after the date of hire or the effective date.

Newly Eligible Maximum Amount — The maximum amount for a newly eligible employee, spouse, and dependents.

Newly Eligible Salary Multiplier — The salary multiplier to use instead of a flat amount. The plan uses the lesser value of the two.

Currently Enrolled Step Amount — The Currently Enrolled Step Amount for the employee, spouse, and dependents.

Currently Enrolled Maximum Amount — The Currently Enrolled Maximum Amount for the employee, spouse, and dependents.

Currently Enrolled Salary Multiplier — The salary multiplier to use instead of a flat amount. The plan uses the lesser value of the two.

Currently Enrolled Step Amount — The step amount for the employee, spouse, and dependents.

Late Entrant Maximum Amount — The maximum amount for the employee, spouse, and dependents.

Late Entrant Salary Multiplier — Enter the salary multiplier to use instead of a flat amount. The plan uses the lesser value of the two.

GI Rounding Method — The GI Rounding Method for the salary multipliers, if required.

  1. Click Save.

Configuring Online Enrollment

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/GBP_Online_Enrollment.htm Path: BA/Topics/GBP_Online_Enrollment.htm

Configuring Online Enrollment

To define how PrismHR processes open enrollment information for the benefit plan, use the Online Enrollment panel on the Group Benefit Plans form.

Note: Note: This section only displays if you select the Enable Benefit Enrollment field on the Global Configuration form.

To configure online enrollment parameters:

  1. Open the Online Enrollment panel.
Use this option To define this
Include in Online Enrollments The plan is used for online enrollments.
Include in Anytime Enrollment Workflow The plan is used in anytime enrollment workflows.
Approval Required Whether to automatically set an initial status of Pending in the Status field of the Employee Group Benefits form.
Collect PCP Information Whether to collect primary care physician ( PCP) information if this plan requires employees to enter PCP information during enrollments. Typically these are health maintenance organization (HMO) medical plans, but some dental or voluntary benefit plans might also require this information. If selected, also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in the PCP Lists field in the Compare Benefits form. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)
PCP Required This option becomes active only if you have enabled the above field. Select this option if PCP is required for the Benefit Plan ID.
PCP Validation Format This is a read-only field. If a PCP Validation Format is available for the selected Benefit Plan ID, it displays here. Click the Edit link next to this field to access the Edit PCP Validation Format form, where you can define a validation format.
Edit This becomes active only if the Collect PCP Information field is checked. Click Edit to open the Edit PCP Validation Format form, where you can enter or edit the format of the Primary Care Physician ID for the selected Benefit Plan ID. The Primary Care Physician ID format can have four types of characters on any position: - Alpha – Select this option for any position if that position needs to be an alphabet. - Numeric – Select this option for any position if that position needs to be a number. - Any Character – Select this option for any position if that position can be any character. - Literal – Select this option for any position if that position need have a specific value for example S. [Image: screenshot] Note: - On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, the Doctor ID field validates the value entered here if that Benefit Plan ID has a validation format set up here. - Edit is not visible to users who only have Inquiry access to the Group Benefit Plans form.
  • Alpha – Select this option for any position if that position needs to be an alphabet.
  • Numeric – Select this option for any position if that position needs to be a number.
  • Any Character – Select this option for any position if that position can be any character.
  • Literal – Select this option for any position if that position need have a specific value for example S.
  • On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, the Doctor ID field validates the value entered here if that Benefit Plan ID has a validation format set up here.
  • Edit is not visible to users who only have Inquiry access to the Group Benefit Plans form.
  1. Click Save.

To configure other parameters of a group benefit plan, use the Other Processing Parameters panel.

Use this option To define this
