For more information, see Setting Up Wellness Benefit Plans.
  • Use Wellness Rates as Default – The wellness banded rates as the default for the benefit plan.
  • Assessment due – The days or months before or after the open enrollment effective date when the wellness assessment is due. | Age Banded Medical Rates | The age calculation information for a medical, dental, or vision plan that requires age-banded billing: - The Age Calc Month method used to calculate employees’ age for insurance premium calculations. - The Age Calc Day on which employees’ insurance premium ages are based. |
  • The Age Calc Month method used to calculate employees’ age for insurance premium calculations.
  • The Age Calc Day on which employees’ insurance premium ages are based. | Coverage Options | The coverage levels allowed for the plan. | | Broker | Optional. Stores a broker contact at the plan level. Enter the Broker Id or click Broker to select an existing one. | | Use Extended Precision Risk Factors | Select this option to enable extended precision for the risk factors. This option enables you to enter more than two decimal places for the risk factor under the Risk Factors panel of the Benefit Plan Setup form. If this setting is disabled, a Risk Factor can only have two decimal places (for example: 1.12). If this setting is enabled, you can enter a Risk Factor with four decimal places (for example: 1.1234). | | Risk Factors By Network | Select this option if Risk Factors vary by network. This only applies to plans with networks. If enabled, the Risk Factor table on the Benefit Plan Setup form will have an extra column named Network where you can set a risk factor rate specific to each network. | | Pay Rate Month & Pay Rate Day | The month and day on which to base the pay rate for insurance coverage calculations. If you select any value in the Month field, you must also select a value in the Day field. Some clients use an insurance coverage calculation (for example, for life insurance) based on the employee pay rate. If you enter a Pay Rate Month and a Pay Rate Day, the system bases the coverage calculation on the employee’s pay rate as of that month and day of the year. If you leave these fields empty, the system recalculates the premiums during every payroll initialization based on the employee’s pay rate at the time. | | Collect Network Information | Whether the system collects network data on this plan. When you select this option, the Benefit Network Locations form becomes available inActions menu [Image: screenshot] . This form is where you can enter network ZIP codes. | | Premium Rates Vary By Network | Whether premium rates are maintained separately for each network. | | Billing Rates Vary By Network | How billing rates are set: - Yes: Bill rates are set by network. - No: Bill rates are set by rate group. - Both: Bill rates are set by network and rate group. |
  • Yes: Bill rates are set by network.
  • No: Bill rates are set by rate group.
  • Both: Bill rates are set by network and rate group. | Coverage Ends On | The date coverage ends when an employee is terminated. You can select a specific date (for example, 16th of the Month) from the drop-down menu, or the following: - Employee’s Date of Termination: Coverage ends on the date the employee is terminated. - End of Month following Termination: Coverage ends at the end of the month in which the employee is terminated. - Employee’s Term Date if prior to 15th of Month else End of Month: If the employee’s termination is before the 15th of the month, coverage ends on the date the employee was terminated. If the employee’s termination is on or after the 15th of the month, coverage ends at the end of the month in which the employee is terminated. |
  • Employee’s Date of Termination: Coverage ends on the date the employee is terminated.
  • End of Month following Termination: Coverage ends at the end of the month in which the employee is terminated.
  • Employee’s Term Date if prior to 15th of Month else End of Month: If the employee’s termination is before the 15th of the month, coverage ends on the date the employee was terminated. If the employee’s termination is on or after the 15th of the month, coverage ends at the end of the month in which the employee is terminated. | Use Billing Wash Rule? | Whether the system applies the billing wash rule to the group benefit plan for all the clients. The Use Billing Wash Rule? is a drop-down has two options: - Select Yes to enable it at the global level, and when enabled, the Wash Rule Date On/Before field displays. You can select for the system to apply the wash rule on or before the 10th Day of the Month through the 20th Day of the Month, or at End of Month. - Select No to not apply the wash rule at the global level. This is a global-level setting. It acts as the default unless there is an override at the client level (on the Benefit Plan Setup form). |
  • Select Yes to enable it at the global level, and when enabled, the Wash Rule Date On/Before field displays. You can select for the system to apply the wash rule on or before the 10th Day of the Month through the 20th Day of the Month, or at End of Month.
  • Select No to not apply the wash rule at the global level. | Flat Coverage Amount | Whether the plan provides a fixed amount of coverage for all benefit plan participants. This amount overrides any existing rules. Typically, you would use this for life insurance plans. | | Premium Based on | Whether to base the short- or long-term disability plan on the employee’s salary rather than coverage amount. > Note: Note: If you select a benefit plan with Offer Type set to Short Term Disability (STD), the Premium Based on field displays these options: - Calculated Coverage – This is the default option. - Rate x Weekly Salary – When you select this option, the conditional Weekly Salary Limit field displays. If you select a benefit plan with Offer Type as Long Term Disability (LTD), then the value in the Premium Based on drop-down are: - Calculated Coverage – This is the default option. - Rate x Monthly Salary – When you select this option, the conditional Monthly Salary Limit field displays. | | Weekly Salary Limit/Monthly Salary Limit | If salary is the basis for LTD/STD premium calculation, the Weekly Salary Limit/Monthly Salary Limit (weekly for STD, monthly for LTD) to the salary amount used during the calculation. | | LTD/STD Rate Tables Banded by Salary rather than Age | Whether the premium rate table for this disability plan is banded by the employee’s annual salary rather than age. | | LTD/STD Use Extended Precision Rates | For a short- or long-term disability benefit plan, whether to enter premium and billing rates that can have any number of digits after the decimal place. If you do not select this option, the rates are fixed at four decimal places. See the Setting Insurance Billing Rates and Setting Premium Rates topics for more information on entering those rates. | | Life Calculation Type | For a life insurance benefit plan, the type of premium calculation used. | | Employee DOB for Spouse Life | For a life insurance benefit plan, whether to use the employee’s date of birth for life insurance premium calculations instead of the spouse’s date of birth. | | Non-taxable Limit | For a life insurance benefit plan, the non-taxable limit if it is completely paid by clients. Any coverage over that limit is taxed. > Note: Note: You can view the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form by selecting View Tax Rates. | | Dependent Life Calc Type | For a life insurance benefit plan, type of dependent premium calculation. | | Dependent Life Age Banded | For a life insurance benefit plan, whether the life insurance calculation for the dependent’s premium is age-banded based on the employee’s age. If not selected, the system calculates the premium using a single rate. | | Directly Carried | For a life insurance benefit plan, whether the employees pay the full premiums and coverage over the limit should not be taxed. |
  1. Click Save.

Would you like to continue?. | | Inactive | Whether to deactivate the network at the system level. Field Name — Description

Invoice Period section

Year — By default the current year is displayed. Select the year for which to generate COBRA invoices from the drop-down which has a 10 year look back.

Start Day — Enter the day of the month to start the invoice period. Enrollees who have a bill day before this day will be skipped.

End Day — Enter the day of the month to end the invoice period. Enrollees who have a bill day after this day will be skipped.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Group_Benefit_Plan_Types.htm Path: BA/Topics/Group_Benefit_Plan_Types.htm

Defining Types of Group Benefit Plans

Group benefit plans can cover more than one employee coverage situation. For example, an organization can use a benefit plan for single employees, employees who have one child, or employees with large families. Each situation is defined by a group benefit plan type (also called a tier).

Each group benefit plan specifies the plan types it covers.

Before defining group benefit plans:

  • Use the Group Benefit Plan Types form to define the types of group benefit plans.

To define group benefit plan types:

  1. Open the Group Benefit Plan Types form.
Use this option To define this
Type Code The code representing the benefit plan type (for example, ES). You cannot enter a zero in the Type Code field on the Group Benefit Plan Types form. If you do, you will get an error message: Invalid Type Code. Click OK. The zero will be removed from the Type Code field.
Type Description The description of the type code (for example, Employee + Spouse).
Type Description (Spanish) The description of the type code in Spanish.
TPA Type Code The third‑party type code that corresponds to the billing rate. - Single - Couple - 1 Parent + 1 Child - Parent + more than one child - Family
  • Single
  • Couple
  • 1 Parent + 1 Child
  • Parent + more than one child
  • Family | Coverage Class | The class that describes the insurance coverage. - Single (employee) coverage - Dual (employee + 1) coverage - Family (employee + 2 or more) coverage |
  • Single (employee) coverage
  • Dual (employee + 1) coverage
  • Family (employee + 2 or more) coverage | Cover Spouse | Whether the plan can cover a spouse. - Yes, Can Cover Spouse - No, Cannot Cover Spouse - Only Can Cover Spouse |
  • Yes, Can Cover Spouse
  • No, Cannot Cover Spouse
  • Only Can Cover Spouse | Dependent Min/Max Type | Whether the plan can cover the employee’s dependents. - Regular Dependent - Domestic Partner Children - Both |
  • Regular Dependent
  • Domestic Partner Children
  • Both | Minimum Dependents | The minimum number of dependents to include. | | Maximum Dependents | The maximum number of dependents to include. | | Spouse Required | Whether a spouse is required. | | Domestic Partner Required | Whether a domestic partner is required. |
  1. Click Save to save the record.

To delete a group benefit plan type:

Click Delete to delete the selected Type Code.

Note: Note: If an existing Type Code is tied to any of the following, then you cannot delete it. The system displays an error message: There are records associated with (Plan Type). Code cannot be deleted:

  • The Type Code field under the Plan Types section on the Group Benefit Plans form.
  • An Effective Date field set up for the Plan Type on the Billing Rates or Premium Rates forms.
  • The Plan Type field under the Contribution Rules section on the Benefit Rules form.
  • The Plan type field under the Coverage Details section on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

  • Yes - To suppress the re-direct of 12-21 for the selected client.

FSA/HSA Mid-Year Limit Calculations - Enforce Limits During Payroll Processing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/HSA_FSA_Mid-Year-Limit_Calc.htm Path: BA/Topics/HSA_FSA_Mid-Year-Limit_Calc.htm

FSA/HSA Mid-Year Limit Calculations - Enforce Limits During Payroll Processing

When an organization administers an FSA or HSA plan on a calendar year (for example, the plan year begins on January 1st and ends on December 31st), the FSA or HSA plan year limits are in correlation with the IRS annual limits. There are no issues with payroll deduction calculations or risks of deducting plan contributions in excess of the plan or IRS limits.

When an organization administers an FSA or HSA plan on a mid-year basis (for example, the plan year begins July 1st and ends on June 30th of the next year), the potential exists for plan contribution deductions to exceed IRS calendar year limits. This is due to multiple plan years falling within the same tax year.

When a mid-year plan is in effect, the system applies a carryover toward the IRS calendar year limit.

Example:

During the last six months of the previous mid-year plan that occurred during the first part of the current calendar year (for example, from January 1st through June 30th), an employee with a monthly payroll schedule had elected HSA contributions in the amount of $555.56 per month ($3,333.33 for the six-month time-frame). If the calendar year IRS limit was $6000.00, the maximum remaining deductions allowed for the new mid-year plan (that starts on July 1st) would be $2666.67 or $444.44 per month for the remainder of the calendar year. Without accounting for this difference between plan years and IRS calendar year limits, an employee could elect to deduct too much per monthly pay period (for example, $500 per month for the next year of the mid-year plan). This would lead to the employee exceeding the IRS yearly limit by $333.33 for the last six months of the current calendar year.

The following graphic illustrates the plan year for an HSA plan that is set as a mid-year plan starting on July 1st and ending on June 30th.

[Image: screenshot]

The FSA/HSA Mid-Year Limit Calculations feature includes functionality to calculate plan deductions and coordinate plan year and IRS calendar year limits. The feature also takes into account both employee and employer contributions. By calculating deduction limits, the system can enforce the plan year and IRS limits during the payroll process so that plan contributions do not exceed the IRS tax year limits.

Once payroll processing completes and the system calculates a carryover amount. The system displays the carryover amount on the Elections section on the Flexible Spending Accounts form.

The following graphic illustrates the Elections section on the Flexible Spending Accounts form for an employee with a mid-year plan.

[Image: screenshot]

You can also view the carryover amount on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry form.

The following graphic illustrates the Deduction Carryover column on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry form for an employee with a mid-year plan.

[Image: screenshot]

Once payroll processing is complete, you can review the carryover deduction calculations by completing the following:

  1. Selecting a payroll voucher for an employee,
  2. Select the Deductions tab
  3. In the Loan/Docket# HSA Type column, click the hyperlink to view the details.

The system displays the Deduction Carryover Calculation window that displays a summary of the calculations.

The following graphic illustrates the Deduction Carryover Calculation window.

[Image: screenshot]

Setting Up HSA Plan Years

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/HSA_Plan_Years.htm Path: BA/Topics/HSA_Plan_Years.htm

Setting Up HSA Plan Years

To establish health savings account (HSA) plan years in PrismHR, use the HSA Plan Years form.

To set up HSA plan years:

  1. Open the HSA Plan Years form.
Use this option To define this
Plan ID The Health Savings Account plan ID.
Plan Year Number The plan year number, for example, 2016.
Plan Year Name A description of the HSA plan year to differentiate it from other plan years.
Starting Date The date when this plan year goes into effect.
Ending Date The date on which this plan year is no longer available.
  1. Click Save.

Note: Note: A plan year with a starting date of January 1st and an ending date of December 31st of the same year is considered a calendar year plan. If the Starting Date and Ending date fields contain dates that are outside of a normal calendar year, then the system considers the plan to be a mid-year plan. For example, if you enter 07/01/2021 in the Starting Date field and 06/30/2022 in the Ending Date field, the system considers the plan as a mid-year plan that spans the last half of the 2021 calendar year and the first half of the 2022 calendar year. When you set up a mid-year plan, the system must calculate a carryover deduction amount to assist with employee benefit deductions. See FSA/HSA Mid-Year Limit Calculations - Enforce Limits During Payroll Processing.

  1. Open the HSA Plans panel.
Use this option To define this
Plan ID The plan ID for this benefit plan.
Plan Name A name that describes the benefit plan.
Disallow S-Corp Principal From HSA Enrollment Whether S-Corp Principals cannot enroll in this plan.
Plan Termed On The date on which the plan expires. After that date, users cannot select this HSA plan.
  1. Click Save.

Establishing Flexible Spending Accounts

To establish the flexible spending accounts for each HSA plan:

  1. Open the Flexible Spending Accounts panel.
Use this option To define this
Account Code The flexible spending Account Code. The Account Description displays.
Deduction Code The Deduction Code to use for payroll deductions for the flexible spending account type.
Pay Code The Pay Code used to reimburse claimed expenses from the flexible spending account type.
FSA Report Code The FSA Report Code to use in uploads.
  1. Click Save.

Setting Up Wellness Benefit Plans

Some clients offer wellness benefits for employees. Wellness benefits can improve and motivate healthy behaviors in your employees while reducing their health care costs. Before approving employees for lower wellness benefit plan rates, they must pass a wellness assessment.

In PrismHR, you can:

  1. Define a medical benefit plan as wellness banded.

  2. Enter the billing and premium rates.

  3. Manage employee wellness statuses in bulk, or per employee. For more information, see Changing the Wellness Status for Multiple Employees or Changing an Employee’s Wellness Status.

  4. View employee wellness status history. For more information, see Viewing an Employee’s Wellness Status History.

Defining a Wellness Banded Benefit Plan

First, you must define a benefit plan as wellness banded on the Group Benefit Plans form. You can only define a Medical (MED) benefit plan as wellness banded.

To define a benefit plan as wellness banded:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens.

  3. In Offer Type, select Medical (MED).

  4. In the Other Processing Parameters panel, complete the following:

Use this option… To do this…
Wellness Banded Rates Define the medical benefit plan as wellness banded. The Use Wellness Rates as Default and Assessment due fields display. When enabling the Wellness Banded Rates option, the system disables the following options: - Family Rated Premiums - Tobacco Banded Rates - Gender Banded Rates If these options are enabled on a benefit plan, the system shows a confirmation dialog box indicating that they reset when enabling Wellness Banded Rates.
  • Family Rated Premiums
  • Tobacco Banded Rates
  • Gender Banded Rates | Use Wellness Rates as Default | Set the wellness banded rates as the default for the benefit plan. | | Assessment due | Define the days or months before or after the open enrollment effective date when the wellness assessment is due. |
  1. Click Save.

Entering Billing Rates

After defining a benefit plan as wellness banded, enter the billing rates on the Billing Rates form. For more information, see the following:

  • Setting Health Plan Billing Rates by Rate Group

  • Setting Health Plan Billing Rates by Rate Group and Age

Entering Premium Rates

After defining a benefit plan as wellness banded, enter the premium rates on the Premium Rates form. For information, see the following:

  • Setting Health Plan Premium Rates

  • Setting Premium Rates Based on Rate Group

  • Setting Premium Rates Based on Network

Setting Up Network Banded Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Network_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm Path: BA/Topics/Network_MDV_Plans_Intro.htm

Setting Up Network Banded Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans

This section outlines setting up network banded benefit plans for the medical, dental, and vision insurance classes at the system level in PrismHR. It is intended for users who have experience setting up benefit plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Only those settings for network banded benefit plans are covered in this section. Some settings are used only in Benefits Enrollment, and are labeled accordingly. For more information about using Benefits Enrollment, refer to in-product help or to the Benefits Enrollment User Guide.

========================================================================

Optional Settings

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Optional_Settings_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Optional_Settings_MDV.htm

Optional Settings

The following are common optional settings for medical, dental, and vision plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Settings in Group Benefit Plans Panel

Use settings described below to establish whether the plan is:

  • Section 125 Electable if this benefit can be elected for flexible spending plans. If you select this option, you must also enter the prepay benefit account numbers in the 125 Deduction Code field.

  • COBRA Electable if this benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage.

  • A High Deductible Plan (HDHP) if this health benefit plan has a high deductible which might entitle the employee to participate in a health savings account (HSA).

Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel

Use these settings to establish:

  • Dependent age limits

  • Disability coverage eligibility

  • Mid-month coverage

[Image: screenshot]

Dependent Age Limit and Disabled Dependent Eligibility

Enter the Dependent’s Age Limit; if the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The value selected in the drop-down determines when the dependent age limit actually becomes effective:

  • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll.

  • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll.

Note: Note: This means that the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified.

  • End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.

Note: Note: If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective (for example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017 and the plan effective date is April 25, 2017) the dependent will still be considered eligible for coverage and will be able to enroll even if the dependent’s actual age has reached age limit specified.

  • Select Disabled Dependent Eligible and specify a Disabled Alt Age Limit to establish benefit eligibility for disabled dependents who are above the age specified in the Dependent’s Age Limit field and who would otherwise be ineligible for coverage.

Mid-Month Coverage Setting

  • Select Mid-Month Coverage Dates if the benefit plan allows for mid-month coverage start/stop dates. Otherwise, coverage starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.

PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel

If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . Typically these are health maintenance organization (HMO) medical plans, but some dental plans might also require this information. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

If selected, you must also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in the PCP Lists field in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form; For more information, see Defining Enrollment Plans. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Settings in States Offered In Panel

A medical, dental, or vision benefit plan that is state banded is only offered in certain states. To list the states in which this type of benefit plan is offered, you can use the States Offered In panel.

  1. In the States Offered column, enter the two-character state codes for each state where this benefit plan is offered. The State Name displays.

  2. Enter the Plan Number for each state.

Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes

To enter eligible locations by ZIP code, use the Eligible ZIP Codes form.

Note: Note: This form is accessed by selecting Eligible ZIP Codes in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

in Group benefit Plans, and is used only for benefit plans that are not set up to collect network information.

Only those employee home locations that match the ZIP codes on the plan will be eligible for enrollment. If no ZIP codes are entered for the benefit plan, employees will be able to enroll regardless of home location.

  1. Enter the ZIP Codes you want to attach to the benefit plan. The City and State displays.

  2. Click Save.

Required ZIP Code Validation

All ZIP codes must first be entered at the system-level to be attached to a benefit plan. If you enter a ZIP code that is not in the system, an error message displays.

You can correct this by entering the ZIP code at the system-level in the Zip Codes form. Once the ZIP code record is in the system, you can then attach it to the benefit plan. For more information, see Setting Up Zip Codes.

Setting Up Other Processing Parameters for Age Banded Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Other_Processing_Parameters_Age_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Other_Processing_Parameters_Age_MDV.htm

Setting Up Other Processing Parameters for Age Banded Plans

, Use the Other Processing Parameters panel to set up the benefit for age banded premium and billing rates.

  • To set up the benefit plan for age banded billing, select Age Banded Medical Billing, then enter the age calculation information:

  • Select the Age Calculation Month method used to calculate the age for insurance premium calculations.

  • Enter the Age Calculation Day on which the insurance premium age is based.

The system works as follows:

If And Then
Age Calculation Month is January Age Calculation Day is 1 The rate calculates every January 1st. The system calculates the premium based on the most recent January 1st. The system does not look to the next year.

Setting Disability Insurance Premium Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Premium_Rates_Disability.htm Path: BA/Topics/Premium_Rates_Disability.htm

Setting Disability Insurance Premium Rates

To enter the premium rates for a short- or long-term disability group benefit plan by age, use the Premium Rates form.

The rates you enter in the premium rate table refer to the Cost Basis field in the Group Benefit Plans form. For example, if the cost basis is Monthly, the rates represent monthly premium costs.

To set disability insurance rates:

  1. Open the Premium Rates form.

Use this option — To define this

Benefit Plan ID — The Benefit Plan ID. It is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Effective Date — The date when the rate goes into effect. Saving rates according to the effective date enables you to view previous rates. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date. For short- or long-term disability benefit plans, the effective dates indicate whether the rate is set to standard or extended precision. If you selected the LTD/STD Use Extended Precision Rates option in the main form, you can only choose an effective date with extended precision, otherwise you can only select a date with standard precision.

From Age To Age — The starting age and the upper age limit. If the plan’s rates are the same regardless of the employee’s age, enter an “all encompassing” age range, for example, 0-99.

Rate — The premium rate per ten dollars of coverage (short-term disability) or hundred dollars of coverage (long-term disability).

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

If you selected the LTD/STD Use Extended Precision Rates option in the main form, you can only choose an effective date with extended precision, otherwise you can only select a date with standard precision.

From Annual Salary To Annual Salary — The amount for the line. The first From Annual Salary value must be zero. Each subsequent value is one cent greater than the To Annual Salary in the previous band.

Premium — The premium amount for employees in this salary band.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Premium_Rates_Family_Rated.htm Path: BA/Topics/Premium_Rates_Family_Rated.htm

Setting Family Rated Plan Premium Rates

To set up premium rates based on the age of individuals covered by the plan, use the Premium Rates form.

You must enter a premium for each specific age group. If the plan imposes a surcharge for individuals that are smokers, enter the surcharge in the Tobacco Surcharge column. If the plan does not impose a surcharge, that column blank or enter a zero.

If individual rates are the same at the beginning or end of the age range, you do not need to enter individual age rates. For example, assume that the rates start at age 20 and end at 65. For individuals on the plan who are 19 years of age or younger, the system uses the age 20 rate. For individuals who are older than 65, the system charges the age 65 rate.

To set up family rated plan premium rates:

  1. Open the Premium Rates form.

Use this option — To define this

Benefit Plan ID — The Benefit Plan ID. It is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Effective Date — The date when the rate goes into effect. Saving rates according to the effective date enables you to view previous rates. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date.

  1. If Family Rated Premiums is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel:

Use this option — To define this

From Age — The first age.

Premium — The premium cost for the selected age.

Tobacco Surcharge — The surcharge for tobacco usage, if any.

Note: Note: Define this information (for each age. Click + or press Tab to create the next age row.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  2. Click Close when you are finished.

  1. Open the Premium Rates form.

Use this option — To define this

Benefit Plan ID — The Benefit Plan ID. It is populated from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Network ID — A field that is shown when Premium Rates Vary By Network is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel.

Plan Type — A list of the plan types defined for the group benefits plan.

Employee Gender — This option is shown when Gender Banded Rates is selected in the Other Processing Parameters panel in Group Benefit Plans.

  1. If the benefit plan is also set up as tobacco banded:

Use this option — To define this

From Age To Age — Enter the starting age and the upper age limit. Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99. For a life insurance plan, typically you enter smoking and non-smoking rates. If the plan does not offer separate rates, enter the same rate for non-smoker and smoker. The rates are either per thousand dollars or a flat amount, depending on the Life Calculation Type defined for the Group Benefit Plan

Non-Smoker Premium — The amount billed to the client for the plan type and age group for an employee who does not use tobacco products.

Smoker Premium — The cost for an employee who is a tobacco user.

NonSmoking Spouse Premium — The cost for a spouse who does not use tobacco products.

Smoking Spouse Premium — The cost for a spouse who uses tobacco products.

Dependents Premium — If covered, the cost associated with covering an employee’s dependents for this plan type and age group.

Total Premium — The amount billed to the client for the benefit rate level. If the benefit plan is not set up as tobacco banded, the Total Premium field is the sum of the Employee Premium and Dependents Premium. When you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Premium of 500 and an Employee Premium of 300, the system populates Dependents Premium with 200. If the benefit plan is not set up as tobacco banded, the Total Premium field is the sum of the Employee Premium and Dependents Premium. After you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Premium of 500 and an Employee Premium of 300, the system populates Dependents Premium with 200.

Employee Premium — The cost for the plan type and age group.

Dependents Premium — If covered, the cost associated with covering an employee’s dependents for this plan type and age group.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type.

Generate / Print Election Notices

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Print%20Election%20Notices.htm Path: BA/Topics/Print Election Notices.htm

Generate / Print Election Notices

Use this form to generate/print the government-mandated COBRA benefits notices. The election notice provides information about COBRA claim opportunities to an employee who experienced a qualifying event.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Processing click Generate / Print Election Notices.

To generate and/or print Election Notices:

  1. Complete the following:

Field Name — Description

Due Date Range Start — Enter the start date to be used to select enrollees by the date their election notice is due.

Due Date Range End — Enter the end date to be used to select enrollees by the date their election notice is due. > Note: Note: The system uses this range to select enrollees for notice printing, based on the date their notice is due. Notices are due 14 days after the qualifying event.

Reprint (Y/N)? — This field is optional. By default this box is unchecked. Check this box if you want to reprint notices. > Note: Note: If you reprint a notice that was already printed, the notice will show the original print date, but premiums will be calculated using current rates.

Report Filters section

Client ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to run this report for selected clients enter the Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Client dialog box.

Client Name — The names of the selected Clients auto populates here.

  1. Click Run. A dialog box appears to tell you how many notices will be created and how many enrollee errors were found. You may correct the errors and redo the process.

  2. Click Election Notice Report to generate the COBRA Continuation Notices Report if a report is to be generated.

  3. Click Error Report to display the errors if any.

  4. Click Generate Election Notices to generate notices if any.

This COBRA Continuation Notices Report has the following columns:

  • Client - Client ID

  • Employee ID

  • Eligible Person

  • Date Modified

  • Date Qualified

  • Benefits Expire

  • Plan Description

  • Monthly Premium

Printing COBRA General Notices

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Print%20General%20Notices.htm Path: BA/Topics/Print General Notices.htm

Printing COBRA General Notices

Use the Print General Notices form to print COBRA General Notices, which contain information regarding the continuation coverage rights under COBRA for eligible benefit plans. This process will print initial notices of COBRA eligibility for employees who recently enrolled in COBRA-electable benefit plans.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Processing click Print General Notices.

To print general notices for COBRA participants:

  1. Complete the following section:

Field Name — Description

Client ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to print general notices for all clients. If you want to print general notices for selected clients, then enter the client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

Client Name — The corresponding client names appear here.

  1. Click Run to build the COBRA General Notices for the selected clients. A job progress window shows the processing steps. A prompt displays the number of notices ready. Click Close to close the job progress window. In case of any errors, correct them and redo the process.

  2. Click General Notice Report to display the COBRA Initial Notices Report on screen. If no general notice is built for the selected clients, then this button will remain disabled.

  3. Click General Notices to generate the COBRA general notices. A Job progress window opens showing the processing steps. Click Open to open the general notices generated in a PDF format. You can print them now. If no notice is generated for the selected clients, then this button will remain disabled.

  4. Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

The COBRA Initial Notices Report has the following columns:

  • Client ID

  • Participant ID

  • Participant Name

  • Benefit Plan ID

  • Benefit Plan Description

  • Due Date

Purge COBRA Enrollees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Purge%20COBRA%20Enrollees.htm Path: BA/Topics/Purge COBRA Enrollees.htm

Purge COBRA Enrollees

Use this form to permanently purge the selected COBRA participant record from the system.

WARNING: This process will delete enrollees from the COBRA.ENROLLEES file. This program allows you to select individuals and deletes anyone you select. Make sure the people you select are ineligible for COBRA.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Processing click Generate / Print COBRA Payment Coupons.

To generate or print COBRA Payment Coupons for active participants:

  1. Complete the following:

Field Name — Description

Participant ID — Click the Participant ID link and select the IDs of ineligible COBRA participant from the Select Enrollee selector. The Select Enrollee selector contains the enrollee IDs for any participant who has an existing COBRA enrollee record.

Participant Name — This field auto-populates the participant name depending on the selections made above.

  1. Click Run. The following warning message appears.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Click Yes if you want to purge the selected enrollees. A job progress window appears. Click Close to close the job progress window.

  • Click No if you are not sure and go back to the form.

  1. Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

Resetting COBRA General Notices

Use the Reprint General Notices form to reset COBRA General Notices which contain information regarding the continuation coverage rights under COBRA for eligible benefit plans.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Processing click Reprint General Notices.

To reprint COBRA General Notices:

  1. Complete the following:

Field Name — Description

Start Date — Enter the start date for the date range.

End Date — Enter the end date for the date range.

Client ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to reprint COBRA general notices for employees of all clients. If you want to reprint COBRA general notices for employees of selected clients enter the Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Client dialog box.

Client Name — The names of the selected Clients auto populate here.

Employee ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to reprint COBRA general notices for all employees. If you want to reprint COBRA general notices for just one employee, enter the Employee ID here or click the Employee ID link and select it from the Select Employee dialog box.

Establishing Retirement Match Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Retirement_Match_Rules.htm Path: BA/Topics/Retirement_Match_Rules.htm

Establishing Retirement Match Rules

To establish the matching rules used when the client or the PEO contributes to employees’ retirement plans, use the Retirement Benefits Plan form.

Defining the Match Rules

To define match rules:

  1. Open the Retirement Benefits Plan form.

Use this option — To define this

Group — The benefit Group ID. If you are creating a new group, use something brief but descriptive, for example, STD.

Benefit Plan — The Benefit Plan ID.

Network ID — If required, the Network ID for this plan

Effective Date — The date when the plan becomes effective.

  1. Click Save.

Defining Basic Information About Match Rules

To define the basic parameters of the retirement benefit plan, use the Retirement Match Rules panel.

To define the basic parameters of the retirement benefit plan:

  1. Open the Retirement Match Rules panel.
Use this option To define this
Benefit Group The benefit Group ID.
Retirement Plan Enter or select the Retirement Plan plan from the Select Plan selector.
Effective Date An existing Effective Date to edit existing match rules. Click New Date to enter a date when new match rules go into effect.
Match Logic Type The Match Logic Type to use for calculations. All the types include the Maximum Matching Contribution and Other Match Rules panels - Traditional: Calculates a match based on the employees’ contributions, and limits the match to a flat amount or percentage of the employees’ earnings. - Layered: Matches a different percentage for various levels of the employees’ contributions. - Safe Harbor 1: Uses match rates for contributing employees only. - Safe Harbor 2: Uses match rates for both contributing and non-contributing employees. The Traditional and Layered match logic types have additional panels.
  • Traditional: Calculates a match based on the employees’ contributions, and limits the match to a flat amount or percentage of the employees’ earnings.
  • Layered: Matches a different percentage for various levels of the employees’ contributions.
  • Safe Harbor 1: Uses match rates for contributing employees only.
  • Safe Harbor 2: Uses match rates for both contributing and non-contributing employees. | Comments | Descriptive Comments regarding the retirement plan match rules. |
  1. Click Save.

Defining the Maximum Matching Contribution

To define the maximum annual employee matching contributions for a calendar year, use the Maximum Matching Contribution Per Calendar Year (Per Employee) panel.

To define the maximum annual employee matching contributions for a calendar year:

  1. Open the Maximum Matching Contribution Per Calendar Year (Per Employee) panel.

Use this option — To define this

Regular Employer Match — The Regular Employer Match or blank if there is no maximum.

Safe Harbor 1 Contribution Safe Harbor 2 Contribution — The contribution amount.

Safe Harbor 1 Rate Override Safe Harbor 2 Rate Override — The override amount to use if the client uses a retirement plan that mirrors Safer Harbor 1 or Safe Harbor 2 rules, but uses another rate or percentage.

Safe Harbor 2 Flat Rate Override — The amount to use for the calculated match. This overrides the Safe Harbor Type 2 Match.

Non-Elective Contribution — The non-elective contribution.

  1. Click Save.

Setting Traditional Match Rules

If you selected Traditional as the Match Logic Type, the Traditional Match Rules panel displays.

To set traditional match rules logic:

  1. Open the Traditional Match Rules panel.

Use this option — To define this

The company’s matching contribution — The company’s matching contribution that is equal to the % of the employee’s elective contribution to this retirement plan.

The maximum contribution to be made by the company — The maximum contribution to be made by the company that is equal to the % of the employee’s retirement basis earnings.

The maximum contribution to be made by the company — Enter a flat amount that is the maximum contribution to be made by the company.

The basis for calculating the maximum matching contribution — The basis for calculating the maximum matching contribution: voucher earnings (default setting), year-to-date earnings, sheltered earnings, or voucher percent divided by the year-to-date flat match.

Classify as Safe Harbor Match — Whether this rule is a Safe Harbor Match (Type 1).

  1. Click Save.

Setting Layered Match Rules

If you selected Layered as the Match Logic Type, the Layered Match Rules panel displays.

To set layered match rules:

  1. Open the Layered Match Rules panel.

Use this option — To define this

Percent Matched — The Percent Matched. The Description indicates whether it is a percent of the first percentage level (first row) or the next level (subsequent rows).

Percentage Level — The Percentage Level of the employees’ retirement base earnings.

Safe Harbor — Whether the layer is a Safe Harbor Match (Type 1),. This overrides the value set in Classify as Safe Harbor Match.

  1. Click Save.

Setting Other Match Rules

To specify other match rules that can apply to this retirement plan, use the Other Match Rules panel.

To set other match rules logic:

  1. Open the Other Match Rules panel.

Use this option — To define this

Maximum Matching Contributions per Week — The Maximum Matching Contributions per Week if there is a weekly limit on the calculated match.

Calculate Safe Harbor 2 Non-Elective Contribution in addition — Whether to calculate the Safe Harbor 2 Non-Elective Contribution. If not selected, the employer matching contribution is used.

Non-Elective Rate — The rate that is typically used for profit sharing that accrues per pay period.

Calculate PEO Match — Whether to calculate an additional employer matching contribution, funded by the PEO.

Vesting Code — The Vesting Code used for vesting options. Vesting codes were defined when the retirement plan and its reporting parameters were set up.

Vesting Code-ProfShare — The Vesting Code-ProfShare for profit sharing vesting options.

Suppress Match Print On Check — Whether to prevent the retirement match from printing on pay stubs.

Exclude Catch Up Contribution from Match Calculation — Whether to exclude employees’ catch-up contributions when the system calculates the matching contribution.

  1. Click Save.

Retirement Plan Termination

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Retirement_Plan_Termination.htm Path: BA/Topics/Retirement_Plan_Termination.htm

Retirement Plan Termination

In PrismHR, the process for terminating a retirement plan involves navigating to the Benefit Plan Setup and updating the plan to reflect the desired stop date. You must also make all employee retirement enrollments inactive to ensure that deductions cease. Currently, PrismHR does not offer a bulk method for making employee retirement enrollments inactive, and this task must be performed manually through the Retirement Plan Enrollment section on an individual employee basis.

Step One: Terminate a Retirement Plan

To terminate a retirement plan:

  1. Open the Benefit Plan Setup form (Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Client) > Benefit Plan Setup) and display the plan you want to terminate by specifying a Plan Class of Retirement and then selecting the Plan. [Image: Benefit Plan Setup form with Retirement Plan Selected]
  2. Enter the desired Stop Date (termination date).
  3. Click Save.

Step Two: Mark Employee Retirement Enrollments Inactive

To mark employee retirement enrollments Inactive:

  1. Open the Retirement Plan Enrollment form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Retirement Enrollments > Retirement Plan Enrollment) and display the employee whose retirement enrollments you want to make Inactive by selecting the Employee and the Retirement Plan.
  2. Then, change the Status to Inactive Enrollment. (Your setup may vary. If you do not see an Inactive Enrollment option, select an equivalent option for “Inactive”.)
  3. Click Save.
  4. Repeat the above steps for each employee where you want to mark retirement enrollments Inactive.

Establishing Retirement Plan Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Retirement_Plan_Years.htm Path: BA/Topics/Retirement_Plan_Years.htm

Establishing Retirement Plan Parameters

To maintain the retirement plan years and reporting periods for group benefit plans, use the Retirement Plan Years form.

To define information for a plan year:

  1. Open the Retirement Plan Years form.

  2. Set these fields as needed:

Use this option — To define this

Plan ID — The Plan ID that represents this retirement plan.

Plan Year Number — The four-digit Plan Year Number, for example, 2016.

Plan Year Name — The name that describes the plan year and differentiates it from others.

Starting Date — The date when this plan year goes into effect.

Ending Date — The date after which this plan year is no longer available.

ERISA Plan# — The Employee Retirement Income Security Act plan number. These usually start at 501 and go up, depending on the number of plans that have been filed with the IRS.

PEO Match — Whether the PEO Match is available during this plan year to employees of one or more clients that elect the PEO Match option. If you select this option, users can select it at the detail level.

Match Percent — The percent of employees’ contributions the PEO will match.

Match Max Percent — Enter the maximum match percentage of the employee’s gross earnings (retirement basis earnings).

  1. Click Save.

To maintain the periods used in plan year reports to your third-party administrator:

  1. Open the Plan Year Reporting Periods panel.

  2. Set these fields as needed:

Use this option — To define this

Period — An integer for the plan year Period to report. Typically, the reporting period number is the number of a month or quarter within the plan year.

Period Description — A description of the period. For example, Quarter 1 or March.

Thru Date — The date when the reporting period ends. The start date of the first period is the same as the plan year Starting Date. The date must be in the same year as the Plan Year Number.

  1. Click Save.

Changing an Employee’s Retirement Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Retirement_Register_Adjustment.htm Path: BA/Topics/Retirement_Register_Adjustment.htm

Changing an Employee’s Retirement Plan

Use the Retirement Register Adjustment form to change an employee’s existing retirement plan information.

Note: Note: To quickly access the Retirement Adjustments Import form, select Import Retirement Adjustments. You can use the Retirement Adjustments Import process to import 401(k) adjustment information and to generate an error report and a transaction report.

To change retirement plan information:

  1. From the Benefit Enrollment Maintenance work center, select Retirement Enrollments|Retirement Register Adjustment.

  2. Fill in these fields:

Use this option To define this
Transaction The Transaction ID of an existing transaction. Click New Transaction to create a new adjustment. Click Transaction to search and select an existing transaction.
Employee The employee whose retirement plan information is being changed. Either type the name or ID to display a list of matching employee records, or click Employee to open the search window.
Employer ID A valid employer ID for this employee. The default comes from the Employee Details.
Plan The retirement plan for this transaction. The employee must be enrolled in the plan.
Adjustment Date The adjustment date.
Annotation A note for this transaction for future reference.
Contributions
Retirement Earnings The amount of retirement earnings to update.
Employee Contribution The pre-tax elective retirement employee contribution.
Catch-up Contribution The pre-tax catch-up contribution adjustment amount.
Post Tax Contribution The post-tax contribution amount made by the employee.
ROTH Contribution The Roth contribution amount made by the employee.
ROTH Catch-up Contribution The Roth catch-up contribution adjustment amount.
Employer Contribution A employer contribution amount.
Non-Elective Contribution A non-elective contribution amount made on behalf of this employee.
Safe Harbor Type 1 Contribution A Safe Harbor Type 1 contribution adjustment amount.
Safe Harbor Type 2 Contribution A Safe Harbor Type 2 contribution adjustment amount.
Successor Deferrals
Successor Retirement Deferral The amount of successor retirement deferral (pre-tax contributions) made by the employee with a previous employer. The system takes this amount into consideration when calculating a deferral limit, but it is not reported to the third-party administrator of the current plan.
Successor Catch-up Deferral The deferral amount (pre-tax catch-up contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.
Successor ROTH Deferral The Roth deferral amount (post-tax contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.
Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral The Roth catch-up contribution amount (post-tax catch-up contribution) made by this employee with a previous employer.
> Note: Note: The Successor Catch-up Deferral, Successor ROTH Deferral and Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral fields enable you to correct any previous retirement register adjustment entry amounts that caused the employee to exceed the retirement deferral tax year limit. You can enter a negative amount for the overage in the Successor Retirement Deferral field and a positive amount in the Successor Catch-up Deferral field. Entering these values in the appropriate fields ensures that the desired tax year limits will be referenced and applied. Creating a new transaction with amounts on this form and then saving changes causes an adjustment payroll voucher to be created. New successor deferral amounts are created in the Employee Tax Deferral Register and then added to the payroll voucher at the bottom of the Benefits tab in the Retirement amount display column. These amounts must match the amounts entered on the Retirement Register Adjustment form: - Successor Catch-up Deferral - Successor ROTH Deferral - Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral
  • Successor Catch-up Deferral
  • Successor ROTH Deferral
  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral | Loan | The loan ID against which to make a loan payment. | | Loan Payment | The loan payment amount. |
  1. Click Save.

Setting Up Deductions and Bill Codes Overrides

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/RP-Deduction_or_Bill_Code_Setup.htm Path: BA/Topics/RP-Deduction_or_Bill_Code_Setup.htm

Setting Up Deductions and Bill Codes Overrides

Use the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides panel on the Retirement Plans form to establish the deductions or bill codes. These are required for any pre-tax deductions and Roth contributions for a retirement plan. The Global Deduction Code Settings display for your reference. The system uses these global deduction code if no overrides are in place.

To set up deductions and bill codes:

  1. Open the Retirement Plans form: Work Centers|Onboarding & Benefits > Benefit Plan Maintenance > Retirement Plans.

  2. Locate the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides panel.

  3. Set the following parameters for the Deduction Code in the Deduction Code table.

Use this option To define this
Employee Deferral Deduction Code The code used for pre-tax deductions for this retirement plan.
Employee Catch-Up Deduction Code The code used for pre-tax catch-up deductions for this retirement plan.
Employee Loan Deduction Code The code used for pre-tax loan deductions for this retirement plan.
Employee Post-Tax Deduction Code The code used for post-tax deductions for this retirement plan.
Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code The code used for Roth contributions for this retirement plan.
Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code The code used for Roth catch-up contributions for this retirement plan.

Note: Note: When you select the Prohibit Deductions option for any of the parameters mentioned above, then it will allow you to prevent employee Retirement Plan Enrollments from being created.

  1. Set the following parameters for the Bill Code under the Bill Code table.
Use this option To define this
Employer Match Billing Code The code used for the employer match of pre-tax deductions for this retirement plan.

Note: Note: When you select the Prohibit Deductions option for the Billing parameter, then it will allow you to prevent employee Retirement Plan Enrollments from being created.

  1. Click Save.

Note: Note the following:

  • On the System Parameters form, under the Global Codes Setup section, if the Employer Match Billing Code field has an empty value then on the Retirement Plans form, under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section, you can enter an empty value in the Employer Match Billing Code field while updating a plan.

  • When you update an existing Deduction Code Override and click Save, a warning message displays prompting you to acknowledge this update (click Yes to save the update). After clicking Yes, an on-screen report displays the affected employees, with each employee record, deduction type, and code change (original > updated), which requires you to once again confirm this update in the Retirement Plan and its downstream impacts to Recurring Deduction records:

  • Clicking Yes: Updates all associated records and provides a list of affected employee enrollments. Once updated, the corresponding Deduction Code displays on the Recurring Deductions form for each associated employee, which the system pulls into the payroll.

  • Clicking No: Does not update the Retirement Plan setup or the employee Recurring Deduction records.

Note: Note the validations for the Prohibit Deductions option:

  • When you select the Prohibit Deductions or Prohibit Billing option for any of the Deduction or Billing Codes, then that code row clears any existing Deduction Code/Billing Code value and the row is disabled.

  • When you select the Prohibit Deductions for Employee Loan Deduction Code, then on the Employee Retirement Loans form, when you set up a retirement loan, (Prohibited) text is displayed next to the plan name in the Retirement Plan drop-down options. Additionally, if a loan exists for a retirement plan with Prohibit Deductions option flagged for the Employee Loan Deduction Code row, then while running a payroll, the system does not take the loan deductions.

  • When you save the form with a Retirement Plan record and if Prohibit Deductions/Billing is not enabled, then:

  • The record cannot be saved when corresponding Plan-level code is empty and Global Setting is empty.

  • The record can be saved when either corresponding Plan-level code is not empty or Global Setting is not empty or both values are not empty.

  • When you save the form with a Retirement Plan record and if Prohibit Deductions/Billing is checked, then:

  • The record can be saved regardless of whether corresponding Plan-level code is empty and/or Global Setting is empty.

Setting Up Basic Information for a Retirement Plan

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/RP-Maintenance.htm Path: BA/Topics/RP-Maintenance.htm

Setting Up Basic Information for a Retirement Plan

To set up the basic information for a retirement plan, use the Retirement Plan panel on the Retirement Plans form.

To set up basic information for a retirement plan:

  1. Open the Retirement Plans form: Work Centers|Onboarding & Benefits > Benefit Plan Maintenance > Retirement Plans.

  2. Locate the Retirement Plan panel.

  3. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Plan ID A brief but descriptive ID for the plan. For example, 401k.
Plan Name A descriptive name for the plan. For example, 401(k) Master Policy.
Payee ID The ID of the benefit provider
Auto Enroll Whether to automatically enroll any eligible employees in this retirement plan.
Tax Class The tax class. This class affects the ability to define tax deductions.
Third-Party Administrator’s Plan Number The number assigned by the third-party administrator if this plan requires special reporting or media file creation.
Client Sponsored Plan Whether this is a client-sponsored retirement plan.
Employer Contribution Pay Stub Description Whether the employer’s matching contribution prints on the employee’s pay stub.
Non-Elective Contribution Pay Stub Description Whether the employer’s non-elective matching contribution prints on the employee’s pay stub.
Enforce Section 415 Funding Limit Whether to apply Section 415 funding limits to this retirement plan.
Limit Safe Harbor Contribution Based On Match Date Whether to suppress the safe harbor contribution prior to the match start date for this retirement plan.
Exempt take on employees from Minimum Days of Service Requirement Allows the system to waive the waiting period the 401(k) employee contributions for take-on employees. > Note: Note: Please note the following: - This is an optional field and the default is set to unchecked. - This option is only functional when the last hire date and the PEO start date are not same.
  • This is an optional field and the default is set to unchecked.
  • This option is only functional when the last hire date and the PEO start date are not same. | Plan Anniversary Month and Day | Allows you to add new anniversary Month and date to calculate the Next Auto Escalation Date. | | Deemed ROTH | See Using the Deemed ROTH Field. |
  1. Click Save.

Using the Deemed ROTH Field

The Secure 2.0 Act includes a mandatory Roth catch-up requirement for Highly Paid Employees (HPE) participating in a 401(k), 403(b), or 457 retirement plan. For the 2026 tax year, employees with $150,000 in prior year, Social Security wages must contribute catch-up on a Roth basis, to the extent they have not previously made Roth contributions during the year.

This field allows you to elect plans provision to force Pre-tax contributions to ROTH contributions, Pre-tax Catchup contributions to ROTH Catchup contributions, or both, regardless of whether the 402(g) limit has been met for Highly Paid Employees.

Determining a Highly Paid Employee

An employee is considered to be an HPE only if the corresponding Retirement Year is defined and the HPE Prior Year field is set to Yes in the Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant table under the Other tab on the Employee Details form.

This drop-down field has the following options:

  • -Select- – Same as the No (Default) option.

  • No (Default) – Pre-tax Catchup contributions is taken as pre-tax until total pre-tax contributions equals the 402(g) limit. Once the 402(g) limit is reached, no further Pre-tax or Pre-tax Catchup will be taken for contributions.

For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. Any elected ROTH and ROTH Catchup contributions will continue up to the limits. Any remaining pre-tax Catchup contributions will not be forced to ROTH Catchup contribution.

  • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit – Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. Any further catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH catchup contribution.

For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup contribution for the following year (Example: 2026).

Please note the following:

  • If an HPE has a retirement Catchup deductions taken as Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default.

  • When the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a ROTH catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

  • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit – Pre-tax Catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH Catchup regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit.

For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. However, all the pre-tax Catchup contributions are taken as ROTH Catchup contribution regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equals the 402(g) limit.

Please note the following:

  • If an HPE has a retirement Catchup deductions taken as Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default.

  • When the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a ROTH catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

  • Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit – Pre-tax and Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. At this point, all pre-tax elections will be taken as ROTH and all Pre-tax Catchup will be taken as ROTH Catchup contributions.

For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining pre-tax contributions taken as ROTH and pre-tax Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup for the following year (Example: 2026).

Please note the following:

  • If an HPE has a retirement pre-tax or Catchup deductions taken as Roth or Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth and Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth or Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default.

  • When the deduction is taken using the Roth or Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a Roth or Roth catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

Please note that currently, the 402(g) limit is equal to the Contribution Limit defined on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form. The Catch Up Limit is also defined on this form. Additionally, the 402(g) limit and the Catch Up limit can be overridden by defining limits under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form.

Note: Note: When you check Prohibit Deductions for either of the following on the Retirement Plans form:

  • Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code

  • Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code

then, the following options are not displayed in the Deemed ROTH drop-down options:

  • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit

  • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit

  • Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit

Setting Up Plan Year Deferral Limits

To specify plan year limits that control the amount of money contributed to a retirement plan for each year, use the Plan Year Deferral Limits panel on the Retirement Plans form.

To configure plan year deferral limits on a retirement plan:

  1. Open the Retirement Plans form: Work Centers|Onboarding & Benefits > Benefit Plan Maintenance > Retirement Plans.

  2. Locate the Plan Year Deferral Limits panel.

  3. Set the following parameters.

Use this option To define this
Tax Year The tax year for this deferral limit.
Deferral Limit The deferral limit for the tax year.
Catch Up Limit The catch up limit for the tax year. When the Disable Accelerated Catchup? field on the Client Details form is enabled, and when Catch Up Limit is applied to this Retirement Plans form, under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section, the regular contribution overrides Vertex but not for Catch Up (can contribute higher for catchup but sheltered limited at 7500).
60-63 Catch Up This field is optional. As a result of the Secure 2.0 Act of 2022, effective 1/1/2025, for employees who will turn 60, 61, 62 or 63 as of 12/31 of the defined tax year, are permitted to contribute an additional amount to their catch-up contribution. The increased contribution amount should be entered in the 60-63 Catch Up field on the following forms for the employee contribution to be treated as a pre-tax amount: - Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Retirement Plans (under section Plan Year Deferral Limits) - Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Tax Year Limits Maintenance - The value entered in this field will be the total amount such employees can contribute for the tax year. - For tax year 2025, it is the greater of 150% of Catch-Up Contribution limit OR $10,000. - This field will only accept numerical values. - The 60-63 Catch Up amount must be equal to or greater than the value entered in the corresponding Catch Up Limit field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or greater than Catch Up Limit. - The Catch Up Limit amount must be equal to or less than the value entered in the corresponding 60-63 Catch Up field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or less than 60-63 Catch Up. - If the Catch Up Limit field is empty, any value in the 60-63 Catch-Up field will present an error stating 60-63 Catch-Up limits must be defined.
  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Retirement Plans (under section Plan Year Deferral Limits)
  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Tax Year Limits Maintenance
  • The value entered in this field will be the total amount such employees can contribute for the tax year.
  • For tax year 2025, it is the greater of 150% of Catch-Up Contribution limit OR $10,000.

Adding or Editing Employee Retirement Loans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/RPE%20-%20Employee%20Retirement%20Loans.htm Path: BA/Topics/RPE - Employee Retirement Loans.htm

Adding or Editing Employee Retirement Loans

You can use this form to directly access existing employee retirement loan information for the selected Employee. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Employee Retirement Loans that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. This section lists the employee retirement loans for the selected employee in an ascending order by Loan No. by default. This grid has the following columns:

  • Loan No.

  • Loan Amount

  • Loan Date

  • Deduction Start Date

  • Payment Amount

  • Pay Back Amount

  • Override Payment Amount

  • Override From Pay Date

  • Override To Pay Date

  • Paid Back To Date

  • Balance Due

You can click on any of the column headers in the grid to sort the retirement loans as you choose.

  • Click a Loan No. from the list to open the loan details on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form with all corresponding data pre-populated that is tied to the Loan No. selected.

  • The Loan Number, Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • You can edit the other fields for this retirement loan.

  • Click Set up new loan to set up a new retirement loan for the selected employee on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form.

  • The Loan Number is pre-populated with a system generated number. You cannot edit this.

  • The Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form You cannot edit this.

  • Enter the other required fields for this new retirement loan for this employee.

  • Click Save to save the new retirement loan for the employee. After saving the new retirement loan, it will appear in the list under the Employee Retirement Loans section on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

You can access existing employee retirement register adjustment information for the selected Employee, client, and Retirement Plan. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Retirement Register Adjustments that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. By default, this section lists the existing employee retirement register adjustments in an ascending order by Transaction No.. This grid has the following columns:

  • Transaction No.

  • Transaction Date

  • Voucher Number

  • Annotation

You can click on any of the column headers in the grid to sort the retirement register adjustments as you choose.

Setting Up Section 125 Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Section_125_Benefit_Plans.htm Path: BA/Topics/Section_125_Benefit_Plans.htm

Setting Up Section 125 Benefit Plans

To maintain benefit plans that fall under Section 125, use the Section 125 Benefit Plans form.

Before you begin:

  • You must set up Section 125 plans before you can define plan years.

  • You must set up deduction codes and pay codes before you can set up any flexible spending plan, including HSA plans.

Setting Parameters for a Section 125 Benefit Plan

A Section 125 benefit plan enables employees to obtain tax savings when they elect a health plan. You need to establish the PrismHR parameters for a Section 125 benefit plan.

To set parameters for a Section 125 benefit plan:

  1. Open the Section 125 Benefit Plans form.
Use this option To define this
Plan ID The Plan ID for this benefit plan.
Plan Name A name that describes the benefit plan.
Plan Name (Spanish) A name that describes the benefit plan in Spanish.
Disallow S-Corp Principal From HSA Enrollment Whether S-Corp Principals cannot enroll in this plan.
Plan Termed On The date after which this plan is no longer in effect.
  1. Click Save.

Maintaining Flexible Spending Accounts

To maintain flexible spending information for the Section 125 plan for each account type, use the Flexible Spending Accounts panel.

To maintain flexible spending accounts:

  1. Open the Flexible Spending Accounts panel.

Use this option — To define this

Account Code — The flexible spending Account Code that is available for this plan. The Account Description displays.

Deduction Code — The Deduction Code used to make payroll deductions for this account type.

Pay Code — The Pay Code used when reimbursing claimed expenses from this account type

FSA Report Code — The FSA Report Code.

  1. Click Save.

Setting Up Section 125 Plan Years

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Section_125_Plan_Years.htm Path: BA/Topics/Section_125_Plan_Years.htm

Setting Up Section 125 Plan Years

To establish Section 125 benefit plan parameters, use the Section 125 Plan Years form.

Defining Section 125 Plan Year Information

To define the Section 125 plan year information:

  1. Open the Section 125 Plan Years form.
Use this option To define this
Plan ID The plan ID for this benefit plan.
Plan Year Number The four-digit plan year number, for example, 2015.
Plan Year Name The plan year name to describe the plan year and differentiate it from others.
Starting Date The starting date when this plan year goes into effect.
Ending Date The ending date after which this plan year is no longer available.
ERISA Plan# The Employee Retirement Income Security Act plan number.
  1. Click Save.

Defining Plan Year Reporting Periods

The Plan Year Reporting Periods panel establishes the month or quarter within the plan year that is reported to the third-party administrator.

To define the Section 125 plan year reporting periods:

  1. Open the Plan Year Reporting Periods panel.

Field — Heading

Period — An integer for the plan year period to report. Typically, the reporting period number is the number of a month or quarter within the plan year.

Period Description — A description of the period. For example, Quarter 1 or March.

Thru Date — When the reporting period ends. The start date of the first period is the same as the plan year Starting Date. The date must be in the same year as the Plan Year Number.

  1. Click Save.
