Setting Up Benefit Network Locations

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Benefit_Network_Locations_and_Eligible_ZIP_Codes.htm Path: BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Benefit_Network_Locations_and_Eligible_ZIP_Codes.htm

Setting Up Benefit Network Locations

When you select the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel, the Benefit Network Locations form becomes available and can be accessed by selecting Network ZIP Codes inActions menu

[Image: screenshot]

.

This is where you can manually enter network ZIP codes for the benefit plan. You can also use the Network ZIP Codes Import to import multiple ZIP codes to benefit plans that have a network assigned.

Required ZIP Code Validation

All ZIP codes must first be entered at the system-level to be attached to a benefit plan. ZIP code records that are in the system will always display City & State information in the table. If city and state information does not display, it means the ZIP code record does not exist at the system-level.

Users should also note that the Network ZIP Codes Import adds ZIP codes to the benefit plan record, but it does not update the ZIP code records at the system-level.

The import form will allow you to save the imported record without error, but when you view the benefit plan’s networks in the Benefit Network Locations form by selecting the Network ID, the system will display the error message “Warning - Key [ZIP code] is not valid for ZIP codes” for each ZIP code that cannot be validated.

It is recommended that you review and update all ZIP code records in the Zip Codes form, either manually or by using the import. Once a ZIP code record is in the system, you can attach it to a benefit plan. For more information, see Setting Up Zip Codes.

Setting Up Billing Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Billing_Rates_Comp_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Billing_Rates_Comp_MDV.htm

Setting Up Billing Rates

To set up billing rates for a tobacco banded group benefit plan, use the Billing Rates form, accessed in the Actions menu in Group Benefit Plan.

You can use the Copy from Premium Rates option, accessed in the Actions menu to copy age-range information from the Premium Rates record for the benefit plan. This option only displays when an Effective Date is entered in Billing Rates.

KJW: As of 1.2.2, this form does not support Copy from Premium Rates

  1. The Benefit Plan ID populates from the Group Benefit Plan form.

Note: Note: The Rate Group field displays when the Billing Rates Vary By Network drop-down in the Other Processing Parameters panel is set to No (the default setting).

  1. Enter the Rate Group. Your organization might charge different clients at different rates for the same benefit plan. PrismHR allows you to define these different rates using rate groups. You can use as many rate groups as needed. The rates you enter apply only to this rate group.

  2. Select the Plan Type. The drop-down lists only the plan types defined for the group benefit plan.

  3. Enter a new Effective Date, or select an existing one on the right (if any). Organizing saving rates by Effective Date allows you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates billing using the rates with the most recent effective date.

Note: Note: Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99.

  1. For each age range:
a. Enter the From Age for each line, which is the starting age.
b. Enter the To Age, which is the upper age limit.
— —

Note: Note: The Total Bill Amount field is the sum of the Employee Bill Amount and Dependents Bill Amount. Once you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Bill Amount of 500 and an Employee Bill Amount of 300, the system populates Dependents Bill Amount with 200.

c. Enter the Total Bill Amount to bill to the client for the cost of this plan.
d. Enter the Employee Bill Amount for this plan.
— —
e. Enter the Dependents Bill Amount for this plan.
— —

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter billing rates for another plan type.

  2. Repeat these steps for each plan type set up in the Plan Types panel in Group Benefits Plans.

Use this option… To do this…

Premium Enter the cost for the From Age.

Setting Up Deduction Start Dates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Deduction_Start_Dates.htm Path: BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Deduction_Start_Dates.htm

Setting Up Deduction Start Dates

When an employee enrolls in a benefit plan, the deduction typically starts on the first day of the following month. The system sets the start date in this way so the deduction amount associated with the benefit plan is always for a full month.

For example, if an employee enrolls in the month of January, deductions begin on February 1st, and the company creates a benefit billing adjustment for January. The system adjusts the amount for the actual number of days that the employee was covered.

Note: Note: Some plans allow mid-month enrollment, which means coverage may start on any day of the month.

Deduction start dates begin on the first day of the following month with benefit adjustments when either of the following are true:

  • The coverage start date for the benefit plan is before the current date.

For example, if an employee enrolls on 01/11/2017 in a benefit plan that has a coverage start date of 01/01/2017, the system sets the deduction start date for the benefit plan to 02/01/2017.

  • A payroll batch has been created with a pay date that is after the coverage start date.

For example, if an employee enrolls in a benefit plan that has a coverage start date of 01/01/2017, and a payroll batch is already created for the month of January, the system sets the deduction start date for the benefit plan to 02/01/2017.

In both of these scenarios, benefit adjustments are created to cover the deductions for the month of January. Benefit adjustments are based on the pay period for benefit billing frequency and payroll deduction frequency, even if the plan has designated a monthly benefit billing frequency.

Changing Deduction Start Dates and Benefit Adjustments

The recommended best practice is to enroll the employee in benefits prior to their effective date, and use the system defaults for deduction start date and benefit adjustments.

You can, however, modify the deduction start date and/or benefit adjustments as follows:

To modify … Procedure
The Employee Contribution amount or the deduction Start Date in the Benefit Adjustment form. For more information, see the Human Resources User Guide.
The deduction start date when you have already processed the first batch of the month. - Go to Payroll Control and delete that batch. - Delete the employee’s benefit enrollment and re-enter it with the adjusted start date. - Re-create your batch. (This will have to be done for every plan for every employee.)
  • Go to Payroll Control and delete that batch.
  • Delete the employee’s benefit enrollment and re-enter it with the adjusted start date.
  • Re-create your batch. (This will have to be done for every plan for every employee.) | The deduction start date when you have not processed the first batch of the month. | - Go to Employee Benefit Enrollment and delete the employee’s enrollment record. - Re-enter the employee’s enrollment with the status set to E for eligible instead of A for active. Set the coverage and deduction start dates to the dates you want to use. - Click Save to save the record. - Change the employee’s status from A to E and enroll as usual. (This will have to be done for every plan for every employee.) |
  • Go to Employee Benefit Enrollment and delete the employee’s enrollment record.
  • Re-enter the employee’s enrollment with the status set to E for eligible instead of A for active. Set the coverage and deduction start dates to the dates you want to use.
  • Click Save to save the record.

  • Change the employee’s status from A to E and enroll as usual. (This will have to be done for every plan for every employee.)

Setting Up Plan Networks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Plan_Networks_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Plan_Networks_MDV.htm

Setting Up Plan Networks

To establish the networks in which this group benefit plan is offered, use the Plan Networks panel. Typically the benefit provider supplies this information.

  1. Enter the Network ID for the network service area, for example, NE or DFW.

  2. Enter a description of the Service Area for this network, for example, Northeast or Dallas/Fort Worth.

  3. If ZIP Codes Exist in the system for the network ID, Yes displays.

Note: Note: If the field is blank, ZIP codes have not been set up for the network. You must set up ZIP codes in the Benefit Network Locations form. See Setting Benefit Network Locations for more information. You can also set up ZIP codes using the Network ZIP Codes Import.

  1. To deactivate the network at the system level, select Yes from the Inactive drop-down.

Setting Up Plan Types

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Plan_Types_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Setting_Up_Plan_Types_MDV.htm

Setting Up Plan Types

Medical, dental, and vision plans often have multiple types of plans available, such as single employee or family plans.

To associate benefit plan types with the group benefit plan, use the Plan Types panel. First, you must set up group benefit plan types; For more information, see Defining Types of Group Benefit Plans.

  1. Enter each plan Type Code applicable to this benefit plan. The Plan Type Description displays.

  2. If the type code is for a high-deductible health plan, enter the HDHP Max Contribution amount that can be made to the employee’s HSA at this level of coverage.

  3. Enter the annual HSA Match amount for the coverage tier.

  4. Enter Carrier Code 1 and Carrier Code 2 values to use to track the plan.

  5. If the plan type expires, enter the Type Obsolete After date.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Settings_for_GBP_MDV.htm Path: BA/Topics/Settings_for_GBP_MDV.htm

General Settings in Group Benefit Plans

To establish the basic parameters of the group benefit plan, use the Group Benefit Plans form. The Offer Type is required if your organization uses Benefits Enrollment.

  1. Enter the Benefit Plan ID. If you are creating a new plan, use an ID that briefly describes the plan.

  2. Enter the Plan Description.

  3. Select the Insurance Class (Medical, Dental, or Vision) that indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. This affects which panels display, what fields are available, and the calculation method the system uses in deriving the premium for the benefit plan.

  4. Enter the Payee ID of the benefits provider that receives the deducted amounts. If you need to define a new payee for this benefit provider, open the Actions menu and select Payees.

  5. Select the Cost Basis associated with any premiums and contribution amounts for this benefit plan. Refer to this field when changing premium rates or assigning employee overrides.

Note: Note: Some companies offer their employees a set amount of life insurance coverage, and the option to buy more at the employee’s expense. The manual premium calculation allows you to manually enter the employee’s individual premium and contribution on the employee enrollment record. Manual premiums can also apply to some medical plans that do not have set premiums.

Select the Manual Calculation method (Fully Automatic Calculation, Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually, Coverage Entered Manually), which indicates how users enter the plan’s coverage and premiums.

  1. Enter the payroll Deduction Code for the post-tax deduction.

  2. Enter the Offer Type if you want to include the benefit plan in benefits and open enrollments in Benefits Enrollment. Offer types classify the benefit plan and assure that the plan displays correctly in enrollment workflows. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

For a medical, dental, or vision plan, select Medical (MED), Dental (DEN), Vision (VIS).

Only those settings for tobacco banded benefit plans are covered in this section. Some settings are used only in Benefits Enrollment, and are labeled accordingly. For more information about using Benefits Enrollment, refer to in-product help or to the Benefits Enrollment User Guide.

Using the Hawaii 1.5% Rule

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Using_the_Hawaii_15_Rule.htm Path: BA/Topics/Using_the_Hawaii_15_Rule.htm

Using the Hawaii 1.5% Rule

In Hawaii, an employer can elect to pay the entire premium amount or share the cost with the employee. The employer must pay for at least one-half of the (single) premium cost, however, the employee’s contribution cannot exceed 1.5% of the employee’s monthly wages.

Requirements

Within a payroll batch, the system processes this calculation for employees who meet the following requirements:

  • The employee’s resident state is Hawaii

  • The employee has not waived their right to medical coverage. You can set medical waiver information for employees on the Employee Details form Other tab.

For more information, see the Human Resources User Guide.

For the purpose of this calculation, a “wage” is defined as any pay code with a pay classification of Earnings.

Note: Note: This assumption is based on the definition of wages found in the Hawaii Revised Statutes from the Hawaii Department of Labor, Chapter 388, which specifically states that wages do not include tips or gratuities of any kind.

Calculation

The calculation uses the following information in all reports that cover employee premium contributions:

Field — Description

Employee Contribution — The amount the employee is scheduled to contribute towards the cost of single coverage, based on the defined benefit rule.

Employee Premium Contribution — The pay period amount the employee is scheduled to contribute towards the cost of single coverage.

Employee MTD Contribution — The month-to-date amount contributed by the employee towards the cost of the benefit premium.

  • The system processes the deductions for a regular batch, or special batch that is taking the place of a regular batch.

  • The system takes the deduction only from regular and vacation vouchers.

  • The system then checks to make sure that the currently scheduled employee contribution for an active medical plan does not exceed 1.5% of the employee’s current earnings. In doing this, it also calculates month-to-date earnings and employee contributions, and makes adjustments to the employee’s contribution either upward or downward throughout the month.

For example, if the employee’s wages are low in the first two pay periods of the month, the system reduces the employee’s scheduled contribution so that the contribution does not exceed 1.5% of earnings. If the employee is given a large bonus in the third pay period of the month, the system increases the scheduled contribution on the current voucher up to the amount that equals 1.5% of month-to-date wages to make up for the shortfall in the first two periods. This adjustment is done on a monthly basis. The system does not carry over any shortfall or overage into the next month.

Note: Note: To determine the scheduled month-to-date contributions at each pay period in the month, this calculation logic relies on the deduction periods. Be sure that the deduction periods defined in the payroll are defined correctly and in a linear fashion.

Deduction Periods for Vacation Pay Vouchers

It is critical that if vacation is paid in future pay periods, the deduction periods for those vacation pay vouchers must be defined correctly. You can set deduction periods in the Vacation Pay Override form. For more information, see the Payroll Overrides Guide.

Setting Up Web Enrollment Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Web_Enrollment_Parameters_Age.htm Path: BA/Topics/Web_Enrollment_Parameters_Age.htm

Setting Up Web Enrollment Parameters

To define how PrismHR processes open enrollment information for the benefit plan, use the Web Enrollment Parameters panel.

  1. Select Include in Open Enrollments to use this plan for open enrollments.

  2. Enter the Insurance Carrier URL, which is the link to the page that provides detail about the insurance carrier.

  3. Enter the Plan Description URL, which is the link to the plan description page.

  4. Select Approval Required to automatically set an initial status of Pending in the Status field of the Employee Group Benefits form.

  5. Enter the Display Benefit Type, which is the code used for display grouping.

  6. If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) For more information about other required PCP information settings in Benefits Enrollment, see Optional Settings.

  7. In the table, enter each Process Attribute code that applies to the benefit plan. The code Description displays.

Viewing an Employee’s Wellness Status History

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Topics/Wellness-Status-History.htm Path: BA/Topics/Wellness-Status-History.htm

Viewing an Employee’s Wellness Status History

To view the wellness status history of a single employees, use the Wellness Status History form.

To view an employee’s wellness status history:

  1. Click the HR menu.

  2. From HR|View, select Wellness Status History. The Wellness Status History form displays.

  3. In Employee ID, select an employee ID. The following information displays.

Field Description
Date Effective Wellness status effective date.
Assessment Completion Date The date the employee completed the wellness assessment.
Wellness Status Whether the employee qualifies for the wellness benefit plan.
